PUBLICATION + HONEST SCOPE
--------------------------
Published in spec-sheet form as `gitbook/benchmarks/nvidia-enterprise-serving.md` (+ SUMMARY
entry; cross-linked from nvidia-llm-throughput.md and llm-inference-overview.md). The scope
as published, restated for the ledger record: the serving driver is batch-1 resident
(aggregate does not scale with C; the batched stack is bench-only today); aggregate at C>=8
loses to vLLM (tensor-core prefill + continuous batching) — conceded; TTFT loses to both
opponents' warm servers; rag C=32 driver row pending the known-issue fix above; 7B served
only via vLLM reference rows (our 7B lane not built); H100/FP8 datacenter lane not pursued
(no tensor-core surface in the pinned toolchain). The two VM-side fixes (FIX 1 stdin reader,
FIX 2 def-not-fn) still need their repo PR before any further serve-driver runs.

ADDENDUM 2026-08-22 — RAG C=32 "DEADLOCK" ROOT-CAUSED AS A HARNESS LOCK CONVOY (PR #806),
VERIFIED 3x 64/64; RAG C=32 DRIVER ROWS LAND
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Root cause (not a driver/session bug): enterprise_bench.py's JsonlDriverAdapter held the
response-condition lock across the blocking stdin write. Against the batch-1 driver (reads
stdin only between requests) the chain closes into a four-way circular wait: writer blocked
in stdin.write() holds the lock for the whole ~90s compute window -> _read_loop cannot store
responses and no worker can reach its deadline check -> one response accumulates per window
until the 64KB stdout pipe fills (~21 windows; stall onset measured 31.7/33.1 min on A100/L4,
matching the arithmetic) -> driver parks in pipe_write (the observed sigsuspend / GPU 0%),
never reads stdin again, lock held forever. Evidence: A/B replay on the A100 captured all
four parties at once (driver wchan=pipe_write, stdout backlog 53,216 B, stdin backlog 57,653 B,
32 workers stuck in send() with 22 unable to reach deadline checks); local pipe-faithful
repro deadlocks pre-fix harness at C=32 in <1 min, fixed harness completes 32/32 in serial
time. Session-layer hypotheses (KV exhaustion, MAX_CTX math, dispatch budget) refuted: the
driver is strictly serial; the backlog lived in the OS pipes. The "~17 GB L4 working set"
was the ~5 GB driver plus a co-resident foreign workload.

FIX: writers serialize on a private _write_lock, never on the condition lock (one new lock +
one with-target swap). Stacks on #802's stdin reader fix. No metric semantics change.

VERIFICATION (A100, rebuilt driver incl. #802): split-line protocol test PASS; 3 consecutive
rag C=32 runs 64/64 (wall 6066.7/6066.9/6066.0 s; TTFT p50 5117.6/5118.9/5117.4 ms; TPOT p50
175.49/175.49/175.47 ms; agg 5.40 tok/s) + chat C=32 regression 64/64 (828.1 s; TTFT p50
538.5; TPOT 48.63; agg 19.79). Rag C=32 driver rows published in
gitbook/benchmarks/nvidia-enterprise-serving.md with the root-cause note; the Scope bullet
updated (stall was a harness bug, fixed and re-verified).

ADDENDUM 2026-08-22 — LEVER PUSH: THE AUTOPSY'S MEASURED LEVERS LAND IN THE SERVE DRIVER
(L2 ONE-PASS PREFILL GEMM + L1 FLASH PREFILL ATTENTION + L4 PACKED3 BATCHED DECODE;
L3 f16-ACCUM MEASURED AND REJECTED AT ITS OWN GATE) — chat C=8 agg 160.4 -> 552.0 tok/s
(3.44x), TTFT p50 4256.6 -> 668.3 ms (6.37x), TPOT p50 33.3 -> 11.8 ms (2.82x); rag C=8
BEATS llama-server 3.10x (227.1 vs 73.3 tok/s); chat C=8 at 90.9% of llama-server
(552.0 vs 607.5, up from 28.1% pre-change). Branch feat/lever-push.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The nsys/ncu autopsy of this same race (AUTOPSY.md, /tmp/autopsy_a100/ on algenta-ent-a100,
mirrored to /tmp/autopsy_a100_results/ on the build host) ranked four pushable levers; this
addendum records each lever's implementation, its A/B measurement, its gate result, and the
final race, all on algenta-ent-a100 (A100-SXM4-40GB, us-central1-a), same harness
(enterprise_bench.py, greedy, 64 req/cell), same day.

LEVERS, IN ORDER, EACH GATED (16/16 campaign oracle through the serving path + token
identity, per lever's own gate form):

L2 — admission prefill in ONE M-parallel pass (-D ALGENTA_PF_ONEPASS). The pre-change
admission walked every prompt in CUDA_PREFILL_TILE=128-row sequential passes on
decode-shaped grids (autopsy gap #1: prefill GEMM 297.5 ms at 2.66 TF/s, occupancy pinned
12.5%). The driver now owns _PF_PASS_MAX(1152)-row scratch and runs the v2 GEMM family once
at M=prompt_len (chat prompts prefill as a single grid per projection per layer; rag shapes
run ceil(len/1152) passes, each one M-parallel grid). Session modules byte-unmodified.
  MEASURED (1038-token chat prompt, single request, driver-reported TTFT p50, 9 repeats):
  538.5 ms (pre-change arm) -> 278.1 ms [-260.4 ms, 1.94x].
  nsys windowed: prefill GEMM family ~96 ms at M=1038 = 9.5 TF/s = 49% of the 19.5 TF f32
  SIMT peak (the autopsy projected 30-38%; measured above it).
  GATE: selftest PASS 16/16 + 8/8; token_identity_probe vs pre-change: 5/5 requests,
  127/127 tokens IDENTICAL (v2 one-pass vs chunked is same-order math).

L1 — flash-style M-parallel prefill attention (-D ALGENTA_PF_ATTN_FLASH). Additive kernel
residentk.kernels_prefill_attn_flash: one warp per (row, head) — lane owns 4 d_head
elements (coalesced float4 Q/K/V), warp-shuffle score reduction, the tiled kernel's
per-key online-softmax recurrence verbatim, zero barriers/shared; same QK-norm+RoPE contract
(reads the same q_rot/slot ck/cv the unchanged _pf_ropewrt writes). Autopsy gap #2:
271.4 ms = 252 dispatches x 1.08 ms of the per-key two-barrier full-block reduction.
  MEASURED (on top of L2): TTFT 278.1 -> 164.3 ms [-113.8 ms]; the 28-dispatch prefill
  attention total drops from 179.6 ms (one-pass, 1 row/warp) as ncu then showed L1TEX
  pressure (88.8% of peak, L2 hit 95.7%, DRAM 0.4%) -> a 4-rows-per-warp variant shares
  each K/V load across four staggered-causality rows: TTFT 164.3 -> 152.0 ms. Row math
  bit-identical to the 1-row form (same recurrence), so no gate drift.
  GATE: selftest PASS 16/16 + 8/8; token identity vs pre-change stays 127/127.

L4 — packed3 weights in the batched decode step (-D ALGENTA_P3_SERVE). New additive modules:
kernels_packed3_batched.mojo (M=B batched packed3 GEMM family — one output row per block
streams the packed weights ONCE for all B tokens; named-scalar dequant/accumulators for
B<=8 after ncu showed indexed thread-local arrays tripling per-chunk instructions;
128-thread blocks after ncu showed 66% idle lanes at 256; block-8 online softmax in the
split-K partial), kernels_decode_attn_flash.mojo (warp-per-(seq,head,split) split-K PARTIAL,
zero barriers — the replaced kernel's per-key full-block reduction cost 187.6 µs x 28 layers
= 5.25 ms of every 19.5 ms C=8 step; the f32 control paid the same 180.7 µs — a hidden gap
inside the autopsy's attention-decode category), session_cuda_batched_p3_graph.mojo
(composes the f32 batched session — prefill/KV/norms stay f32 — with packed3 decode weight
twins, block-32 zero-point int8, 3 quants per f32 word, ~0.94 GB beside the 2.62 GB f32
residents; one captured 258-node p3 graph per B; per-dispatch p3 fallback; chunk readback
narrowed from the full 1.2 MB token log to a head-staged B*n_steps copy).
  MEASURED (chat): TPOT 28.9 ms (B=1 pre-change f32) -> 5.6 ms; C=8 decode-only step
  33.3 -> 9.5 ms; in-cell (admission interleaving) 11.8 ms.
  GATE: selftest PASS 16/16 + 8/8 concurrent-vs-sequential-p3 (the packed3 campaign's G1
  form — a second resident f32 reference exceeds the 40 GB card beside the 32-slot KV).
  Quantization vs the pre-change f32 driver, measured honestly: 3/5 requests identical,
  33/127 tokens flipped on the 2 divergent requests (razor-thin greedy argmaxes; the flips
  are inherent to packed3 quantization — the same gate shape the single-stream p3 arm
  shipped under).

L3 — f16-SIMD accumulation in the v2 prefill GEMMs (-D ALGENTA_PF_F16GEMM). Unlocked per
the brief because L1+L2+L4 left C=8 below 570 (561.3 in that build); adopted ONLY if 16/16
oracle + token identity pass. Implemented (kernels_prefill_v2f16.mojo: f32 storage/load

WIN-TARGET VERDICT, HONEST: the brief's win target (chat C=8 agg >= 700 tok/s AND TTFT
p50 <= 250 ms) is NOT met; the minimum acceptable (agg > 570 AND TTFT < 550) is also just
missed (552.0 / 668.3). Per-layer hardware evidence for the remaining gap, measured not
guessed:
1. TTFT floor: admissions are serialized on one stream; 8 prefills x 152.0 ms each sets an
   arithmetic p50 floor of ~4.5 x 152 = 684 ms for the median request — the measured 668.3
   sits AT that floor. Beating it requires a faster single prefill or multi-stream prefill,
   not scheduling.
2. Single prefill = 152.0 ms = GEMM 96 ms (49% of the f32 SIMT peak — ncu; the toolchain
   has no tensor-core/mma surface, autopsy §7, and the f16-accum path fails the token-
   identity gate) + attention ~53 ms (ncu L1TEX/L2-rate bound at the 4-rows/warp sharing
   limit) + ~3 ms norms/rope/lm_head.
3. Decode step at B=8 = 9.5 ms pure: packed3 GEMM group 5.15 ms at ~136 GB/s effective —
   instruction/latency bound inside the B-wide inner loop (ncu: long-scoreboard at k=3072,
   barrier + idle-lane effects at k=1024; the batch-1 probe's 470-497 GB/s is the B=1
   instruction floor), split-K flash attention ~0.9 ms, p3 lm_head ~1.3 ms, the rest
   norms/kvprod/merge. Tensor cores would change every one of these ceilings; the pinned
   toolchain exposes none.
4. llama's remaining chat edge is structural: f16 weights + tensor-core prefill (their
   prefill GEMM runs cuBLAS HMMA at 53.6 TF/s, autopsy §6) + q8_0 KV; at C>=16 their
   fused-batch decode GEMM (mul_mat_f<half2,...>) pulls further ahead.

L5 — MULTI-STREAM ADMISSION PREFILL (-D ALGENTA_PF_STREAMS_2 / _4)
    The round-1 TTFT floor: 8 serialized admission prefills on ONE stream, p50 = 668.3 ms
    against the arithmetic floor 4.5 x 152 ms = 684 ms. L5 runs admission prefills
    CONCURRENTLY on side CUDA streams: PF_STREAMS independent `_AdmissionPrefill` lanes,
    lane i on `ctx.select_stream(i+1)` (the AsyncRT stream pool starts at ONE stream and
    grows via `create_stream()` — multistream_probe.mojo paid for that and for the 2x/4x
    overlap proof), each lane with its OWN `_PF_PASS_MAX`-row scratch set AND its own
    lm_head/argmax tail buffers allocated against the lane's stream view (the round-1
    agent's named "separated scratch" requirement — syncscope_probe.mojo verified the view
    sync scopes are per-stream and completed side-stream writes are visible cross-stream).
    Decode chunks keep running on the primary stream; the scheduler loop is
    collect-wave -> compact -> launch-wave -> step-chunk.

    THE CORRECTNESS FINDING (measured, bisected, instrumented — NOT assumed): captured
    graph replay co-resident with side-stream lane kernels corrupts tokens. Gate 2 caught
    it (4/8 requests divergent, deterministic per configuration, ALWAYS at a chunk's step
    0). The bisect chain, each arm a build+run:
      * seed-state tearing hypothesis: REFUTED — instrumented post-chunk STATE dumps show
        tokens/poss/step exactly as seeded+advanced while divergence persists;
        a seed-copy sync added anyway (both graph arms) changed nothing.
      * compute-sanitizer memcheck on the failing arm: 0 errors (no OOB — a visibility/
        ordering phenomenon, not a bounds bug).
      * graph_race_probe (trivial captured chains, 3000 replays under side-stream kernel +
        copy concurrency, incl. inter-replay device-side feedback): PASS — the runtime's
        graph machinery is sound for chains that don't touch the session state.
      * DBG_NOGRAPH (per-dispatch decode + concurrent lanes): PASS.
      * DBG_NOOVERLAP (graph decode, lanes never co-resident): PASS.
    Conclusion: the driver's captured decode chain replayed while lane kernels are resident
    mis-reads session state; per-dispatch decode under the same concurrency is token-exact.
    SHIPPED FIX — HYBRID DECODE: while any lane is in flight, `step_chunk` steps the
    per-dispatch arm (proven safe); the moment no lane is busy it reverts to the fast
    captured-graph arm. The runtime-level graph-vs-concurrent-kernel hazard stays
    documented, unfixed underneath (it is a toolchain finding, not a scheduler choice).
    GATES: selftest 16/16 oracle + 8/8 token identity PASS on S2 and S4 builds.

    MEASURED (chat, 64 req/cell; ctl = same sources with PF_STREAMS off, reproduces the

CEILING ANALYSIS (measured inputs, no guessing):
1. Decode-only wall floor at C=8: 1024 batch-steps x ~9.2 ms (the R2 graph step, from the
   9.9 ms in-cell TPOT minus admission seams) = 9.4 s -> 872 agg with ZERO admission
   overhead. The 626-vs-872 gap is admission: 64 prefills x 152 ms = 9.7 s of f32 SIMT
   prefill work sharing the SMs with decode (waves run ~85% packed — S2/S4 wave walls
   measured via the TTFT p50 deltas), plus the hybrid's per-dispatch windows while lanes
   are in flight (~1 ms/step penalty) and wave seams.
2. Prefill is the binding constraint and stays f32-SIMT: 49% of the 19.5 TF peak at
   M=1038 (round-1 ncu), the f16-accum arm fails token identity (0/5, round-1 L3), and the
   pinned toolchain exposes no mma/tensor-core surface (autopsy §7). llama's prefill runs
   cuBLAS HMMA at 53.6 TF/s — 2.7x our f32 rate — which is exactly the aggregate headroom
   the C>=16 cells show.
3. Decode is HBM/instruction-bound p3 streaming: the R2 battery lifted the three GEMM roles
   1.18-1.29x (136 -> ~165 GB/s effective); the B=1 GEMV ceiling (470-497 GB/s) is not
   reachable at B=8 — the instruction floor of the B-wide inner loop (round-1 ncu: long-
   scoreboard / barrier stalls), so decode-side headroom left is incremental, not 12%.
4. The graph-replay-vs-side-stream hazard (L5 finding) taxes overlap: decode steps inside
   admission windows run per-dispatch (~+1 ms/step). A runtime fix for captured-graph
   co-residency would recover it — estimated worth ~30-50 agg at C=8 — and is the named
   next lever if the toolchain exposes one.

================================================================================

THE LANE: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct through the resident CUDA sessions with the 7B
enablement switched ON (qk_norm=0, untied lm_head, GQA 28:4 group-7, d_ff=18944,
ALGENTA_STAGE_18944). Two arms: f32 (full Float32 projections resident, 29.9 GB)
and p3 (packed3 projections + JIT-dequant prefill + packed3 graph decode, 16.6 GB).
Opponent: the campaign-pinned llama.cpp build (ALGENTA_RACE_PIN 000547513f) with
Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct F16 and Q8_0 GGUFs, SAME A100, solo-GPU census throughout.

CORRECTNESS ROOT CAUSE — THE MISSING q/k/v ATTENTION BIASES (bisected, proven)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Symptom: greedy stream diverged from the transformers fp32 reference at token 0
on every prompt (engine [9754,13,13,16,...] degenerate vs reference); both arms
agreed with EACH OTHER, isolating the bug to the common forward path.

Bisection (layer-dump hook, comptime-gated `-D ALGENTA_7B_DUMP`: per-stage f64
checksums of embed/xn1/qkv/qrot/attn/post_attn/xn2/act/post_mlp on the final
prompt row, diffed against identical checksums from a hooked transformers fp32
forward — tooling kept in-tree: dump_transformers_cpu.py / diff_dump7b.py):
    embed    EXACT (0.0 rel)          -> ids + embedding table correct
    xn1      1.2e-7 rel (f32 noise)   -> rmsnorm correct
    qkv      DIVERGED: engine sum -114.87 vs transformers +953.75 (layer 0)
Every later stage diverged downstream of it. First divergence: the fused QKV
projection output.

Disambiguation (check_blob_qkv.py, numpy f64 on the blob's own weights):
  * the blob's layer-0 q/k/v weights are BIT-EXACT hf.T (element-wise vs the
    safetensors) — the converter's data is CORRECT;
  * numpy math on those exact weights reproduces the ENGINE value (-114.87),
    not the transformers value -> the engine faithfully computes a MISSING TERM.
The missing term: Qwen2/Qwen2.5 carry q/k/v PROJECTION BIASES, and neither the
converter nor the engine had them. Arithmetic proof, layer 0:
    sum(bias_q) + sum(bias_k) + sum(bias_v) = 370.64 + 697.61 + 0.37 = 1068.62
    953.75 - (-114.87) = 1068.62                                    (exact)
Why it slipped through: the converter's refusal gate checked
`config.get("attention_bias") not in (False, None)` — and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct's
config.json OMITS the key entirely (the model defaults it TRUE), so the gate
never fired and the 84 bias tensors were silently dropped. (None of the three
ranked suspects — qk_norm=0 handling, untied lm_head binding, GQA group-7
indexing — was at fault; each verified clean during the bisection.)

THE FIX (all gated; Qwen3 lanes byte-unmodified, regression-compiled):
  * converter (packages/algenta/algenta/inference.py): `_detect_attention_bias`
    probes the SAFETENSORS for `model.layers.0.self_attn.q_proj.bias`
    (tensors-are-the-truth, the `_detect_has_qk_norm` convention); the three
    biases per layer are converted (1-D, untransposed) and the manifest carries
    `attention_bias` 0/1; the config-key refusal removed.
  * engine: `_qkv_bias_add_rows_kernel` (residentk/kernels.mojo) adds the
    resident [Q|K|V] bias vector to the fused QKV output BEFORE RoPE; dispatched
    after every QKV-producing op in ALL five 7B-relevant paths — f32 prefill,
    f32 decode step, f32 decode graph, p3 JIT-dequant prefill, p3 per-dispatch
    decode AND the p3 captured graph — only when the session is opened with
    `has_qkv_bias=1` (`upload_qkv_bias` per layer). Zero buffers/launches when 0.
  * checkpoint re-converted with the biases (blob +1,032,192 bytes = exactly
    28 layers x (3584+512+512) f64 values).
Post-fix re-dump: ALL 225 compared stages AGREE with transformers fp32 within
rel tol 5e-3 (measured drift 1e-7..3e-5 — pure f32 accumulation noise).

ORACLE INTEGRITY FINDING (fixed before any gate counted)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The first ref_tokens.json was itself WRONG: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct ships a
generation_config.json with repetition_penalty=1.05, and `model.generate()`
silently applies any generation-config value the call does not override — the
reference had been produced with the penalty active. It flipped chat_1's step-6
near-tie (raw-logit argmax 323 @ 27.202 vs 374 @ 26.163; penalized 27.202/1.05 =
25.907 < 26.163) and disagreed with the model's OWN plain-forward argmax —
proven bit-for-bit: generate()'s step-6 lm_head-input hidden is EXACTLY equal
(max abs diff 0.0) to a manual cached forward's, and its RAW logits top-1 is 323
(= the engine's pick); only the post-processor scores differ (39 tokens, all
in-context, max 1.295 = the penalty). ref_transformers_cpu.py now pins
repetition_penalty=1.0 (pure greedy) and the oracle was regenerated.

prefill runs f32 SIMT tiled GEMMs at ~5% of the A100's F16 tensor-core rate
(llama's prefill is cuBLAS HMMA), and the pinned toolchain exposes no mma
surface. Decode loses too: derived per-token projection traffic at 7B is ~26.1 GB
(f32) and ~10.4 GB (p3, packed3 + scales/zeros), so the f32 arm's 42.0 tok/s runs
at ~1.10 TB/s (71% of the A100's HBM peak) and the p3 arm's 76.9 tok/s at
~0.80 TB/s (52%) — while llama's F16 arm moves its 14.2 GB/token at 85.3 tok/s
(~1.21 TB/s, 78%) and Q8_0 its ~7.6 GB/token at 127.5 tok/s (~0.97 TB/s, 62%):
llama streams every format harder than we do, on top of the format handicap.
WINS: correctness (the lane now gates clean against transformers AND llama.cpp
simultaneously), decode stability (gen256 within 1% of gen64 on both arms — the
captured graph holds the rate flat as depth grows, 42.0->41.9 f32, 76.9->76.2

L7 — MAKE GRAPH REPLAY SAFE UNDER LANES (root cause FOUND — it was never a stream hazard)
    THE ROUND-2 CONCLUSION, CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT: the captured-graph replay
    "co-residency corruption" (gate-2 divergences, always at a chunk's step 0,
    memcheck-clean, seed STATE intact) was NOT a runtime graph-vs-stream hazard. It was
    `move_slot_kv` — compaction's slot-KV copy — computing its slot windows as
    `Int(ptr) + slot * n_elem`: a BYTE address plus an ELEMENTS offset, a 4x under-offset
    for Float32. Every compaction move copied from the wrong source window AND into the
    wrong destination: the moved sequence's true slot window stayed stale while the
    mis-addressed copy shredded the lower slots' KV (dst slot i lands at i/4 of the true
    stride — a move into slot 3 overwrote the last quarter of slot 0's window and the
    first three quarters of slot 1's). The divergence then surfaced at the next chunk's
    step 0 — exactly the round-2 signature — and the co-residency correlation was
    incidental: moves only land while admission waves churn. The round-2 drain/seed-sync
    fences masked nothing; the bisect arms (NOGRAPH/NOOVERLAP) passed because their loop
    pacing changed WHICH moves lined up with WHICH reads, not because the fences held.

    THE BISECT CHAIN (every step a build+run on this branch, A100):
      * repro: race flags + graph-under-lanes forced (ALGENTA_DBG_GRAPH_LANES) -> gate 2
        3/8 divergent (round-2 signature reproduced: victims at step 0 of the chunk after
        a compaction move).
      * K=1 horizon (ALGENTA_DBG_CHUNK1): PASS 8/8 — boundary pacing changes move/victim
        geometry; K=2 (CHUNK2), K=4 (CHUNK4) and per-step host sync between replays
        (ALGENTA_P3G_PSS) all FAIL identically -> multi-replay pacing NOT the mechanism.
      * graphsync_probe (in-tree): base-captured replay ordering vs a preceding base-stream
        copy under pressure — ORDERED (Q1, 0/200 wrong); lane->graph visibility after the
        lane's host sync — VISIBLE (Q6, 0/200); base ctx.synchronize waits base-captured
        replays but NOT user streams (Q4/Q5); cross-view enqueue_wait_for WAITS the other
        stream (Q7). The stream machinery the round-2 story blamed is SOUND. Side-stream
        graph CAPTURE is BROKEN on MAX 26.5: Q3/Q3b 200/200 rounds wrong with and without
        event fences (single-node side-captured graphs work — multi-node dependency chains
        tear), confirmed in-driver: the dedicated-replay-stream arm failed gate 1 13/16
        with NO lanes involved. The replay stream is not relocatable on this toolchain.
      * graphscale_probe (in-tree): a 258-node synthetic chain, K=8 back-to-back replays,
        under spin + H2D/D2H-churn lane pressure — CLEAN in all six arms (quiet/spin/
        lane-traffic/per-step-sync/K=1/2-node). Generic graph-scale co-residency is safe.
      * ALGENTA_DBG_SCHED audit: every divergent request's first wrong token lands at the
        chunk AFTER the compaction move that relocated it or shredded its window
        (3 moves x 28 layers x 2 caches = 168 `_slot_copy_kernel` dispatches in the nsys
        cuda_gpu_trace of the corrupted run — no anomalous overlap structure).
      * THE FIX: typed element-scaled pointer arithmetic in `move_slot_kv` (both arms).
        With the fix alone, gate 2 PASSES with the graph arm forced under lanes at the
        full horizon (repro_fixed: 16/16 + 8/8).

### 1. The scaling anomaly — root cause, measured

Fixture prefill (256 tok, warm) scaled only 1.54x A100->H100 (3260 -> 5027 tok/s) while the
f32 peak ratio is 3.43x (19.5 -> 66.9 TF/s). ncu on the fixture's v2 GEMMs (M=128 chunks):

  kernel (role)          grid    dur(ncu)  occ%  dram%  issue%  fma_pipe%  regs  waves  L2hit%
  cd8a (o/down accum)    32      293.9us   12.48 1.26   29.51   17.88      64    0.06   47.5
  a0c2 (swiglu)          96      173.1us   12.50 4.72   40.12   24.89      90    0.36   44.1
  6215 (qkv assign)      128     117.9us   12.50 4.40   29.94   18.05      64    0.24   49.4

Two compounding ceilings, each quantified:
(a) WAVE QUANTIZATION at small M. Occupancy pinned at 12.5% = exactly ONE 256-thread block/SM:
    the narrow-N roles launch 32-96 blocks on 132 SMs (waves 0.06-0.36). At the serve shapes
    (M=1152 one-pass) the SAME kernels run at occ 24-44%, issue 47-57%, fma_pipe 28-35% —
    the fixture's M=128 chunking (CUDA_PREFILL_TILE=128, two sequential passes for 256 tokens)
    is what keeps them in the quantized floor. The batch-1 fixture path also NEVER received the
    round-1 serve levers (L1 flash attention, L2 one-pass grids) — its nsys window shows the
    legacy tiled attention kernel at grid h_q*m and the 128-row GEMM walk.
(b) ISSUE-MIX ceiling. Even at M=1152 the FMA pipe tops out at 28-35% with issue at 47-57%:
    FMA is ~62% of issued instructions (16 FMAs per 8 shared loads + loop/address overhead in
    the 4x4 register block). H100 doubled FP32 lanes/SM (64 -> 128) WITHOUT widening issue
    (4 warp-inst/cycle/SM both generations), so an issue-mix-bound kernel can scale at most
    SM-count x clock = 132x1.98/(108x1.41) = 1.715x — and the fixture measured 1.54x = 1.71x
    GEMM scaling dragged by the (a) wave floor. The 3.4x peak ratio would need ~100% FMA
    fraction of issue; no tile variant measured reaches it (section 3).

## MICRO-AUTOPSY (2026-08-23, algenta-ent-a100 a2-highgpu-1g, A100-SXM4-40GB, driver 595.71.05, SM clocks pinned 1410 MHz; worktree .qwen/worktrees/micro-autopsy, branch feat/micro-autopsy; artifacts ~/micro on the VM)

Owner directive: "disect more, do autopsy on micro level, you missed something." The prior
autopsies were per-LAYER (us gap tables). This one is per-KERNEL micro-architecture: PTX load
instruction mix, ncu stall reasons / sector coalescing / L2 hit / occupancy / instruction mix.
It found the missed something: a codegen defect present in EVERY hot kernel since the first
CUDA lane, invisible to every layer-level table because it leaves the byte-count and the math
untouched and only changes WHICH instructions the loads lower to.

### LEVER #0 — the missed something: every `load[width=4]` was scalarizing to 4x `ld.global.b32`

THE DEFECT (PTX evidence, not inferred). Every kernel-pointer parameter this backend lowers
carries `.param .u64 .ptr .align 1` — NO alignment information survives from the DeviceBuffer
to PTX. Disassembling the embedded PTX of the shipped binaries
(`strings <binary> | grep ld.global`) shows the consequence: the campaign's `load[width=4]`
idiom — documented everywhere as "the ONE 128-bit load path this toolchain streams at HBM
speed" — actually lowers to FOUR scalar 4-byte loads, not one 16-byte vector load:

    BEFORE (`_packed3_gemv_kernel` weight stream, shipped):   AFTER (`load[width=4, alignment=16]`):
        ld.global.b32   %r2, [%rd53];                             ld.global.v4.b32 {%r2,%r3,%r4,%r5}, [%rd53];
        ld.global.b32   %r3, [%rd53+4];
        ld.global.b32   %r4, [%rd53+8];
        ld.global.b32   %r5, [%rd53+12];

Binary census: the shipped packed3 probe binary had 0 `ld.global.v4` and 75 scalar
`ld.global.b32`. Four load instructions + four address computations per 16 bytes where the
hardware takes one — issue-slot pressure on exactly the loops that are latency/issue-bound.
The defect is format-agnostic: it hit the packed3 decode GEMVs, the f32 prefill v2 GEMMs, and
the flash-attention Q/K/V streams identically. (The earlier "f32 streams at 75-105% of HBM"
probe result survived despite the defect because 32 contiguous scalar 4-byte lanes still
coalesce to full 128B lines — the scalarization costs ISSUE slots and, as ncu shows below,
sector efficiency, which only bites once the loop is not pure streaming.)

THE FIX. `UnsafePointer.load` takes an `alignment=` annotation; `load[width=4, alignment=16]`
restores the single `ld.global.v4.b32`. The annotation is a PROMISE, so it is applied only where
alignment is PROVABLE, and it was proved on this A100 (`align_check_probe.mojo`): every fresh
DeviceBuffer base is 256-byte aligned (a superset of 16); the packed3 layout pads every row
stride to a multiple of 4 words and every chunk offset is a multiple of 12 elements (48 B);
the v2-GEMM cooperative-load column is `lc=(tid%4)*4` with BK=16; flash Q/K/V offsets are
multiples of `d_head=128` + `lane*4`. Shared-memory staging loads (`xs`) are deliberately NOT
annotated (different address space). Landed as a byte-preserved toggle: new
`residentk/loadvec.mojo` exposes `_ld4(ptr, off)`; default is the shipped scalar
`load[width=4]` verbatim, `-D ALGENTA_L0_ALIGN` switches on the vector path. Math is
bit-identical (only the load instruction width changes, not the bytes, the dequant, or the
accumulation order). Applied to: packed3 decode GEMVs (`kernels_packed3`, `session_cuda_p3`),
prefill v2/v2n GEMMs, flash1/flash2 prefill attention, and decode flash attention.

MICRO-AUTOPSY (ncu, packed3 GEMV v1, k=1024 n=4096, 1 launch in the timed loop; sudo ncu,
sections SpeedOfLight/MemoryWorkloadAnalysis/Scheduler/WarpState/Occupancy/Launch/Instruction):

| metric                              | control (scalar) | L0 (vector) | reading |
|-------------------------------------|------------------|-------------|---------|
| sector bytes utilized / 32 B (load) | **4.9**          | **18.9**    | scalarization induced a 16-B lane stride; ncu flags it ("Est. Speedup 50.7%") and the vector load restores 3.9x sector efficiency |
| L1/TEX Cache Throughput             | **70.6 %**       | **39.1 %**  | the LSU/memory pipe, NOT DRAM, is the binding pipe — the kernel is load-issue-bound |
| DRAM Throughput                     | 25.1 %           | 26.0 %      | HBM nowhere near saturated -> bandwidth is NOT the wall |
| Mem Pipes Busy                      | 27.5 %           | 20.8 %      | |
| Memory Throughput                   | 388 GB/s         | 404 GB/s    | ncu cold-replay window |
| Compute (SM) Throughput             | 58.4 %           | 59.1 %      | |
| Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction  | 19.60            | 19.05       | latency-bound; top stall = 7.2 cyc/warp at the CTA barrier (36.5 % of the gap) from the two-level reduction |
| Issued Warp Per Scheduler           | 0.69             | 0.70        | |
| Achieved / Theoretical Occupancy    | 84.8 % / 100 %   | 83.6 % / 100 % | register-limited to 8 blocks/SM (32 reg/thread); not the wall |
| FP32 fused vs non-fused             | 147 k / 721 k    | (same math)  | ncu est. +41.5 % if the dequant FMAs fused — a SEPARATE lever (changes accumulation order, needs its own gate), recorded not attempted here |

Reading: the packed3 GEMV streams at only ~37-44% of HBM (below its own f32 twin) NOT because
HBM is full (25%) but because four scalar loads per 16 bytes saturate the L1/TEX issue path
(70.6%) with 15%-efficient sectors. One vector load per 16 bytes halves the L1/TEX pressure and
restores 3.9x sector efficiency. That is the missed something.

DECODE MEASUREMENT (B=1, `qwen3_p3_graph_cuda`, gates-first; control = same tree, flag OFF).
Gates BOTH arms: G0 16/16 greedy-oracle PASS, G1 3 seeds x 128 steps graph==per-dispatch
token-identical PASS, G2 engagement PASS — the alignment annotation is provably safe and the
math bit-identical (no misaligned-address fault across the whole battery).

| cell                        | control | L0_ALIGN | delta |
|-----------------------------|---------|----------|-------|
| gen64 graph-p3              | 431.3 tok/s (148.37 ms, IQR 0.026%) | 455.3 tok/s (140.58 ms, IQR 0.011%) | **+5.5 %** |
| gen256 graph-p3             | 412.6 tok/s (620.40 ms, IQR 0.013%) | 434.5 tok/s (589.20 ms, IQR 0.001%) | **+5.3 %** |
| G2 per-step wall (32/64/128/256) | 2.301/2.318/2.353/2.424 ms | 2.179/2.196/2.231/2.303 ms | -5.3/-5.3/-5.2/-5.0 % |
| f32-graph (INTERNAL CONTROL, unannotated path) | 328.2 tok/s | 328.3 tok/s | flat (the win is specific to the annotated kernels) |
| per-dispatch-p3 gen64/gen256 | 74.3 / 57.9 tok/s | 75.1 / 58.4 tok/s | +1.0/+0.8 % (launch-overhead-bound, kernel gain diluted) |

### LEVER #0 on the flash prefill-attention twins (Q/K/V streams)

Same annotation applied to the global Q/K/V loads of `kernels_prefill_attn_flash` (flash1) and

admission shapes (h_q 16 / h_kv 8 / d_head 128), 4 interleaved runs/arm, REPS=30, clocks pinned.

now on the attention side of admission prefill.

WHY THE DECODE TPOT (+5%) IS SMALLER THAN THE KERNEL GB/s (+17%): a decode step is GEMV roles +
attention + norms + lmhead + graph replay; the vector-load win lands only on the weight-streaming
GEMV fraction, so the per-role kernel gain dilutes to ~+5% end-to-end. Prefill, where the v2 GEMMs
dominate the chunk, captures +14.2% at the GEMM layer.

### STATUS — what landed, how it is gated, what is deferred

LANDED (flag-gated, additive, byte-preserved control): `residentk/loadvec.mojo` (`_ld4`), default
OFF = the shipped scalar `load[width=4]` verbatim; `-D ALGENTA_L0_ALIGN` turns on the 16-B vector
loads. Applied to the global weight/activation/Q/K/V loads of: `kernels_packed3` (bare + norm
GEMVs), `session_cuda_p3` (accum/swiglu/lmhead decode twins), `kernels_prefill_f32_v2` and `_v2n`,
`kernels_prefill_attn_flash` + `_flash2`, `kernels_decode_attn_flash`. Shared-staging (`xs`) loads
deliberately untouched. Every measurement above is gated FIRST: 16/16 greedy-oracle + 3x128
token-identity + engagement for decode; v2-vs-v1 bit-exact (n_diff 0, incl. ragged-m) for prefill;
flash2-vs-flash1 max_abs 0.0 for attention. Internal unannotated controls (f32-graph decode arm,
first-gen prefill GEMM) stayed flat across the arms, isolating the delta to the annotated loads.

SERVE-PATH COMPILE + GATE (the wave-2 edits reach the serve driver through `kernels_prefill_f32_v2n`
and `kernels_decode_attn_flash`, which only the serve driver compiles): `qwen3_serve_batched_cuda`
built BOTH arms on the production race flag set (PF_ONEPASS + PF_ATTN_FLASH2 + P3_SERVE + P3B_R2 +
GRAPH_LANES), then `--selftest` run on each — gate 1 16/16 oracle and gate 2 8/8 concurrent
token-identity PASS in BOTH serve_ctl and serve_l0. The annotated admission-prefill kernels are
therefore gate-2-clean; the batched DECODE packed3 kernels (not annotated) are untouched, so this
round changes the serve path's prefill/attention only.

DEFERRED / NEXT (not done this round, named so it is not lost): (1) the batched-decode packed3
kernels (`kernels_packed3_batched`, the serve driver's C>=8 path) were NOT annotated — they are

graph-replay node-gap / host-seam nsys decode of the captured-graph step; (3) the ncu-estimated
+41.5% dequant-FMA fusion lever (reassociates the sum -> needs its own oracle gate); (4) the

per-M-bucket lever from the brief is feature work beyond this kernel-level round.

## THE L4 COST AXIS — tokens-per-spot-dollar on the $0.512/h L4 (2026-08-23, algenta-ent-l4b g2-standard-8 SPOT us-central1-a, tree f9bfda32 = #821, feat/l4-cost): single-stream decode BEATS llama.cpp F16 (1.12x/1.09x, $0.753 vs $0.823 per Mtok) — but the L4's fixed 72 W cap flips the concurrent serving verdict: chat C=8 loses to BOTH llama-server configs, and the cost ledger follows

CONTEXT: the prior L4 lane (2026-08-21) raced the f32 graph arm and the batch-1 enterprise
matrix. This lane races the CURRENT main — packed3 + L7 graph-under-lanes + L-H3/L-H4 — on a
FRESH L4 VM (the old algenta-ent-l4 was TERMINATED; algenta-ent-l4b created 2026-08-23
14:20 UTC), and adds the axis the segment was named for: delivered tokens per spot dollar.
Same fixture, same harness (enterprise_bench/1.0, unchanged), greedy everywhere, 64 req/cell,
medians, frozen rel-IQR <= 5% discipline.

COST BASIS (recorded at provision time, 2026-08-23 ~14:20 UTC, Cloud Billing catalog API,
Americas tier which carries us-central1): G2 core $0.014990/h x8 = $0.119920; G2 RAM
$0.001756/GiB.h x32 = $0.056192; NVIDIA L4 GPU spot $0.335900/h; TOTAL $0.512012/h
(on-demand SKUs sum $0.853608/h -> spot is 40.0% off). Every $/Mtok below = 0.512012 /
(tok/s x 3600) x 1e6.

BUILD (sm_89, plain builds, no object+link fallback needed):
  p3 graph decode driver: -D ALGENTA_GPU -D ALGENTA_CUDA (default v4 packed3 kernels).
  serve driver s2l7f2: -D ALGENTA_GPU -D ALGENTA_CUDA -D ALGENTA_PF_ONEPASS
    -D ALGENTA_PF_ATTN_FLASH -D ALGENTA_PF_ATTN_FLASH2 -D ALGENTA_P3_SERVE
    -D ALGENTA_PF_STREAMS_2 -D ALGENTA_P3B_R2 -D ALGENTA_GRAPH_LANES -D ALGENTA_CTX_1536
    — the shipped concurrent configuration (L1/L2/L-H4 prefill + packed3 serve decode +
    2-stream admission + two-rows p3 GEMMs + #816's production switch) with the L4-24GB
    chat-only context ceiling (32 slots x 1536; the rag mix does NOT fit this ceiling and
    was out of scope for this lane by construction).

GATES BEFORE NUMBERS (all on the L4, all PASS):
  * qwen3_generate_cuda oracle: 16/16.
  * p3 graph driver: G0 PASS — 16/16 greedy tokens through ONE async graph chain; G1 PASS —
    3 seeds x 128 steps token-for-token identical (graph == per-dispatch == oracle via G0);
    G2 PASS — per-step wall flat (spread 4.24% <= 10%) and strictly faster than
    per-dispatch at all four depths (e.g. n_steps=64: 5.07 vs 13.43 ms/step).
  * serve --selftest: "RESULT: PASS — selftest (gate 1 oracle 16/16 + gate 2 token
    identity)" — gate 2 is the 8/8 concurrent-vs-sequential identity check that gates L7.

DVFS / POWER DISCIPLINE (this is the L4 lane's defining measurement note): SM clocks were
pinned min=max at 2040 MHz (nvidia-smi -lgc, verified accepted) and every window was a
fresh-boot-era solo run with a 500 ms nvidia-smi sampler alongside. BUT the L4's power limit
is FIXED at 72.00 W (default = min = max = 72 W; not raisable on this SKU), and the two
engine families hit that cap differently under load — measured, per arm, from the samplers:
  * algenta serve C=8: 73.0-73.8 W peak, 82 C -> clocks back off BELOW the 2040 lock under
    the power cap (loaded samples median ~1590 MHz); algenta p3 single-stream: median 2025
    with 51% of loaded samples below the lock (74.1 W / 81 C peaks).
  * llama-server: 66.4-69.7 W, 59-76 C -> mostly sustains 2040 (median 2040 in both KV
    configs, 16-40 of 82-90 loaded samples below the lock).
This is workload power-physics, not measurement noise: every cell reproduces across its two
clean runs within 0.75% (algenta 306.3/306.3 = 0.0%; llama f16-KV 358.8/361.5 = 0.75%;
q8_0-KV 399.3/401.1 = 0.45%) — a stable thermal/power steady state, PASS at the frozen 5%
gate with wide margin. The throttle asymmetry is disclosed because it is PART of the result:
on a fixed-72W card, the SIMT-f32 engine spends its watts differently than the tensor-core
engine, and the sustained token rate is what an enterprise actually buys. All numbers below
are that sustained rate, at the card's only sustainable power limit.

## THE TENSOR-CORE ESCAPE HATCH (2026-08-23): nvcc-compiled CUDA linked into a Mojo CUDA binary — FEASIBILITY PROVEN, cuBLAS ARM AT LLAMA-CLASS GEMM SPEED, VERDICT GO

**The one-line verdict:** the NVIDIA analog of the Metal escape hatch WORKS — an nvcc-compiled
`tc_shim.cu` object links into a Mojo CUDA binary via the exact `-Xlinker` recipe the Metal
lanes already ship, its cuBLAS HMMA GEMM runs CORRECT (rel <= 2.3e-3 vs an f64 CPU oracle,
gate 1e-2) on Mojo-allocated device pointers behind a sync seam, and it measures up to 15.8x (A100) /
17.0x (H100) faster than the in-tree v2 f32-SIMT prefill GEMM at the same shapes — putting the prefill
GEMM layer at llama.cpp cuBLAS parity on A100 (14.5 ms modeled vs the autopsy's measured
14.7 ms) for the first time. Additionally demonstrated end-to-end inside the same Mojo
binary: (a) a runtime-loaded PTX module dispatched through the driver API with ZERO link-time
coupling (vector-add bit-exact on Mojo buffers), and (b) a hand-written inline-PTX
`mma.sync.m16n8k16` f16->f32 GEMM, correct vs the f64 oracle (rel 4.2-5.9e-7) at 23-39% of
cuBLAS speed — below the 60% viability gate, so cuBLAS ships first and the hand kernel stays
as the strategic no-vendor-dependency path. PROBE ONLY: nothing here is wired into the session.

**Why this probe exists.** Every remaining race loss traces to one ceiling: the pinned Mojo
1.0.0 / MAX 26.5.0 CUDA backend exposes no tensor-core surface (mma_surface_probe.sh: every
std/max mma import compile-FAILS) and scalarizes sub-f32 loads, so the prefill GEMMs sit
at f32-SIMT efficiency (A100 autopsy: our 297.5 ms f32 SIMT vs llama's 14.7 ms cuBLAS
ampere_h16816gemm over the same 895-token prefill; H100 warm pp256 13.6-14.1k tok/s llama
vs our 9291). The Metal serving path already runs the escape-hatch pattern (hand-written
.metal shim linked as a blob over a discovery ABI); this is the measured NVIDIA analog.

**Artifacts:** `benchmarks/llm_smoke/nvidia_race/tc_shim.cu` (the extern "C" shim: cuBLAS
GemmEx arms + f16<->f32 staging + packed3->f16 dequant + driver-API PTX loader + hand mma
dispatch), `tc_rt_kernels.cu` (runtime-loaded kernels: vadd + the hand mma.sync GEMM, shipped
as embedded PTX), `tc_escape_probe.mojo` (the Mojo driver: external_call wrappers, f64 oracle,
20-run median+IQR timing), `scripts/build_tc_probe.sh` (nvcc + PTX-embed + two link recipes).

### 1. LINK FEASIBILITY — PASS on both GPUs

* Recipe 1 worked on BOTH VMs: plain `mojo build -D ALGENTA_GPU -D ALGENTA_CUDA
  --target-accelerator sm_NN -I mojo/engine probe.mojo -o bin -Xlinker tc_shim.o
  -Xlinker -lcublas -Xlinker -lcudart -Xlinker -L/usr/local/cuda/lib64`. No object+clang
  fallback needed (recipe 2 is scripted anyway, mirroring setup_vm.sh's build_one_driver).
* The binary runs on Mojo's context: `tc_shim_init` = 0 on both GPUs; cuBLAS handle + a
  dedicated non-blocking stream bind to the CURRENT (Mojo's) context without any context
  juggling. SYNC SEAM: MAX 26.5 exposes no raw cudaStream_t accessor, so the probe brackets
  every shim call with ctx.synchronize() and the shim stream-syncs before returning. Prefill
  waves are synchronous admissions, so a per-wave device-sync seam is structurally acceptable
  for the probe; the integration round decides seam granularity. `tc_shim_use_stream` is
  already in the ABI for a future MAX release that exposes handles.
* One diagnostic curiosity, recorded honestly: `cuPointerGetAttribute(CONTEXT)` on a
  Mojo-allocated buffer returns status 0 with a NULL context handle (both GPUs), so the
  pointer-level ownership query is non-diagnostic for Mojo's allocator (likely a VMM/pool
  path). Interop was instead PROVEN empirically: cuBLAS GEMMs and a runtime-loaded kernel
  consumed Mojo-allocated pointers with correct results. The recipe: pass
  `Int(DeviceBuffer.unsafe_ptr())` across the FFI as a device address; no copies.

### 2. CORRECTNESS — all arms PASS the rel < 1e-2 gate vs f64 CPU (64x256x128, identical fills)

  dense peak. These are llama-grade cuBLAS numbers because they ARE cuBLAS.
* Modeled full Qwen3-0.6B prefill GEMM layer (28 layers x {qkv, o, gate/up-pair as the
  down/gate shape} at M=1024, tc_full 32acc medians): A100 = 28 x (90.5+93.9+2x166.4) us =
  14.5 ms — vs the autopsy's MEASURED llama cuBLAS total of 14.7 ms over its 895-token
  prefill. GEMM-layer parity with llama.cpp, from f32-SIMT exile, in one link step. H100:
  28 x (47.1+46.8+2x74.1) us = 6.8 ms.
* The hand mma.sync kernel clears the CORRECTNESS bar with room to spare (rel ~5e-7, f32
  accum) but lands at 22.9%/39.3% of gemmex_only on A100 (M=1024/M=256 qkv) and
  15.2%/31.0% on H100 — BELOW the 60% viability gate the brief set. Diagnosed, not
  mysterious: single-stage shared tiles (no cp.async double buffering), 4 warps/block, no
  ldmatrix, guarded scalar epilogue. It still beats v2 f32 SIMT 2.5-3.4x — the point of it
  is strategic: tensor ops we emit ourselves, independent of any vendor library, on the same
  runtime-load path (next-round work; int8 TC mma doubles the roof when we get there).
* H100 two-regime note: the v2 control's 1.96-3.1x A100->H100 scaling and clean IQRs
  (<= 1.3% on every arm) place this run in the healthy regime; no quarantine needed.

### 4. WEIGHT FORMAT — packed3 -> f16 dequant at session open (measured, both GPUs)

Layout-faithful to kernels_packed3.mojo (3 uint8 quants per 32-bit word, block-32 f32
scale+zero, 12-element row stride). Dequant kernel = grid-stride word-unpack -> f16 write.

| model | params | A100 one-time | A100 GB/s | H100 one-time | H100 GB/s | packed3 VRAM | f16 VRAM (delta) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B | 0.508 B | 5.55 ms | 330 | 3.90 ms | 470 | 0.812 GB | 1.022 GB (+1.02 GB) |
| Qwen2.5-7B-scale | 7.615 B | 55.4 ms | 493 | 37.0 ms | 739 | 12.08 GB | 15.24 GB (+15.2 GB) |

The 7B-scale battery was ALLOCATED AND RUN for real on the A100 40GB (27.3 GB live footprint,
it fit) — not just projected. The campaign brief's "~0.6GB->1.2GB / ~4.7GB->14GB" estimates
are corrected by measurement: packed3 is 1.583 B/w, so 7B packs to ~12.1 GB, and the
dual-residency cost of the TC lane is the FULL f16 copy (the packed3 original stays for
decode). Both sizes fit the A100 40GB with headroom; the dequant cost is one-time per
session open and trivially amortized by the per-wave GEMM wins above (at qkv M=1024 the seam
saves ~735 us per call on A100 — the 0.6B one-time dequant pays back inside ~8 prefill waves).
TF32 remains the zero-dual-residency alternative (f32 weights direct, 75-266 TF/s measured)
if VRAM ever becomes the binding constraint.

### 5. FOUNDER-LEVEL CHECK (angle 4) — no MLIR route in the pinned dist; the backend knows mma

Ten-minute scan of `mojo_env/.pixi/envs/default` on the VM: NO `mlir-opt` / `mlir-translate`
anywhere, no mllvm/libmojo* trees. BUT `strings` on the mojo compiler binary surfaces
`nvvm.mma.sync`, `wmma.mma.sync` and even a full `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32...mxf8f6f4
block_scale` PTX pattern — the NVPTX backend inside mojo-compiler ALREADY contains NVVM-level
mma lowering machinery; what does not exist is any Mojo-language surface that reaches it
(mma_surface_probe.sh remains the compile-level proof of absence). Strategic reading: the
custom-MLIR-lowering route would mean building our own LLVM/MLIR stack against a closed
codegen — not actionable on the pinned dist; the actionable hatches are exactly the ones
this probe measured (native object link, runtime PTX load). If Modular ever exposes the mma
surface, the integration seam designed here (f16 staging, sync seam, dequant at open) ports
as-is.

### 6. REFUTED / PAID-FOR paths (recorded so nobody re-pays)

1. cublasGemmEx with OP_N on the [n,k] weight: fails arg validation (lda >= m with m=N) —
   the row-major [N,K] weight is a column-major [K,N] and must be passed OP_T. First run's
   INVALID_VALUE caught it before any number was published; the mapping is documented in
   tc_shim.cu's header.
2. mma.sync A-fragment register order a1<->a2: the PTX order is a0=(g,c), a1=(g+8,c),
   a2=(g,c+8), a3=(g+8,c+8) — row-pair-first. The first iteration emitted col-pair-first and
   rendered rows 8-15 transposed from rows 0-7's col+8 data; the standalone identity-B
   harness (100m+k fills through a diagonal W) revealed the exact permutation in one run.
3. cuPointerGetAttribute(CONTEXT) as the interop proof: returns NULL-context success on
   Mojo buffers (both GPUs) — non-diagnostic; correctness-based proof used instead.
4. Hand mma at >= 60% of cuBLAS in a first-cut kernel: REFUTED (23-39% A100, 15-31% H100);
   the 60% gate needs cp.async-staged double buffering + ldmatrix + wider blocks — scoped
   as next-round work, not a blocker: the cuBLAS arm already wins the round.

### VERDICT — GO for the integration round

Feasibility, correctness, and speed are all measured PASS on BOTH GPUs. Integration-round
scope the probe supports (not done here — probe only, per the brief): (1) session-open
packed3->f16 dequant into a dual-resident f16 weight set (5.5 ms / 37 ms one-time cost);
(2) prefill-wave GEMMs through the tc_full seam under the existing synchronous admission
(5.6-17.0x kernel-level over v2 f32 across the probed shapes); (3) decode stays on packed3 f32-SIMT GEMV (untouched —
decode is bandwidth-bound and the packed3 lane already passed its gates). Risks, honestly:
the per-wave sync seam is fine while prefill admission is synchronous and goes per-layer or
per-wave-graph if admission ever pipelines; dual residency costs +1.0 GB (0.6B) / +15.2 GB
(7B) VRAM; cuBLAS kernel selection is a vendor blob (the runtime-loaded hand-mma path is the
documented fallback and the attention kernel's eventual home). No gitbook page; no session
changes in this PR.

## THE AMD ROCM COMPILE GATE — the portable GPU kernel layer cross-compiles for AMD CDNA on the PINNED toolchain (2026-08-23, macOS build host, Mojo 1.0.0 / MAX 26.5.0 stable + 1.1.0.dev nightly cross-check; worktree .qwen/worktrees/amd-gate, branch feat/amd-gate)

MODULAR MAX CLAIMS AMD Instinct support (MI355X/MI300X/MI325X, ROCm >= 6.3.3, MI355X on
ROCm 7). The fleet has NO AMD hardware anywhere, so this lane is the strongest AMD claim
available without it: a COMPILE gate of the portable kernel layer for AMD targets, the exact
mirror of the NVIDIA compile gate (build-runtime.yml's build-linux-cuda job, `-D ALGENTA_GPU
-D ALGENTA_CUDA --target-accelerator sm_90`). Same honesty line as the CUDA lane:
compile-verified, launch-UNVERIFIED — nowhere does algenta claim decode/GEMM RUNS on AMD.

SCOPE — the PORTABLE layer only, sessions excluded by construction:
`residentk.kernels` (f32 GEMV baseline), `residentk.kernels_packed3` (the packed-int8 arm,
all six kernels), `residentk.kernels_decode_attn_flash` (split-K batched flash),
`residentk.kernels_prefill_attn_flash` (M-parallel flash), `residentk.kernels_prefill_f32_v2`
(the 6.75x register-blocked GEMM family). The resident session (`session_cuda*.mojo`) is the
CUDA-specific layer and was deliberately NOT ported or gated.

### 1. BACKEND FINDINGS — the AMDGPU backend EXISTS in the pinned toolchain (verbatim evidence)

`mojo build --print-supported-accelerators` on the PINNED stable toolchain (Mojo 1.0.0,
ed45d567 — the `mojo_env/pixi.toml` pin) prints a full AMD table:

    AMD (ROCm/HIP):
      gfx90a         - CDNA2 (MI250X)
      gfx942         - CDNA3 (MI300X)
      mi300a         - CDNA3 APU (MI300A)
      mi300x         - (alias) -> gfx942
      gfx950         - CDNA4 (MI355X)
      mi355x         - (alias) -> gfx950
      gfx1030 ... gfx1201   (RDNA2/RDNA3/RDNA3+/RDNA4 consumer)
      amdgpu:<arch>  - (alias) e.g., amdgpu:gfx942

`mojo build --print-supported-targets` registers the LLVM device backend: `amdgpu - AMDGPU
gfx6+` (and `amdgcn - legacy name for amdgpu`), alongside `nvptx64` — i.e. the AMD backend
ships inside the toolchain exactly the way NVPTX does for the CUDA gate. The flag help is
explicit: `--target-accelerator <ACCELERATOR> — Sets the GPU or accelerator architecture for
heterogeneous computing (e.g., sm_90 for NVIDIA H100, gfx942 for AMD MI300)`, and `--emit
asm` documents the device sidecar format: "`.ptx` for NVIDIA, `.amdgcn` for AMD, `.ll` for
Metal". The MAX dist's `lib/mojo` ships ROCm engine bindings on BOTH toolchains tested
(`_miopen.mojoc`, `_rocblas.mojoc` present in the 26.5.0 stable and 26.6.0.dev nightly).
The nightly (Mojo 1.1.0.dev2026082305 / MAX 26.6.0.dev) prints the identical table.

### 2. THE GATE DRIVER + RESULTS

`benchmarks/llm_smoke/amd_rocm_compile_gate.mojo` (this branch): one driver that
`enqueue_function`s every kernel named in SCOPE — 12 kernels — so each is forced through
device codegen (the packed_int8_phase0 rule: an unreachable kernel compiles vacuously and
proves nothing). Defines mirror the two-tier scheme: `-D ALGENTA_GPU -D ALGENTA_ROCM`.

Exact command (macOS build host, pinned env, `MODULAR_HOME=<env>/share/max`):

    mojo build -D ALGENTA_GPU -D ALGENTA_ROCM --target-accelerator gfx942 \
        -I mojo/engine benchmarks/llm_smoke/amd_rocm_compile_gate.mojo -o gate_gfx942

| target | device | stable 1.0.0 | nightly 1.1.0.dev |
|---|---|---|---|
| gfx942 | MI300X (CDNA3) | PASS (warnings only, ~6 s, 216720 B binary) | PASS |
| gfx950 | MI355X (CDNA4) | PASS | — |
| gfx90a | MI250X (CDNA2) | PASS | — |
| mi300x | alias -> gfx942 | PASS | — |

Warnings are the same deprecation set the CUDA lane already compiles with (`alias` ->
`comptime`, `load` -> `unsafe_load`, `@parameter if` -> `comptime if`). Zero errors.

### 3. EVIDENCE THE AMD DEVICE CODE IS REAL (the PTX-equivalent)

`--emit asm` emits one `.amdgcn` sidecar per instantiated kernel — 12 files. Header:

    .amdgcn_target "amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-unknown-gfx942"
    .amdhsa_code_object_version 6

The micro-autopsy's lever #0 carries over: the `load[width=4, alignment=16]` annotation
(`residentk.loadvec._ld4`) lowers to a single 128-bit vector load on AMD too — the exact
equivalent of the PTX `ld.global.v4.b32` the autopsy demanded. `_packed3_gemv_kernel`'s
weight stream:

    v_lshl_add_u64 v[10:11], v[4:5], 2, v[2:3]
    global_load_dwordx4 v[6:9], v[10:11], off
    global_load_dwordx4 v[2:5], v[22:23], off offset:16
    ...
    global_load_dwordx4 v[14:17], v[22:23], off
    global_load_dwordx4 v[10:13], v[22:23], off offset:-16   # the block-crossing reload

Census across the 12 kernels: `global_load_dwordx4` present in ALL (packed3 GEMV x4 sites,
decode flash x17, prefill flash x6, v2 GEMM x6-9, f32 GEMV x1, norm-GEMV x1); the
`warp.sum` reduction lowers to `ds_bpermute_b32` cross-lane ops; `s_barrier` + LDS (`ds_*`)
traffic present in all 10 shared-memory kernels. The linked executables embed the device
image verbatim (`strings gate_gfx942`: `amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-unknown-gfx942`, `.AMDGPU.
gpr_maximums`, per-kernel `.kd` descriptors; gfx950 binary carries `-gfx950`).

Host run on macOS (compile-gate artifact, for the record): PART 0 host pack round-trip
passes (20768 triples, 0 mismatches; lengths 5376/512/512 as expected; 0 elements above the
quantization bound), then the device section aborts with the exact expected error —
"Unhandled exception ... max/mojo/max/gpu/host/device_context.mojo:3825:17: Failed to open
HIP library: hip is not supported on this operating system." The MAX host runtime routes the
AMD target through HIP; launching therefore needs a Linux host with ROCm's libhip — the
compile gate is decided at build time, not here.

### 4. DELIVERABLES ON THIS BRANCH

- `benchmarks/llm_smoke/amd_rocm_compile_gate.mojo` — the gate driver (this section's SCOPE).
- `.github/workflows/amd-rocm-gate.yml` — DISABLED by design: `workflow_dispatch` only, in
  no job's `needs`, same fleet-container pattern as build-linux-cuda; re-proves the compile
  from CI the day launch hardware appears.
- `.github/scripts/amd_rocm_compile_gate.sh` — the container leg: pixi env, then the gate
  build for gfx942 + gfx950 + gfx90a, each binary asserted to embed its `amdgcn-amd-amdhsa`
  target string.

### 5. WHAT IT WOULD TAKE TO GO FURTHER (launch stage)

Hardware: one MI300X (192 GB HBM3, 5.3 TB/s) is the natural first target — gfx942 is the
campaign's anchor; MI355X (gfx950) needs ROCm 7. ROCm: >= 6.3.3 (Modular's stated floor).
Cloud path: Azure ND96isr_MI300X_v5 (8x MI300X) — blocked today only by an owner support
ticket (no AMD quota on the campaign's clouds otherwise). Before ANY correctness claim on
AMD, the launch stage must re-verify the wavefront geometry: these kernels were written
against the NVIDIA warp (`_LANES = 32` thread geometry, 32-lane `warp.sum` trees) and CDNA
wavefronts are 64 — the compile gate deliberately makes no correctness or performance claim,
it proves the portable layer survives AMD codegen end-to-end. That is the claim, and it is
the strongest AMD claim this campaign can make without hardware: algenta's portable GPU
kernel layer — packed3 GEMV (v1/v2/v3), fused norm-GEMV, decode + prefill flash attention,
and the v2 prefill GEMM family — compiles and lowers to real CDNA machine code (128-bit
vector loads included) on the pinned Mojo 1.0.0 / MAX 26.5.0 toolchain for MI300X, MI355X,
and MI250X.

### 6. LAUNCH-READINESS AUDIT (2026-08-23, feat/amd-launch) — the wavefront verdict + Azure quota discovery

The launch-stage map lives in `benchmarks/llm_smoke/amd_launch_readiness.md` (this branch).
Headline findings, all evidence-backed:

1. WAVEFRONT AUDIT of the 12 gated kernels vs 64-lane CDNA: 7 PORTABLE, 5 wave64-LOCKED —
   `_packed3_gemv_kernel{,_v2,_v3}` (warp.sum spans two logical groups -> silent EXACT 2x),
   `_splitk_partial_batched_flash_kernel` and `_pf_attn_flash_kernel` (warp_id()/lane*4 maps
   -> silent corruption). The fix lever is compile-time — `std.gpu.WARP_SIZE` resolves 64 on
   gfx942 — but the fixes themselves are hardware-verification-gated and deferred to launch.
   The gate now prints this as PART 0.5 on every run (re-verified: gfx942/950/90a compile
   clean, PART 0.5 prints `WARP_SIZE = 64`).
2. ROCm matrix: MI300X floor ROCm >= 6.3.3, MI355X ROCm 7 (Modular's stated floors; the
   current max.modular.com docs no longer publish a numeric floor — boot re-verification rule
   recorded). MAX v26.5 notes show Modular disabling their OWN v2 attention prefill kernel on
   AMD over a NaN race — the launch bar must be numerical.
3. AZURE: the five eastus quota requests ALL auto-failed (ContactSupport); catalog scan shows
   eastus does not OFFER H200 v5 / GB300 v6 / MI300X v5 at all — MI300X v5 exists ONLY in
   francecentral. Four support tickets open (eastus), zero granted quota in any region;
   `benchmarks/llm_smoke/nvidia_race/azure_provision.sh` (sibling branch) is the quota-aware
   spot provisioner for when grants land.


## THE TC INTEGRATION ROUND (2026-08-23, feat/tc-int -> PR #829): cuBLAS HMMA prefill landed behind -D ALGENTA_TC_SHIM (default OFF) — fixture prefill 3.2-3.35x over the native chain on BOTH GPUs, 7B prefill 11.1x, chat TTFT wins flip across the board; gates all green, decode byte-untouched

The probe round's GO verdict, integrated: every resident CUDA session's PREFILL GEMMs (qkv
ASSIGN / o_proj ACCUMULATE / gate+up ASSIGN + native SwiGLU epilogue / down_proj ACCUMULATE)
dispatch through the nvcc shim when the tile carries >= TC_MIN_M (128) rows — sub-threshold
tiles and prompt tails keep the v2 chain. Weights: packed3 -> DENSE f16 dequant at first
prefill (p3 session, both residency modes) or f32 -> f16 convert (f32/batched sessions),
inside a VRAM headroom try/except that demotes to native with a printed record, never fatal.
The seam is the probe's per-call ctx.synchronize() (MAX 26.5 exposes no raw stream). Decode
is untouched (packed3 GEMV / captured graph). Flag-off builds carry ZERO tc_shim symbols —
measured on every flag-off binary; the link line is byte-unmodified.

ARTIFACTS: `tc_shim.cu` integration entries (tc_shim_gemm_f16_32c = f16 A/W, f32 C DIRECT,
COMPUTE_32F, beta 0/1 — the ship candidate; + TF32/16F ladder entries;
tc_shim_dequant_packed3_f16_dense), `residentk/tc_shim_bridge.mojo` (private FFI wrappers +
the swiglu epilogue kernel + TC_SHIM_BUILD gate), the three session modules, the serve
driver's admission paths (per-lane scratch), `scripts/build_tc_drivers.sh` + `setup_vm.sh`
shim-link support, `tc_seam_diag.mojo` (the seam-cost diagnostic).

### 2. SEAM DIAGNOSTICS — the first-prefill anomaly, decomposed (tc_seam_diag, A100)

The gen driver's FIRST TC prefill measured 252.6 ms vs 44.9 native — an anomaly, because
the probe measured the seam 5-15x FASTER per GEMM. Decomposition: bare back-to-back TC
calls 25.8 us/call; the sync+call seam adds ~2 us; an empty ctx.synchronize() floors at
~2-44 us depending on device state; and a REAL warm prefill through the session runs
20.2 ms TC vs 63.3 ms native (3.1x). Verdict: the gen-driver number was the ONE-TIME cold
cost — f16 staging (24.1 ms) + cuBLAS algo-selection per shape — absorbed by every raced
protocol's untimed warmup. The bench driver's warm cells confirm it (below).

## LEVER (a) LANDED -- kvprod FUSED into the split-K partial (feat/metal-beat, 2026-08-23): 157 -> 135 dispatches/token, TinyLlama decode +2.5-3.0%, gap vs Q8_0 narrows to ~1.7% @256 / ~4.7% @1024

THE LEVER: the feat/llama-q80gap profile verdict (kvprod 0.21ms/token and merge 0.12ms/token at
their per-dispatch LAUNCH floors; wall <= GPU-sum so the floor is GPU-side dispatch latency,
not host encoding) said the remaining non-GEMV gap was dispatch-count-bound. This change removes
the per-layer kvprod dispatch entirely: NEW attention_forge kernel
`_native_kv_decode_splitk_partial_kernel_f2s4k` (module `kvfuse_f2s4_decode_splitk`) = f2s4 with
the producer's math folded into the prologue, race-free under Metal's no-cross-threadgroup-
barrier rule by making every TG SELF-SUFFICIENT: each TG re-derives its head's roped Q from the
F32 qkv scratch with the EXACT producer formula sequence (including the Float16 narrowing
round-trip the kvprod->partial handoff physically performs); the last split (the only slice
containing the new key pos == n_keys-1) re-derives its kv head's roped-K/V pair in registers
and consumes the final key from those registers instead of the cache, while ONE designated TG
per kv head writes the packed slot for future tokens (no same-dispatch TG reads that slot, so
the concurrent write races nothing; dispatch boundaries make it visible to the next step). The
q_rot write disappears with its read.

WHAT LANDED: kernel + blob (generated/kvfuse_f2s4_decode_splitk_blob.c, forged on mma_forge
nightly) + standalone driver (kvfuse_f2s4_decode_splitk_driver.mojo) + engine wiring
(session_prefill.mojo: discovery `kvfuse_f2s4`, d64+qk0 PREFERRED eff slot gated behind
`native_splitk_partial_kvfused`, table builder omits the kvprod descriptor + binds the 18-arg
fused layout, per-step pos/n_splits patches follow the flag) + MB_MAX_ARGS 17 -> 18 (ffi.mojo +
batch_shim.m + batch_shim_counters.m) + counter probe adapted to the fused table shape.

## LEVER (b) LANDED -- small-N (2-8 row) int8 GEMV for batched decode (feat/metal-beat, 2026-08-23): TinyLlama batched B=2 3.5x / B=4 1.9x, capability-gated after an HONEST loss on Qwen3

THE LEVER (parent-prescribed): the batched decode tier ran ALL four projection roles through the
prefill GEMM kernels at every batch size -- 32-row MMA tiles 1/16..1/4 occupied at B=2..8 (and
the MSL split-K variants additionally stream the F16 weight twins). NEW residentk family, the
int8 analogue of llama.cpp's `mul_mv_ext_f16_f32_r1_N`: `_smalln_assign_kernel_simd_i8` (qkv),
`_smalln_accum_kernel_simd_i8` (o_proj/down), `_smalln_swiglu_kernel_simd_i8` (gate/up+swiglu)
-- one weight load amortized over all m_rows <= 8 batch rows in per-row PRIVATE register
accumulators, single-stream decode GEMV grid shape (ceil(n/8) TGs x 256), same int8 dequant
math. ORDER-PRESERVING by construction: per (row, column) the lane-stride element sequence,
two-step unroll and `_warp_sum` collapse are byte-for-byte the single-stream GEMV kernels' --
cross-row interleaving never reorders one row's additions. Wired into the batched table builder
for 2 <= B <= 8 (B=1 stays delegated to serial; B>=9 keeps the MMA path byte-unmodified); when
active the split-K qkv/swiglu zero/partial/apply extras vanish with the kernels they serve
(TinyLlama: 269 -> 203 dispatches/token).

small-N GEMV LOSES ~17% there (the simdgroup-matrix kernels out-stream it despite the F16

## 2-COL qkv GEMV VARIANT -- REFUTED AND REVERTED (feat/metal-beat, 2026-08-23): role-level -5% only; e2e unmeasurable (machine saturated at load avg 50)

HYPOTHESIS: the post-fusion profile put the qkv role at ~233 GB/s while `_norm_gemv2_swiglu_
kernel_simd_i8` -- SAME k=2048, SAME two-step unroll, but TWO weight streams against the shared
input -- runs ~407 GB/s. Built `_norm_gemv2c_kernel_simd_i8`: the rmsnorm stage byte-for-byte
the parent's, then two output columns per SIMD group (two private accumulators, shared
normalized-input loads, dual weight rows, grid halved to ceil(n_qkv/(2*_SUBS))). Per-column
order preserved (each column still one SIMD group, same lane-stride sequence + `_warp_sum`),
wired into the split-K decode table behind its own discovery slot (`norm_gemv2c`; the shared
`_classify_pipeline` refuses the substring so it can never pollute the swiglu role slot).

EVIDENCE: (1) byte-identity gate PASS -- greedy sequences hash-identical pre2c-vs-2c workers at
the France prompt and the 1024-deep prompt. (2) counter probe @288 keys: qkv role 0.494 ->
0.469 ms (-5%); even taken at face value that is ~0.6% of the token -- not a cell flipper.
(3) the e2e interleaved A/B could not produce a verdict: the machine was saturated (load
average ~50, sibling workloads; samples ranged 100-240 tok/s with 30-60% spreads -- far
outside the frozen rel-IQR <= 5% acceptance band), so no pooled median from that sitting is
recorded as a number. VERDICT: REFUTED as shipped (no demonstrated gain; the frozen production
package does not carry unproven variants) and REVERTED from the tree -- the kernel, wiring and
classifier refusal are all out; this section + the session memory keep the design (two-cols-per-
SIMD-group, swiglu dual-stream structure, `norm_gemv2c` discovery) for a future retry on a
quiet machine. NOT the same as the gemv-streaming `_TG=512` refutation (that was 16
one-column SIMD groups per threadgroup; this was 8 two-column groups at the same 256 threads),
but the outcome family matches: more columns per threadgroup did not buy bandwidth.

## MAX METHODOLOGY ADOPTION (2026-08-23): official `max benchmark` sonnet cells — MAX 26.5.0 from the repo pixi toolchain drives all four race engines; the thin OpenAI shim for the JSONL CUDA driver lands; first saturated sonnet cells measured (algenta beats llama-server 4.4x aggregate, trails vLLM under 500-deep saturation — the vLLM loss is queued for the autopsy/optimize loop, NOT a published win)

**What this section is.** The owner mandated adopting Modular's official "Benchmark MAX on
NVIDIA or AMD GPUs" methodology (max.modular.com/serve/benchmark) for the campaign race.
Done: the official `max benchmark` sonnet workload now drives every race engine — MAX
serve, llama-server, vLLM, and algenta — through OpenAI-compatible endpoints, including a
new thin OpenAI shim that adapts algenta's JSONL CUDA serve driver. This section records
the extracted methodology, the adoption's protocol deviations (each with its reason), and
the first measured cells. Internal ledger per the standing publish-wins-only rule: every
number is recorded here; only winning comparisons graduate to public pages.

### Official methodology, extracted (MAX 26.5.0)

Sources: max.modular.com/serve/benchmark (tutorial), github.com/modular/modular
`max/python/max/benchmark` (README, `benchmark_serving.py`, `benchmark_shared/*`,
`configs/gemma-3-27b-sonnet-decode-heavy-prefix200.yaml`).

- **Official reference config** (the tutorial's Gemma cell): backend `modular`, endpoint
  `/v1/chat/completions`, dataset `sonnet`, `num_prompts 500`, `sonnet_input_len 550`,
  `output_lengths 256`, `sonnet_prefix_len 200`.
- **Sonnet dataset** (`benchmark_shared/datasets/sonnet.py`): packaged `sonnet_4x.txt`
  poem lines. Per-request prompt = chat-templated "Pick as many lines as you can from
  these poem lines:\n" + the FIRST ~200 tokens of fixed poem lines (a shared prefix, to
  exercise prefix caching) + ~350 randomly-sampled poem tokens. Sampling seed is pinned
  (DEFAULT_BENCHMARK_SEED 0x5EED = 24301) so the workload is byte-identical across
  engines and across runs.
- **`output_lengths 256` sets `ignore_eos=True`** → exactly 256 generated tokens per
  request; the workload shape is deterministic.
- **Traffic**: `--request-rate` defaults to `[inf]` (saturated — all 500 in flight,
  unbounded concurrency). Finite-rate variant = `--request-rate R[,R...]`: Poisson
  arrivals (burstiness 1.0), and at finite rates skip_first/skip_last resolve to 0
  ("steady drip", PERF-878). At inf rate with max-concurrency>1 the harness auto-skips
  the first/last max-concurrency requests.
- **Metric set**: successful/failed requests, duration, request throughput, total
  input/output tokens, per-request input/output throughput (mean/std/median +
  P90/P95/P99), TTFT, TPOT = (latency-TTFT)/(out-1), step-TPOT/ITL, E2E request latency
  (mean/std/median + percentiles), client-side GPU stats (`max.profiler`
  BackgroundRecorder, `--collect-gpu-stats`), CPU stats, and a server-side Prometheus
  scrape auto-derived from host/port.
- **MAX-26.5 behaviors** (not in the older vLLM fork): (1) post-run steady-state
  auto-windowing (`steady_state.py`, rolling MAD on TTFT/TPOT) trims ramp-up/ramp-down
  from the headline metrics — `Successful requests` counts the steady-state window, not
  the number dispatched; (2) a default warmup-to-steady-state phase (8x oversample at
  concurrency 128, aborted in flight).
- **`--backend` semantics** (`backend_names.py`/`config.py`): choices
  {modular, vllm, sglang, trtllm, ...} (+`-chat` variants) select the prefix-cache flush
  endpoint (modular/vllm → `/reset_prefix_cache`, sglang → `/flush_cache`), pixel/video
  endpoint auto-selection, and the metrics scrape target. Request drivers are keyed by
  endpoint, so any OpenAI-compatible server is drivable.

### Engines and how each is driven (Qwen3-0.6B-Base, one H100 each, algenta-ent-h100)

- **llama-server** (campaign pin 000547513f): `qwen3-0.6b-f16.gguf -ngl 99 --parallel 32

  thread per request). GPU4, port 8084, driven with `--backend modular`. The driver
  protocol is BATCHED (`stream` accepted but no incremental deltas), so HTTP-observed
  TTFT == E2E for this engine; the driver's own `ttft_ms`/`tpot_ms` are recorded per
  request in a sidecar JSONL (`--metrics-out`) and are algenta's latency source.

1. `--no-warmup-to-steady-state` on ALL engines: the default warmup aborts ~4000

   subject of this race; the pinned seed keeps sampling byte-identical).
3. Gemma 3 27B (the tutorial model) is HF-gated and no HF_TOKEN exists on this VM —

## VLLM-SATURATION LEVER ROUND 1 (2026-08-23): nsys micro-autopsy of the 500-deep sonnet loss + LEVER L9 deep-saturation batch expansion (decode cap 32->64 + deep-queue admission un-throttle) — aggregate 2,852 -> 4,020 tok/s (+41%), the vLLM gap narrows 5.20x -> 3.69x; loop continues (worktree .qwen/worktrees/vllm-sat-lever, branch feat/vllm-sat-lever, VM algenta-ent-h100 GPU4; MAX-methodology cells of PR #834 are the baseline)

**Mandate.** Owner standing directive (2026-08-23): the algenta-vs-vLLM saturated sonnet loss
is never published as a final result — dissect, optimize every layer, re-race until algenta
>= vLLM aggregate, then publish. Same technique as the A100/H100 lever rounds. This section
is the running ledger of that loop.

### 1. MICRO-AUTOPSY (nsys 2024.5.1, serve_s4_l7 under the full 500-prompt sonnet saturation cell)

Capture: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt` wrapping the shim+driver across one official
`max benchmark` sonnet run (GPU4, wall window 42.8 s of traced activity).

| Quantity | Measured |
|---|---|
| GPU busy (union across streams) | **74.7%** of wall (idle 25.3%) |
| Decode graph replays | 1,566 replays, median **19.3 ms** -> horizon collapses to ~1.6 steps/replay (K = min remaining budget over the active set under staggered completions) |
| Prefill share of discrete kernel time | **96%** (GEMM passes 68.6% + flash attn 27.3%); ~9 s of it overlaps decode via the L5 lanes |
| KV compaction (slot copies under churn) | 7,224 copies, **135 ms total (0.3% of wall)** — NOT a bottleneck |
| Long idle gaps (>=5 ms) | only 0.64 s total — the idle is spread, not seam-spikes |
| Admission pacing | ADMIT_GROUP_MAX=2 per loop iteration -> ~13 admits/s -> **median driver TTFT 44 s** for 500 queued requests |
| Ceiling arithmetic | B=32 x ~12 ms/step ~= 2.7k tok/s == the measured 2,852 aggregate — the 32-slot decode cap is the binding ceiling |

**Root-cause chain** (why vLLM is 5.20x ahead): (1) decode batch capped at 32 sequences
(`_CUDA_BATCH_DECODE_MAX_SEQS=32`, f32 KV provisioned 32 x 4736 ctx ~= 35 GB) vs vLLM's
~500 concurrent continuous batching; (2) group-2 admission pacing leaves the prefill lanes
idle between waves while the queue is deep; (3) vLLM pages bf16 KV and swaps finished
sequences every step. Compaction, seams, and long idles are all measured NON-issues.

### 2. LEVER L9 — deep-saturation batch expansion (implemented, gated, raced)

Changes (all flag-gated; the shipped race arms are untouched — the default build keeps the
proven 32-row/2-admission behavior):

1. `_CUDA_BATCH_DECODE_MAX_SEQS`: 32 -> 64/128 under `-D ALGENTA_SEQS_64` / `_SEQS_128`
   (residentk/session_cuda_batched.mojo).
2. `_BATCH_LMHEAD_MAX_ROWS` (residentk/kernels.mojo) must track the same cap — raising the
   seq cap WITHOUT it is an out-of-bounds per-thread-local write; proven by
   compute-sanitizer before the fix (Invalid __local__ write of size 4 in the packed3
   batched lm_head at graph replay, block = row index past 32). Now flag-coupled.
3. `_P3G_LOG_HEAD_CAP` re-coupled to B_MAX x CHUNK_MAX (the narrow log-readback guard
   `B*n_steps > cap` would otherwise reject every legal chunk at B>32).
4. `-D ALGENTA_DEEP_ADMIT`: while >= 16 requests are pending, the wave cap lifts from
   ADMIT_GROUP_MAX to ALL lanes every iteration (queue-drain ~4x faster; small queues keep
   the paced cap — the chat/rag cells are unaffected).
5. Race arm pairs SEQS_64 with `-D ALGENTA_CTX_1536` (KV 64 x 1536 x ~224 KB ~= 22 GB;
   sonnet's 551+256 tokens fit under 1536).
6. SHIM FIX (found by this cell): the stdlib server's listen backlog of 5 overflowed under
   the 500-connection burst (measured: `Connection reset by peer`); `request_queue_size`
   raised to 1024 in algenta_openai_shim.py.

**Gates (serve_s4_l7_seqs64, sm_90, this VM):** selftest PASS — gate 1 oracle 16/16 +
gate 2 concurrent token identity 8/8 (multi-stream scheduler token-identical to the
sequential per-dispatch p3 chain).

### 3. RE-RACE — official saturated sonnet cell, N=20, Qwen3-0.6B-Base, H100 x1

Medians of 20 runs; aggregate = per-run total_output_tokens/duration; same official
`max benchmark` sonnet workload (500/550/256/200, seed 0x5EED).

| Arm | agg output tok/s (relIQR) | duration (s) | vs vLLM 14,839 |
|---|---|---|---|
| vLLM 0.27.1 (baseline, PR #834) | **14,839** (6.8%) | 8.6 | 1.00x |
| algenta serve_s4_l7 (baseline, PR #834) | 2,852 (39.7%) | 97.0 | 0.19x |
| algenta serve_s4_l7_seqs64 (L9) | **4,012** (21.5% *) | 109.6 | 0.27x |
| algenta serve_s4_l7_seqs128 (L9-128) | 2,975 (36.8% **) | 147.8 | 0.20x |

\* L9-64 IQR audit: 13/20 runs sit in a 0.3% band at 4,011-4,022; seven runs collapse to
850-3,604 tok/s. Census at the collapses: no foreign GPU process — the machine was sharing
the MAX-serve first-boot AOT compile (~1,100% CPU) and this agent's own scp/build bursts.
Diagnosis: the serve loop's host orchestration (stdin drain -> wave collect -> chunk seed)
is on the critical path; when the host is contended, chunk seams stretch and the GPU idles
between waves. vLLM/llama tolerate the same contention (their runtimes spread across many
threads). Per the frozen rules the outliers are NOT excluded (excluding 7 would leave 13 <
16) — the median stands as reported, the cell is flagged, and a clean sequential re-battery
(machine to ourselves) is queued before any public number moves.

\** L9-128 IQR audit: same pattern — 14/20 runs in a 0.3% band at 2,974-2,982; six
contention collapses (738-1,891). Not excluded (20-6 = 14 < 16). The deterministic band
makes the REFUTED-vs-64 verdict unambiguous regardless.

**VERDICT (round 1):** L9 is a real, gated +41% aggregate win over the baseline arm
(decode cap 32->64 + un-throttled deep admission), narrowing the vLLM gap 5.20x -> 3.69x
on the median. It is NOT yet a race win — per the standing directive the loop continues.
Per-lever B scaling: 32 -> 2,852; 64 -> 4,012 (step time ~12 -> ~16 ms; marginal tok/s per
slot falls 89 -> 63, i.e. KV/activation traffic is taking over from weight-sweep
amortization).

### 4. LEVER L9-128 — REFUTED with measurement (B-scaling peak is 64 under f32 KV)

SEQS_128 arm (same flags, 128 slots x 1536 ctx ~= 44 GB KV): gates PASS (selftest 16/16
oracle + 8/8 concurrent token identity), raced N=20 same protocol.

**Result: 2,980 tok/s aggregate — WORSE than the 64-slot arm (4,012).** The per-step cost
grows super-linearly with B: ~11.2 ms (B=32) -> ~16.0 ms (B=64) -> ~43 ms (B=128). At
B=128 the decode step is dominated by KV reads — every step re-reads each active sequence's
whole context: B x avg_pos x ~224 KB (f32 K+V, all layers) ~= 128 x ~400 x 224 KB ~= 11+
GB/step before weights, against an effective stream of only ~500 GB/s. Batch amortization
of the 2.4 GB weight sweep is overtaken by KV traffic. RECORDED REFUTED (measured, not
assumed): under f32 KV the batch ceiling sits at B ~= 64 for this workload; larger B
requires cheaper KV bytes first.

### 5. NEXT LEVERS (queued, in projected size order)

1. **KV traffic reduction — the named structural lever.** f16 KV (2x traffic cut; halves
   the 22/44 GB footprint too, opening B=128 at ~22 GB) or int8-KV-at-high-B. The prior
   "int8-KV refuted" verdict was measured at C=8 where attention is load-LATENCY-bound
   (DRAM 0.26%); at 500-deep saturation attention is BANDWIDTH-bound — the regime where
   KV quantization pays. Re-test in-regime before assuming the old verdict carries.
2. Per-step decode bandwidth: effective ~500 GB/s vs HBM3's 3.35 TB/s — the packed3 GEMV
   high-B load path (the alignment-lever census applies: strings/`--emit asm` audit).
3. Host-loop robustness: the L9-64 outlier collapses show the single-threaded serve-loop
   orchestration is on the critical path under host contention — multi-threaded seam work
   or pinned-thread isolation (also a fairness artifact of the shared-machine pilot).
4. Clean sequential re-battery (machine to ourselves; MAX-serve compile off the CPU) to
   retire the IQR flags before any number graduates to public.

**Loop state:** round 1 closed — best gated arm serve_s4_l7_seqs64 = 4,012 tok/s = 0.27x
of vLLM's 14,839. The vLLM loss remains unpublished per the standing directive; round 2
opens on lever 5.1 (KV traffic).
