## GEMMA 3 LANE OPENED — algenta RUNS google/gemma-3-27b-it on ONE 80 GB H100: the family port is correctness-gated two ways and the f16 arm fits 27B; this is the starting baseline, NOT a race win (2026-08-24, algenta-ent-h100 a3-highgpu-8g SPOT, 8x H100 80GB HBM3, sm_90, branch feat/gemma3 / worktree .qwen/worktrees/gemma3; artifacts /tmp/g3conv27b + ~/gemma3_bin on the VM)

The owner's front: beat Modular MAX's published `google/gemma-3-27b-it` numbers
(max.modular.com/serve/benchmark/, `max benchmark` sonnet methodology — 500 prompts,
550-in/256-out, prefix-200, MAX metric set). This entry records the lane OPENING: the whole
Gemma 3 family ported from zero and correctness-gated, and 27B running on a single GPU. It is a
baseline, not a win — the win path is named at the bottom.

### 1. The family port, and why it is a real port, not a shape-swap

Gemma 3 differs from the Qwen3/llama family the kernels grew up on in SIX structural ways, all
verified against the shipped config.json + transformers 5.15.1 (configuration_gemma3.py /
modeling_gemma3.py) + the 4B safetensors before a kernel was written:

1. FOUR RMSNorms per layer in gemma2-style wiring: input_layernorm pre-attn;
   post_attention_layernorm applied to the o_proj OUTPUT before the residual add;
   pre_feedforward_layernorm pre-MLP; post_feedforward_layernorm on the down_proj OUTPUT before
   its add. (llama adds the branch raw then norms the stream.) Two extra norm dispatches/layer.
2. Every RMSNorm uses Gemma's `(1.0 + weight)` gain convention. The converter rebases every norm
   tensor to (1+w) BEFORE the blob, so the existing gain-multiply kernels compute it exactly with
   zero kernel branches (manifest `norm_weight_plus_one=1` records it).
3. Dual RoPE: full-attention layers theta_global 1e6 WITH the config's linear factor (8.0)
   dividing the inverse frequencies; sliding layers theta_local 1e4 unscaled. Two rope tables,
   selected per layer at dispatch. Layer mix: full iff (i+1)%6==0 (27B: 10 full / 52 sliding).
4. Sliding-window attention: local layers attend only the last 1024 keys (a key lower bound in the
   decode attention kernel; full layers pass 0).
5. GeGLU with gelu_pytorch_tanh — NOT the SiLU the kernels fuse. New kernel epilogue.
6. sqrt(hidden_size) input-embedding scale (27B: x73.3); tied lm_head stays the RAW table. Plus
   head_dim independent of hidden//heads (27B: hidden 5376, h_q 32, h_kv 16, head_dim 128; the
   1B/4B omit the head fields and use the Gemma3TextConfig class defaults 8/4/256 — verified
   against the 4B q_proj [2048,2560]=8x256).

Built: SDK converter (wrapper-config lift + class defaults + (1+w) rebase + f32 blob option);
residentk/kernels_gemma3.mojo (the six family kernels + f16 twins); session_cuda_gemma3.mojo (f32)
and session_cuda_gemma3_f16.mojo (f16); driver gemma3_correctness_cuda.mojo (--f16, --dump-logits,
TTFT + decode tok/s); harness sonnet mix + MAX metric set.

### 2. Correctness, gated two ways before any number

* Synthetic identity gate (CUDA f32, on the H100): a gemma3-shaped random checkpoint (dual rope,
  mixed full/sliding layers, GQA, tied) run through the converted engine matches the independent
  fp64 torch reference logits to <2e-6, greedy tokens identical, at 1x/2x/3x-window and
  single-token prompts. The f16 kernels are bit-exact on it (dyadic weights).
* Real-weights gate (the 4B sibling, CUDA f32 AND f16, vs HF-transformers CPU fp32): 444 tensors
  load clean, final-position logits agree to 2.5e-4 (fp32-vs-fp32 rounding), top-5 identical, and
  the greedy tokens match across engine-f32 / engine-f16 / transformers:
  [236761, 108, 1018, 236778] for prompt [2,1756,3402,762].

The 27B itself runs the identical code path (62 layers) and emits valid tokens; a 27B-specific
token diff vs a reference is not yet run because the only same-size reference would be a CPU-fp32
27B forward (impractically slow) — the sibling + synthetic gates carry the correctness claim.

### 3. The fit: why f16, and the baseline

Float32 gemma3-27B is ~109 GB — it does not fit one 80 GB H100. The f16-weight arm (weights
f16, everything else f32 — same mixed-precision discipline as session_cuda_f16) is 54 GB and fits.
On CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6, 27B, prompt [2,1756,3402,762], --max-new 32:

    ttft_ms 859.9 (sequential 4-token ingest — decode-only arm, NOT a parallel prefill)
    decode  4.63 tok/s single-stream (32 tokens, f16)

### 4. VERDICT — this is a STARTING BASELINE, and it is a loss, named precisely

MAX's published 27B cell (concurrency 50): ~27.3 mean / 30.6 median output tok/s per request,
TPOT mean 46.7 ms, TTFT mean 860 ms, request throughput 1.98 req/s. algenta's current
single-stream decode is 4.63 tok/s — roughly a 6x gap, and there is NO concurrent arm yet. The
diagnosis is the same one the Qwen3 CUDA lane proved on day one: ~500 dispatches/token
(62 layers x 8 + 3) of host submission, no CUDA graph, no split-K attention, f16 GEMV not yet
bandwidth-tuned for HBM3. The TTFT is serial ingest, not a real prefill. NONE of this is a
kernel-math problem — the math is gated exact above; it is the serving/launch/bandwidth problem
the campaign has solved before on Qwen3/llama and re-solves here for Gemma 3.

### 5. The win path (named, in order)

1. CUDA-graph decode arm for gemma3 (the session_cuda _build_decode_graph pattern) — removes the
   ~500-dispatch/token host overhead; historically the single biggest decode lever (the Qwen3
   lane's 71 -> 330 tok/s was this + split-K).
2. Split-K / flash-decoding attention for the gemma3 windowed kernel (deep-context decode).
3. A real tiled prefill for gemma3 (parallel, not serial ingest) — flips TTFT.
4. A concurrent gemma3 serving driver (the qwen3_serve_batched_cuda.mojo pattern) so the sonnet
   500-prompt / C=50 cell can actually be raced.
5. Then the MAX-methodology cell: enterprise_bench.py already has the sonnet mix (550-in/256-out/
   prefix-200) and the MAX metric set (TTFT/TPOT/ITL mean+p50/p90/p95/p99, in/out tok/s, req/s,
   E2E). Opponents: max serve, vLLM, llama-server.

STATUS: branch feat/gemma3 (draft PR). The race is NOT won and no win is published; this entry is
the internal baseline per the publish-wins-only rule. Real-weights gate used the 4B sibling (a
CPU-fp32 27B reference is impractically slow); 27B f32 does not fit one 80 GB GPU — f16 is the
race arm. Next session: levers 1-4 above, then measure the sonnet cell.

## GEMMA 3 TILED PREFILL LANDED — TTFT flips 122.7 s -> 278.6 ms at the official 550 shape (441x), correctness-gated at every stage; beats llama-server cold and MAX's published loaded TTFT number, but vLLM leads single-stream — internal result, NOT a published win (2026-08-24, algenta-ent-h100, GPU 6 for algenta / GPU 5 vLLM / GPU 7 llama-server, branch feat/gemma3)

**What landed.** The real tiled prefill for Gemma 3 (the win path's lever #3), on BOTH sessions,
correctness-gated before any number. Reused VERBATIM per the reuse-map: `_pf_gemm_*_v2` family
(QKV/o/down) and `_pf_rmsnorm_rows_kernel`; `_pf_ropewrt_kernel` carries the dual rope through
the session's per-layer global/local table-pointer select (qk_norm=1). NEW kernels
(`residentk/kernels_prefill_gemma3.mojo`): the GeGLU prefill epilogue
(`_pf_gemm_geglu_kernel_v2`/`_v2h` — gelu_pytorch_tanh, not SiLU), windowed prefill attention
(`_pf_attn_window_kernel`, per-row lower bound max(0, pos+1-window) for the 52 sliding layers,
0 for the every-6th global), the f16-resident-weight v2 twins (`_v2h`: f16 weights widened into
f32 staging/accumulation — the eager arm's exact arithmetic at half the storage), the four-norm
row wiring (`_pf_norm_accum_rows_kernel`: o/down -> branch scratch -> norm -> residual add),
scaled m-row embed gather, and the TC-seam GeGLU combine (`_pf_geglu_rows_kernel`). Ten
dispatches per layer per tile; `G3_PF_TILE = 1024` rows so the raced 256/550 shapes run ONE
M-parallel pass. Under `-D ALGENTA_TC_SHIM` full tiles (m >= 128) ride cuBLAS HMMA GemmEx
(COMPUTE_32F) straight over the RESIDENT f16 weights — no f16 staging twin needed; the weights
ARE the B operand (that is the fit-fact this arm exists for); short tiles stay native. Driver:
`--prefill` + `--tokens-file`; gate script: `--driver-args=` passthrough;
`make_race_prompts.py` builds MAX-sonnet-shaped exact-length token prompts (+ `.text` twin for
OpenAI-compatible opponents); `ttft_openai_client.py` streams TTFT from the opponents.

**Correctness battery (all PASS, H100 GPU 6):**
1. 4B tiled f32 vs transformers CPU fp32: logits max_abs_diff 2.39e-4, top-5 identical, tokens
   [236761, 108, 1018, 236778] identical. Same gate, f16 tiled arm: 2.68e-4, PASS.
2. 4B f16 eager-vs-tiled token identity, native chain: 160 ([17084,684,910,78241,528,910]),
   300 ([236764,784,756,236754,1303,236789]), and 1200 ([1093,107,3133,600,5888,3155]) — the
   1200 prompt is multi-tile (1024+176) AND crosses the 1024 sliding-window boundary, so the
   windowed attention's per-row lower bound is exercised for real. Identical both arms.
3. 4B f16 eager-vs-tiled on the cuBLAS arm: identical at 160 and 1200 (the seam is exact-
   enough for greedy identity at these shapes).
4. 27B f16 eager-vs-tiled(TC) 160-token prompt: identical [17084,607,9899,236764,532,607];
   the decode steps AFTER the tiled ingest read the KV cache the batched ropewrt wrote —
   cache-layout compatibility proven by generation, not just by the prefill's own tokens.

**TTFT, 27B f16 on one H100 (GPU 6), MAX-sonnet-shaped prompts, fresh-process per cell (blob
load excluded — the driver times ingestion only); tiled = median of 3:**

| Cell | eager-serial | tiled (cuBLAS TC seam) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 160 tokens | 33,476.7 ms | 138.6 ms | 241x |
| 256 tokens | 54,447.5 ms | 162.7 ms (162.5/166.8/162.7) | 335x |
| 550 tokens (official shape) | 122,738.4 ms | 278.6 ms (277.8/280.4/278.6, IQR <1%) | 441x |
| 550-in/256-out full shape | — | TTFT 279.7 ms, decode 4.88 tok/s (prefill+graph) | — |

Tokens identical eager-vs-tiled in every cell ([3133,834] @256, [236764,532] @550). The
baseline's own ledger line ("ttft_ms 859.9, serial 4-token ingest") is now the bottom of the

before each of the 4x62 GemmEx calls (MAX exposes no stream handle — structural, ~5 ms of the
sum at host-microsecond seam cost each); (3) the final `_lmhead_argmax_kernel_f16` is the
decode-shaped 262,208-wide sweep measured at ~13 ms/token in the decode autopsy — a tiled
batch-1 lm_head would shave it; (4) GEMM efficiency: 28.2 TFLOP over 278.6 ms = ~101 TF/s ≈ 10%
of the H100 HMMA rate — cuBLAS-heuristic tuning (or the hand mma.sync path the escape-hatch
probe parked at 23-39% of cuBLAS) has headroom, but vLLM's ~450 TF/s-equivalent comes mostly
from (1)+(2)+fusion, so the flash attention twin is the first move.

## GEMMA 3 BATCHED DECODE LANDED — B-sequence M=B steps + f16 batch-KV fit lever; C=50 sonnet shape RUNS on one H100 at 430.4 aggregate tok/s, token-identical to single-stream; MAX still leads aggregate (~507) by 1.18x — internal result, NOT a published win (2026-08-24, algenta-ent-h100 GPU 6, branch feat/gemma3)

**What landed.** Batched decode for Gemma 3 (`residentk/kernels_batched_gemma3.mojo` +
`residentk/session_cuda_gemma3_batched.mojo` + `nvidia_race/gemma3_batched_cuda.mojo`, all
additive): B sequences share ONE f16 weight-residency; each decode step is ONE M=B plan —
rmsnorm-rows -> QKV GEMM -> `_g3_ropewrt_batched_kernel` (device `poss` array, per-layer
dual-rope pointer select, KV write at `b*kv_stride + pos`) -> windowed batched flash-decoding
(`_g3_kv_decode_splitk_partial_batched_kernel`, the qwen3 batched pair + Gemma's per-sequence
`max(0, n_keys - window)` lower bound, split-the-span partition; the merge reused verbatim from
attention_forge) -> o_proj to branch scratch -> norm-accum-rows -> rmsnorm-rows -> gate/up +
GeGLU -> down_proj to branch scratch -> norm-accum-rows, tail = B-row final norm +
`_g3_batched_lmhead_argmax_kernel_f16` (one vocab sweep for all B rows) + B-row reduce. GEMMs
ride the cuBLAS HMMA seam at EVERY B (decode's weight-streaming shapes win on GemmEx even at
M=1); the native v2h chain is the flag-off fallback. Per-sequence ingestion reuses the
single-stream tiled prefill with the KV pointers offset into the sequence's cache region.

**The C=50 fit lever:** `-D ALGENTA_G3_KV_F16` narrows the batched KV cache to Float16 (rope
math stays f32, narrowed at the store, widened at the read, f32 accumulation): 50 sequences x
832 ctx = 21.2 GB of KV instead of 42.4, so the sonnet shape fits one 80 GB H100 next to the
54 GB weight residency. kv16 gates: 4B B=1/B=4 and 27B B=1 tokens IDENTICAL to the f32-KV arm.

**GATES (all PASS):** 4B batched B=1/B=4 == single-stream tiled arm (13 tokens incl. 2 warmup
steps); 27B B=1 == single-stream; gen_seq0 IDENTICAL across B=1/2/4/8/16/32 and across the
kv16/f32-KV arms; C=50 first_tokens all 236764 and gen_seq0 byte-identical to the

## GEMMA 3 STREAM-ORDERED SEAM + cuBLAS lm_head LANDED — C=50 aggregate 444.8 -> 767.3 tok/s (+72%), nsys-proven lm_head was 43% of the step; same-H100 C=50 references measured (vLLM 1028.6 / llama-server 217.9); beats MAX's published C=50 and beats llama-server on BOTH axes — vLLM leads both axes and the gap is precisely characterized (2026-08-24, algenta-ent-h100, GPU 6 algenta / GPU 5 vLLM / GPU 7 llama-server, branch feat/gemma3)

**What landed.** Two G3_STREAM levers (`-D ALGENTA_G3_STREAM`, both sessions, all additive —
flag-off builds keep the legacy seam byte-for-byte), each correctness-gated before a single
number:

1. **The zero-sync legacy-stream seam.** The named "248 cuBLAS sync seams" lever was
   executed — and its cost MEASURED, not assumed. First the interop probe map: MAX 1.0.0's
   `DeviceContext.create_external_stream` exists, but the wrapped `DeviceStream` carries NO
   kernel launcher (ext_stream_probe2: no enqueue_kernel/launch/submit/enqueue_copy; its
   `enqueue_function` is the DeviceExternalFunction entry) and the external stream never
   joins the pool `select_stream` addresses — so the external-stream route is a dead end on
   this MAX build. The shipped route instead: `tc_shim_use_stream(cudaStreamLegacy)` binds
   the cuBLAS handle to the CUDA LEGACY default stream, which legacy_probe.mojo proved is
   device-ordered against Mojo's default stream in BOTH directions with ZERO host syncs (a
   100-iteration Mojo-kernel/GemmEx/Mojo-kernel chain runs data-correct at ~6 us seam
   cost). The sessions then dispatch `_tc_gemm_dispatch_async` (new shim entry: A-convert +
   GemmEx, no internal cudaStreamSynchronize) and drop their own pre-seam
   `ctx.synchronize()` — both halves of the old 2-sync-per-GEMM seam gone (4x62 = 248 GemmEx
   calls/step x 2 = 496 device syncs removed per 27B decode step). MEASURED EFFECT: C=50
   aggregate 430.4 -> 444.8 tok/s (+3.3%), TTFT@550 278.6 -> 274.5 ms. The campaign's
   10-25 ms/step seam estimate is REFUTED: the real cost was ~3.6 ms/step — the syncs
   overlapped bandwidth-bound GPU work. (The lever ships anyway: it is the precondition
   that lets cuBLAS ride the pipeline at all, and it removed ~0.6 s of host-sync stalls
   from the 50-admission ingest.)

2. **The cuBLAS lm_head — the lever nsys found.** nsys over the 34-step C=50 stream arm
   (`/tmp/g3prof/g3stream_c50`): `_g3_batched_lmhead_argmax_kernel_f16` cost **48.2 ms per
   step = 43% of the 112 ms step** at B=50 (its per-thread B-row accumulator arrays
   collapse occupancy; the 2.8 GB tie table crawls at ~58 GB/s), and the ingest-side
   `_lmhead_argmax_kernel_f16` cost 13.2 ms x 50 admissions (0.66 s of the 10.7 s ingest).
   FIX: the logits GEMM rides the stream-ordered seam — `logits[B, vocab] = xn @ embed^T`
   through `_tc_gemm_dispatch_auto` (COMPUTE_32F, f32 logits direct) — followed by
   `_g3_logits_argmax_kernel` (one block per row, ascending strict-`>` sweep, the fused
   kernel's lowest-id tie-break byte-for-byte); the reduce stage is gone with the blk
   staging. Same swap on the single-stream prefill tail (the TTFT first token). New scratch:
   the `[max_seqs, vocab]` f32 logits table (52 MB at B=50).

**Correctness battery (all PASS, byte-identical greedy tokens, H100 GPU 6):**

2. 27B stream arm B=1 == single-stream reference ([17084,607,9899,236764,532,...] 10 tokens).
3. 27B B=32 gen_seq0 == old seam arm (67 tokens, 64 timed steps).
4. C=50 sonnet cell gen_seq0 == old seam arm byte-for-byte (259 tokens); all 50

The cuBLAS logits GEMM rounds the normalized activations to f16 exactly like the four

**GAP ANALYSIS (precise, per the brief):**

  weights/stream at an effective ~1.8-2.0 TB/s = 55-60% HBM3 — healthy), batched split-K

* TTFT vs vLLM 56.6 ms: the 272.4 ms arm moves 28.2 TFLOP of prefill GEMM at ~105 TF/s

  prefill attention twin — a different round of work than this one's seam/epilogue levers.
  The TTFT lm_head tail itself is only ~2 ms at B=1 (the decode-shaped sweep parallelizes
  over the vocab at 2048 blocks — already near bandwidth), which is why the cuBLAS swap

## LEVER 1 LANDED — flash-style M-parallel BATCHED DECODE ATTENTION (feat/vllm-flip, 2026-08-24, algenta-ent-h100, branch race/vllm-flip): the barrier-tree partial is replaced by a warp-per-unit flash twin — C=50 sonnet cell 766.5 -> 1121.1 tok/s (+46%), step 65.2 -> 44.6 ms; first cut (warp-interleaved splits) REFUTED for a token-identity break, the fix is a FAITHFUL port of the serve lane's PROVEN byte-compatible flash geometry

**The gap this attacks (from the G3_STREAM round's own nsys):** the batched split-K attention
partial streamed the 20.6 GB C=50 KV at only 630 GB/s = 19% of HBM3, costing 32.6 ms of the
65.2 ms C=50 step — the barrier-tree kernel pays TWO full-block `barrier()` hits + a shared
round-trip per key. The brief's lever (1): a flash-style M-parallel twin.

**What REFUTED first (recorded honestly).** The first cut split each split's key span across the
block's four warps as DISJOINT INTERLEAVED SUBSEQUENCES (warp w owns keys j ≡ w mod 4) with an
end-of-block online-softmax combine. Gate battery FAILED token identity at 27B (deterministic
flip at token 2, same position across B=1/B=32/C=50 and across two prompts — a real bug signature,
not noise), while the 4B arm (d_head=256 -> legacy path) and the flag-OFF control both PASSED,
isolating the flash kernel. Diagnosis: online softmax is order-sensitive in FP; reordering the
ACROSS-KEY accumulation changed enough low bits to flip a near-tie argmax. Refuted and reverted.

**What landed (the fix).** A FAITHFUL kv16 + Gemma3-windowed port of the serve lane's PROVEN
`_splitk_partial_batched_flash_kernel` (`residentk.kernels_decode_attn_flash`) — the geometry the
qwen3 lane already gates byte-compatible: ONE WARP per (sequence, query head, split) unit
(`grid = ceil(B*h_q*n_splits/8)`, block 256 = 8 warp-units), keys streamed ASCENDING within each
split (the legacy accumulation ORDER preserved — the only numerical difference is the score dot's
reduction tree, ulp-level), BLOCK-8 online softmax (8 independent K dots, ONE rescale, the block's
V-accum — the serial load->score->rescale chain cut ~8x), and 8-byte vectorized f16 K/V loads
(`alignment=8`) widened to f32 accumulation. Gemma 3 window carried through verbatim; empty splits
keep the finite `_NEG_HUGE`/0 no-op sentinel; the merge kernel is reused byte-unmodified.
Gated behind `-D ALGENTA_G3_ATTN_FLASH`, d_head==128 fact-driven dispatch (4B stays legacy).

**Correctness battery (all PASS, byte-identical greedy tokens, H100):** 4B flash arm B=1 and B=4
== single-stream tiled reference (d_head=256 -> legacy path, plumbing control); 27B flash arm B=1
== single-stream reference (9 tokens); 27B B=32 == legacy seam arm (67 tokens); C=50 sonnet cell
gen_seq0 == legacy seam arm byte-for-byte (259 tokens) + all 50 first_tokens == legacy (236764).

**Numbers (27B f16, one H100 80GB, kv16, static closed-loop C=50 sonnet cell, median of 3):**

| Arm | C=50 agg tok/s | C=50 step ms | B=32 agg tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline (barrier-tree partial) | 766.5 | 65.2 | 923.4 |
| **flash twin (`-D ALGENTA_G3_ATTN_FLASH`)** | **1121.1 (1120.8/1121.1/1125.6, IQR 0.2%)** | **44.6** | **1047.5** |
| delta | **+46.3%** | **1.46x faster** | +13.4% |

TTFT is untouched by construction (decode-only lever): the TTFT arm re-measured 263-265 ms at the
550 shape, identical to this session's own baseline.

**VERDICT — lever lands and wins, race is NOT over:** the flash twin flips the C=50 CLOSED-loop
aggregate to 1121 tok/s — 1.09x vLLM's same-session OPEN-loop 1032 (protocol caveat stated: our
cell is the static closed-loop batch, vLLM's is serving; the closed-loop is the upper bound of the
serving protocol, so this is NOT yet a published win over vLLM). The single-stream TTFT still
TRAILS vLLM 4.6x (263 vs 57.4 ms). Both remaining gaps are named: (a) the honest open-loop
concurrent serving driver (harness-side agg) to replace the closed-loop estimate with a measurement;
(b) the TTFT lever round — windowed PREFILL attention flash twin (the biggest native bucket, same

## LEVER 2 LANDED — flash-style M-parallel PREFILL ATTENTION (feat/vllm-flip, 2026-08-24, algenta-ent-h100, branch race/vllm-flip): the windowed barrier-tree prefill kernel is replaced by a four-rows-per-warp flash twin — TTFT@550 263.2 -> 178.9 ms (-32%), C=50 ingest 9983 -> 5651 ms (-43%), decode byte-untouched; nsys named the bucket first (140.3 ms = 72.5% of TTFT GPU time)

**The gap this attacks (measured, not assumed).** nsys over the stream+lm_head TTFT arm at the
550 shape (`/tmp/g3flip/ttft_prof`): the windowed barrier-tree prefill attention
(`_pf_attn_window_kernel`, one d_head-thread block per (row, head), TWO barriers + a shared
round-trip PER KEY) cost **140.3 ms = 72.5% of the 193.5 ms GPU time** (62 dispatches x
2.26 ms). The cuBLAS prefill GEMMs are only ~39 ms (~723 TF/s effective — healthy); the
f32->f16 A-staging converts ~4 ms. The brief's TTFT lever (1) — the flash-style M-parallel
attention twin — was therefore the right first move, exactly as the A100/H100 autopsy
predicted for the serve lane.

**What landed.** `_pf_attn_window_flash_kernel` + the kv16 twin `_pf_attn_window_flash_kernel_h`
in `residentk/kernels_prefill_gemma3.mojo`, a FAITHFUL Gemma 3 windowed port of the serve
lane's PROVEN `_pf_attn_flash_kernel` (`residentk/kernels_prefill_attn_flash`, the A100
autopsy's L1 lever): FOUR CONSECUTIVE ROWS PER WARP against one head's K/V stream (the K/V
float4 loads paid once for all four rows — the proven answer to the 1-row/warp cut's
load-pressure bound), one warp per (4 rows, head) unit, `grid = ceil(m/32) * h_q`, block 256,
ZERO barriers / ZERO shared memory (one `_warp_sum` per row per key), 128-bit `_ld4` Q/K/V
loads (kv16: 8-byte f16 loads `alignment=8` widened to f32, f32 accumulation — the tiled
kernel's exact arithmetic). Gemma 3's window rides through as four staggered per-row
`[max(0, n_keys - window), n_keys)` spans folded into ONE ascending key stream with per-row
activity guards. Per-row online softmax is the tiled kernel's recurrence VERBATIM, keys
ascending — the only numerical difference is the score dot's reduction tree (ulp-level), the
same byte-compatible contract the decode flash lever shipped under. Gated behind
`-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_ATTN_FLASH`, d_head == 128 fact-driven dispatch (4B stays tiled), wired in
BOTH the single-stream f16 session (the TTFT cells) and the batched session's per-sequence
ingest (the C=50 admission path).

**Correctness battery (all PASS, byte-identical greedy tokens, H100):** 27B TTFT arm @160

opponent race client's OWN protocol — 500 requests, 550-in/256-out, C=50 in flight, greedy,
exactly 256 output tokens per request; a finished slot immediately admits the next queued
request through the single-stream flash ingest (engine-side TTFT = the ingest wall);
finished-and-unrefilled slots PARK (keep decoding, tokens ignored, ctx-bounded) so the batch
stays full to the last completion; one untimed warmup pass pays first-launch costs before the
wall clock (the engine analogue of a warm server). Same GPU solo window as the vLLM reference.

TTFT honesty notes (both directions): the algenta engine-side TTFT is the admission-to-first-

## 7B TC AUTOPSY ROUND (2026-08-24, feat/7b-tc-autopsy, A100): main-break fix (#839), flash/flash2 row-0 causal leak FOUND+FIXED (the tc_b1 gate skip-one), one-pass+flash2+NOSEAM = pp256 2.05x / pp1024 3.48x over the TC baseline — WINS vs llama Q8_0 on both prefill cells (1.82x / 1.37x, stable refs); F16 pp1024 stays an honest 0.67x loss (autopsied: flash2 f32 attention is 55% of the wall — the named next lever is tensor-core attention)

CONTEXT: the 7B TC-seam round (#829) shipped pp256 4,146 / pp1024 2,004 tok/s = 0.56x/0.19x of
llama F16 — losses. This round's brief: micro-autopsy the TC prefill, optimize every layer,
wire the batched axis. What it found first was worse than a gap:

1. **MAIN WAS BROKEN FOR ALL CUDA BUILDS (2026-08-23..24).** #829's squash merge committed
   unresolved rebase conflict markers into `session_cuda_p3.mojo:223` (the feat/tc-int rebase
   over #823's `loadvec` import). Every build importing `residentk.session_cuda_p3` failed to
   parse — the 7B driver, the p3 gate battery, the batched serve drivers. The CUDA lane
   compiles on the VMs (not CI), which is how it shipped. Fix = keep BOTH imports (each
   load-bearing: 24x _ld4, 16x TC symbols). Hotfix PR #839 MERGED same day. Lesson recorded:
   CUDA-lane PRs need a VM compile+gate attestation in the PR body.

2. **BASELINE REPRO EXACT (integrity anchor).** From the fixed tree, the TC arm reproduced
   the #829 ledger numbers within 0.03% UNPINNED (pp256 4,145.2 vs 4,146.5; pp1024 2,004.0
   vs 2,003.7; IQR <= 0.15%), G0 16/16 + G1 64/64 PASS. TC staging one-time 71-85 ms,
   13.05 GB f16 twins. All race cells below are PINNED 1410 MHz (`-lgc`), interleaved A/B,
   20 runs, median, IQR <= 0.22%.

3. **THE B1 GATE FAILURE + ROOT CAUSE (the round's central finding).** Building the 7B driver
   with the never-before-applied B1 flags (one-pass + flash2) FAILED the token-identity gate
   with an ALIGNED SKIP: got [14374, 19479, 304, ...] vs want [14374, 84648, 19479, ...] —
   the oracle stream minus token 1, 5-6 tokens aligned, then diverging. A 9-probe bisect
   battery nailed it:
     * skip reproduces at a SINGLE 128-row tile (m=128) → not the multi-tile walk;
     * sub-threshold m=64 (tiled fallback) is IDENTICAL → needs the flash path;
     * the f32 arm skips IDENTICALLY → shared attention infra, not the TC seam;
     * NOSEAM-alone (no B1) is token-IDENTICAL → the stream-ordering gamble is sound.
   ROOT CAUSE: `_pf_attn_flash_kernel` AND `_pf_attn_flash2_kernel` compute row 0 of each
   4-row warp WITHOUT the causal guard rows 1-3 carry (`if j < nkN`) — row 0 attends the
   warp's own FUTURE keys (m0+1..m3). Rows 0,4,8,... are corrupted at layer 0, and the KV
   cache those rows feed carries the corruption through EVERY layer. The corruption is
   systematic, not noise: leaking future keys biases the affected representations toward the
   NEXT token's distribution — which is precisely why the failure mimicked a clean skip-one
   (the flipped token was consistently the oracle's k+1). The leak never surfaced in a
   shipped number because (a) 0.6B d_head=64 selects the tiled kernel — flash/flash2 only
   dispatch at d_head=128 and no d_head=128 CUDA lane had been oracle-gated with them (their
   acceptance was kernel-vs-kernel bit identity — both kernels leaked identically, the probe
   shapes with single-row warps cannot see the leak); (b) in single-sequence prefill the
   corrupted rows never reach the last-row argmax — decode sees them only through the KV
   cache, where the bias shows up as a next-token flip, not garbage. FIX: guard s0 with
   `if j < nk0` in both kernels (a strict no-op elsewhere — rows 1-3 already mask this way).
   Post-fix: b1 streams byte-identical to the tiled baseline at 256 AND 128; full 6-prompt
   gate battery PASS (16/16 x 6) on tc_b1 and tc_b1_ns.

4. **NOSEAM (the sync-seam eliminator) — gated SOUND, worth +6%/+1% on top of one-pass.**
   `-D ALGENTA_TC_NOSEAM`: `tc_shim_noseam(1)` repoints the shim's cuBLAS handle AND its
   f32->f16 A-conversion launches onto the LEGACY DEFAULT stream and skips the per-call
   cudaStreamSynchronize; the session skips the bracketing ctx.synchronize(). Ordering rides
   the CUDA legacy-stream contract — the token gates are the proof (MAX 26.5 exposes no
   stream handle to check a priori): ns_256 probe byte-identical, full battery PASS on
   tc_b1_ns. Ablation: NOSEAM ALONE (128-row tiles + tiled attn) = 0.0% measurable (the
   probe-round's "seam is noise" holds at those shapes); under one-pass it is +6.3% pp256 /
   +1.2% pp1024 (fewer, fatter GEMMs put each seam on the critical path).

5. **NUMBERS (A100-SXM4-40GB, pinned 1410, interleaved, 20 runs, median; decode invariant):**

   | arm                          | pp256 tok/s | pp1024 tok/s | gen64 tok/s |
   |------------------------------|-------------|--------------|-------------|
   | TC baseline (shipped #829)   | 4,145       | 2,003        | 83.3        |
   | + L1 one-pass+flash2 (seams) | 7,998 (1.93x) | 6,883 (3.44x) | 83.3      |
   | + L1 + L2 NOSEAM             | **8,504 (2.05x)** | **6,968 (3.48x)** | 83.3 |
   | L2 NOSEAM alone              | 4,147 (1.00x) | 2,004 (1.00x) | 83.2      |

   Fresh same-day llama controls (llama-bench -r 5, solo GPU): F16 pp1024 10,448.2 +/- 9.5
   (stable), Q8_0 pp1024 5,089.1 +/- 1.6 (stable), F16 pp256 7,958.8 avg FLAGGED (samples
   4,777/8,725/8,732/8,769/8,790 — bursty per the frozen protocol; fast regime ~8,750),
   Q8_0 pp256 4,524.4 avg FLAGGED (fast regime ~4,680).

   RACE VERDICTS vs the stable references: pp1024 vs Q8_0 = **1.37x WIN** (6,968 vs
   5,089.1); pp256 vs Q8_0 fast regime = **1.82x WIN** (8,494 vs ~4,680). LOSSES (internal):
   pp1024 vs F16 0.67x (6,968 vs 10,448.2); pp256 vs F16 fast regime 0.97x (8,494 vs
   ~8,750 — not publishable either way under the flag). Decode single-stream unchanged
   (0.65x Q8_0, 0.97x F16) — the batched axis at 7B remains NEVER RUN (see follow-ups).

6. **NSYS AUTOPSY (why 0.67x vs F16 remains — the decomposition, one pp1024 pass):** the
   one-pass prefill runs at 98-99% GPU busy (window 151 ms busy 150 ms; no bubbles left —
   NOSEAM + one-pass removed the seams AND the tile overhead). Per-pass kernel mix: flash2

   llama's F16 edge lives in TENSOR-CORE flash-attention (f16 HMMA scores) — our f32 SIMT
   flash2 is the entire remaining gap. NEXT LEVER (named): TC attention — f16 flash through
   the shim (scores = Q@K^T and O = S@V are GemmEx-shaped; online-softmax between), or an

7. **REFUTED / KNOWN-COST this round:** TF32 rung for 7B p3 (needs f32 weights ~30 GB +

## TTFT MICRO-AUTOPSY vs vLLM (feat/vllm-flip, 2026-08-24, algenta-ent-h100 GPU 1, nsys 2024.5.1): the per-phase table names vLLM's single biggest advantage QUANTITATIVELY — prefill attention 55.5 ms vs 3.77 ms = 14.7x (tensor-core flash vs our SIMT warp-per-row); GEMMs are at cuBLAS parity; our ~70 ms wall-GPU dispatch gap is the second lever, structurally blocked today by the legacy-stream seam

**Method.** nsys `-t cuda` over ONE 550-token prefill (seed-24301 sonnet prompt, greedy,
max_tokens=1) on each engine, kernel summaries via `cuda_gpu_kern_sum`. Ours: the flash TTFT
arm (`gemma3_correctness_cuda_pf_tc_stream_pfflash`, wall 191.4 ms under nsys, 178.9 ms
normal — nsys overhead is in the wall, not the kernels). vLLM 0.27.1: offline `LLM()` with
`enforce_eager=True` under `--capture-range=cudaProfilerApi` around the single timed generate
(wall 99.2 ms eager-offline; the SERVED single-stream TTFT is the 56-58 ms measured via HTTP —
eager mode disables the served path's CUDA graphs, which is exactly what the wall-delta below
shows). Raw reports: `/tmp/g3flip/{ours_ttft_flash,vllm_ttft}.nsys-rep`.

**Per-phase table (550-token prefill, GPU kernel time):**

| Phase | Ours ms | vLLM ms | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prefill attention | **55.5** (62 x 895 us) | **3.77** (62 x 61 us, `kernel_unified_attention`) | **14.7x — THE gap** |
| QKV/o/gate-up/down GEMMs | 39.4 (nvjet 353+2x99+68 us) | 37.6 (nvjet_sm90 same tiles) | parity — both cuBLAS |
| lm_head GEMM | 0.98 | 0.98 | parity |
| f32<->f16 staging converts | 4.0 (249 x 16 us) | ~6.6 (elementwise casts) | ours leaner |
| norms / rope / elementwise | ~10 | ~18 (unfused eager) | ours leaner |
| **GPU kernel total** | **~109** | **~66** | |
| **Wall TTFT** | **178.9** | **56 (served)** | |
| **Dispatch gap = wall - GPU** | **~70 ms** | **~0 (CUDA graphs)** | second lever |

**Finding 1 — attention, quantified (the A100-style single named advantage).** vLLM's prefill
attention runs the 550x550x32-head attention in 3.77 ms total. Ours spends 55.5 ms. Root cause
is STRUCTURAL, not tuning: our `_pf_attn_window_flash_kernel` is a flash-DECODED arrangement —
one warp per QUERY ROW streaming ALL keys (the right structure at 1 query/decode, where the
decode lever won), so at 550 queries it re-reads every key 550 times with SIMT f32 dots and no
cross-query key reuse. vLLM's kernel is a 2D-tiled tensor-core flash attention (QK^T and PV as
HMMA GEMMs over (query-tile x key-tile)). The fix is named: a 2D tiled TENSOR-CORE prefill
attention for Gemma 3 — QK^T + masked softmax + PV via the existing cuBLAS seam (strided-batched
GemmEx over [heads, 550, 128] x [heads, 128, 550], causal + sliding-window mask in the softmax
pass) or an mma.sync kernel; the GEMM FLOP floor for 550 is ~2.5 GFLOP x 2 = sub-ms at HMMA
roofline, so ~3-6 ms is the realistic target = parity with vLLM's 3.77 ms.

**Finding 2 — GEMMs are NOT the gap.** Both engines dispatch the same cuBLAS nvjet sm90 tiles
(192x144 / 128x184 / 192x192) at 39.4 vs 37.6 ms — within 5%. The TC seam is already at
cuBLAS-native speed for the prefill GEMMs (~723 TF/s effective); no GEMM lever is queued.

**Finding 3 — the ~70 ms dispatch gap, and its structural blocker.** Our wall is 178.9 ms on
109 ms of GPU kernels: ~70 ms across 620 `enqueue_function`s + 248 cuBLAS seams (~80 us host
each). vLLM's served path graphs the chain, so its wall ~= GPU. For us, CUDA-graph capture of
the prefill chain is BLOCKED today by the same interop fact the G3_STREAM round recorded: the
cuBLAS seam rides the CUDA LEGACY stream (not capturable) because MAX 1.0.0 exposes no Mojo
stream handle to unify a capturable stream with the engine's enqueues. The lever unblocks when
MAX ships a stream surface (the shim's `tc_shim_create_stream` + `_tc_use_legacy_stream` are the
two halves ready to re-bind), or by piecewise capture of the native-only segments. Until then
the ~70 ms is a measured host-side tax, not a kernel problem.

**TTFT floor analysis (honest):** with ZERO dispatch overhead our TTFT floor is the 109 ms GPU
sum; with the tensor-core attention lever it becomes ~57-62 ms GPU — parity territory with
vLLM's 56 ms served ONLY if the dispatch gap is also closed. Winning TTFT requires BOTH levers
(attention tensor-core + graph capture); either one alone leaves us >= 1.9x off. Both are queued
in that order; neither is protocol luck, and the 14.7x attention number is the target.

+ `.sqlite`, kernel summaries `ours_kern_sum.csv` / `vllm_kern_sum.csv`, profile drivers
`/tmp/g3flip/ttft_autopsy.sh` + `vllm_prof2.py`.

## AGG-AXIS AUTOPSY vs vLLM/SGLang (feat/vllm-flip, 2026-08-24): the open-loop aggregate gap decomposes into TWO measured causes — the 34.5% admission duty cycle (our single-stream ingest stalls the decode batch; vLLM/SGLang overlap prefill with decode) and the 44.4-vs-29.8 ms per-step gap (attention bandwidth + f32 activations + launch overhead); SGLang joins the race at 1333.9 tok/s and is the new aggregate bar

**The 4-way C=50 open-loop scoreboard (same 500-prompt sonnet cell, this session):**

| Engine | Agg tok/s | req/s | TTFT p50 loaded ms | TPOT p50 ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SGLang 0.5.18 (bf16) | **1333.9** | 5.21 | 1670.2 | 31.0 |
| vLLM 0.27.1 (bf16) | 1032.0 | 4.03 | 2274.5 | 29.8 |
| **algenta fullflip (f16)** | 781.3 | 3.05 | **111.8** | ~44.8 |
| llama-server (Q8_0, q8_0 KV, -np 50 -c 41600) | 164.3 | 0.64 | 36675.1 | 182.1 |

Algenta's LOADED TTFT leads ALL engines (14.9x SGLang, 20.3x vLLM, 328x llama-server). The
aggregate does not: 0.76x vLLM, 0.59x SGLang. Decomposition below — both causes measured.

**Cause 1 — admission duty cycle (34.5%).** Our open-loop driver admits one request at a time
through the single-stream flash ingest (~113 ms at 550) while the decode batch STALLS (one host
thread, one stream, ingest and decode serialize). 500 admissions x ~113 ms = ~56.5 s of the
163.8 s wall. Closed->open efficiency = 781.3/1126.3 = 69.4%. vLLM/SGLang interleave chunked
prefill with decode on the scheduler, so their admission overlaps the batch. The lever is named:
MULTI-STREAM admission — ingest riding a second stream/device-ordered against decode (the pf_*
scratch and the batch scratch are already disjoint; the weights are read-only; the blockers are
the session's single-host-thread enqueue discipline and the token-readback sync, both engine work,
not kernel work). Ceiling if admission were free: ~1126 x ~0.95 = ~1070 tok/s = vLLM parity.

**Cause 2 — the per-step gap, 44.4 ms vs vLLM's 29.8 (nsys, c50_flash_prof, per decode step at B=50):**

| Phase (per step) | Ours ms | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| batched flash attention | 15.3 (62 x 246 us, 20.6 GB KV at 1.35 TB/s = 40% HBM3) | roofline floor 6.1 ms |
| projection GEMMs (cuBLAS) | 19.3 (51.2 GB weights at ~2.65 TB/s) | weight-stream bound, floor ~15.3 |
| lm_head (cuBLAS + argmax) | 1.1 | |
| f32->f16 A-convert seams | 2.4 (249 x 9.8 us) | gone with f16 activations |
| merge + norms + rope + embed + geglu | ~4.0 | half with f16 activations |
| host sync / launch gaps | ~2.3 | graph lever |

vLLM's 29.8 ms TPOT implies their decode attention runs at roofline flash-decoding (~6-8 ms) and
their activations/launch overhead are near-zero (bf16 end-to-end + CUDA graphs). Our lever order:
(a) attention bandwidth (the 246 us kernel at 40% HBM3 — split-count / unroll / L2 tuning; floor
6.1 ms, headroom ~9 ms), (b) f16 activations (removes the 2.4 ms converts + halves the ~4 ms
elementwise — ~4.5 ms), (c) graph capture of the decode step (~2 ms; blocked by the same
legacy-stream interop as the TTFT graph lever). Stacked ceiling: 44.4 -> ~29 ms = vLLM step
parity; with cause-1 fixed, ~1100-1150 open-loop = vLLM win. SGLang's 31.0 ms TPOT then becomes
the bar: winning SGLang additionally needs the attention kernel at/below their flash-decoding
speed — the decode twin of the TTFT tensor-core lever.

**Honest verdict:** the agg axis is NOT at a measured floor — three concrete levers (multi-stream
admission, attention bandwidth, f16 activations) total ~15-17 ms/step + the 34.5% duty cycle,
and the path to beating vLLM is quantified end-to-end above. SGLang (1333.9) is the new bar and
is recorded in every table from this round forward. MAX's published C=50 (~507 tok/s) remains
the cited external pin; algenta leads it 1.54x even open-loop (781.3) and 2.22x closed-loop
(1126.3).

**Artifacts:** `/tmp/g3flip/c50_flash_prof.nsys-rep` (decode step profile),
`/tmp/g3flip/pub/{vllm_c50_ref.json,sglang_c50.json,llama_c50.json}` (4-way C=50 raw),
`/tmp/g3flip/vllm_c50_ref.log`.

## LEVER 3 LANDED — TENSOR-CORE PREFILL ATTENTION via cuBLAS strided-batched QK^T + softmax + PV (-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_TCATTN, feat/vllm-flip round 2, 2026-08-24): the autopsy's 14.7x vLLM delta attacked directly — TTFT@550 178.9 -> 136.4 ms (-23.7%), tokens byte-identical at all three lengths; shape-fact-gated at m >= 256 (strided-batched GEMMs lose to SIMT flash below the crossover, measured, so the dispatch keeps flash there)

**The lever.** The TTFT autopsy named prefill attention as vLLM's single biggest advantage
(their tensor-core flash 3.77 ms vs our SIMT 55.5 ms = 14.7x at 550). The counter is to run
THE SAME attention math through tensor cores: QK^T and PV as strided-batched cuBLAS HMMA
GEMMs with a masked softmax between, all through the existing tc_shim (new entries:
`tc_shim_bgemm_f16_async` — generic strided-batched GemmEx, f16 A/B, f32 C, COMPUTE_32F,
transB flag for the A@B^T vs A@B shapes; `tc_shim_attn_softmax_mask_async` — one block per
(head, position) row applying the causal+window mask + row softmax -> f16 weights).

**GQA batching (the layout trick).** gemma3's g = h_q/h_kv query heads share each KV head, so
the batch runs over the h_kv KV heads with g*M rows per batch: Q is packed head-major
[h_q, m, d] f16 (one Mojo kernel, the attention scale rides this pack = pre-scaled scores),
K/V are read STRAIGHT FROM the resident cache as strided [n_keys, d] views (leading dimension
h_kv*d, per-batch offset hk*d — zero K/V copies on the kv16 batched session; the f32-KV
single-stream session stages the key range to f16 per layer, ~3 ms of the total). Softmax
rows are the same [h_q, m] grid; PV output lands head-major [h_q, m, d] f32 and one unpack
kernel restores the position-major [m, h_q*d] the o_proj seam consumes. Per layer: 2 Mojo
kernels (pack, unpack) + 2 staging converts (f32-KV sessions only) + 4 shim calls — all
stream-ordered, zero device syncs.

**Correctness (byte-identical greedy tokens, H100, all PASS):** @160 [17084, 607, 9899,
236764, 532, 607, 990, 776] == reference; @256 [3133, 834, 529, ...] == reference; @550
[236764, 532, 3819, 11015, 910, 2473, 236787, 107] == the legacy seam arm. f16 HMMA
attention with f32 accumulate holds the token identity bar exactly like the f16-A projection
seams have all campaign.

**Numbers (27B f16, one H100, fresh process per cell, median of 3):**

| N | flash SIMT (prior lever) | + TC attention | delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 160 | 121.1 | 121.97 (flash path kept — below crossover) | — |
| 256 | 132.3 | **121.68** | **-8.0%** |
| 550 (official) | 178.9 | **136.41 (134.5/136.4/137.7)** | **-23.7%** |

**REFUTED IN THE SAME ATTEMPT (measured, recorded):** the first cut WITHOUT the m-gate lost
@160 (152.9 vs flash 121.1) — the strided-batched GEMMs + K/V staging only amortize from
m >= 256; the dispatch is therefore shape-fact-gated on the tile row count (256 crossover
measured on this H100), never on the model name. Also recorded: a naive @550 "OOM" during
bring-up was NOT a memory bug — it was two overlapping 56 GB processes colliding on one GPU
(verified: single process fits with ~23 GB headroom; the allocator log's 286 GB figure was
the collided second process's view).

**Where the remaining TTFT gap sits (updated budget, 136.4 ms @550):** GPU kernels now
~55-60 ms (GEMMs ~39 at cuBLAS parity + TC attention ~4 + norms/rope/elementwise ~12) —
the remaining ~75-80 ms is the HOST dispatch gap across ~750 enqueues/seams per prefill,
the CUDA-graph lever still blocked by the legacy-stream interop. vLLM: 56 ms served. The
kernel-side attention delta is closed to ~parity; the interop is the whole remaining story.

## LEVER REFUTED AT MEASURED FLOOR — decode-attention bandwidth via split-count tuning (feat/vllm-flip round 2, 2026-08-24): n_splits 8 and 32 BOTH lose to the shipping 16 at C=50 (1103-1107 / 1097 vs 1126 tok/s), tokens byte-identical — the block-8 SIMT flash decode kernel is split-count-saturated at 40% HBM3, so the remaining decode-attention headroom is kernel-restructuring work, not a tuning knob

**Hypothesis.** The decode flash partial streams the C=50 KV at 1.35 TB/s (40% of HBM3,
15.3 ms of the 44.4 ms step; roofline floor 6.1 ms). If it were split-starved, more/fewer
split-K units would move it toward roofline. Measured, same fullflip arm, C=50 closed-loop
(median, tokens byte-identical to the legacy seam arm in all three):

| decode n_splits | C=50 agg tok/s | vs shipping 16 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8 | 1105.1 (1103.0/1107.2) | -1.9% |
| **16 (shipping)** | **1126.3** | — |
| 32 | 1097.2 | -2.6% |

**Verdict: REFUTED as a tuning lever, documented as a floor.** Both directions lose, so the
16-split grid is the split-count optimum at B=50 and the 1.35 TB/s figure is NOT
split-starvation — it is the block-8 SIMT kernel's own streaming efficiency (8-byte f16
loads, one warp per (seq, head, split) unit, exp/softmax interleave). Closing the
15.3 -> 6.1 ms gap needs a restructured decode-attention kernel (the decode twin of the
tensor-core attention lever, or a wider-vector/L2-pinned flash-decoding), which is queued
rather than a knob left on the table. Nothing published from a refutation.

**Agg-axis status after this round (all same-session, C=50):** closed-loop 1126.3 (upper
bound), open-loop 781.3 (69.4% duty) vs vLLM 1032.0 / SGLang 1333.9. The two remaining agg
levers are (a) admission overlap (would lift open-loop toward the 1126 ceiling) and (b)
decode-step time (44.4 ms; needs the decode-attention restructure + f16 activations) — both
named, neither landed this round; admission overlap is blocked by the same MAX
no-stream-handle interop that blocks the TTFT CUDA-graph lever.
## Model-agnostic onboarding + fact-driven bench battery (2026-08-24, branch feat/model-agnostic-conformance, PR #847)

OWNER MANDATE: "any LLM model should work on this hardware; test and optimize
once on hardware, then it works for any model whose facts fall in the proven
envelope" + "our benchmarks must withstand any of new models." This round makes
both the SUPPORT decision and the THROUGHPUT battery pure functions of the
normalized fact manifest — zero per-model code, zero forked drivers.

1. **ONBOARDING LOOP** (`algenta_conform.py onboard <hf-repo-or-local-config>`,
   logic in `packages/algenta/algenta/onboarding.py`): resolve config ->
   extract facts -> per-backend capability verdict -> staging-tier-gap analysis
   -> support-matrix row + JSON ledger line. A pure-staging refusal names the
   exact `ALGENTA_STAGE_<n>` tier that flips the model supported, and
   `backend_staging_ceiling` distinguishes a missing build from a hardware
   limit (Metal's 32 KiB threadgroup caps it at the 6144 tier; NVIDIA's
   163 KiB opt-in budget builds the big tiers). 12 unit tests fix the decision
   layer (`tests/test_onboarding.py`).

2. **ONBOARDING BATTERY (verdicts, facts-not-names):** 10 diverse models, both
   backends. Supported on CUDA + Metal: Qwen3-1.7B (grouped_fa_steel),
   TinyLlama-1.1B + SmolLM2-360M (parametric_native_decode). CUDA-only
   (staging above Metal's ceiling): Qwen2.5-7B (stage 18944), Llama-3.2-3B
   (stage 8192), Mistral-7B-v0.3 (stage 14336). Refused both backends (typed,
   honest): Phi-3.5-mini (head_dim 96 not a power of two + longrope),
   gemma-2-2b (gelu_pytorch_tanh + window 4096 + softcaps 50/30). gemma-3-27b
   runs its own CUDA lane (separate kernel set), not this qwen3_llama path.

3. **FACT-DRIVEN BENCH** (`scripts/algenta_bench.py`): one entry point,
   shapes x concurrency, driven purely by the converter output, REUSING the
   existing doors (no per-model harness): the Metal arm drives the production
   SDK path (`decode` single-stream TTFT+decode, `decode_batched` concurrent
   agg); the CUDA arm drives `conform_generate_cuda` (gained `CONFORM_TIMING`
   + a `--prompt-len` override so ONE converted checkpoint serves every
   prefill shape — the blob is prompt-independent).

4. **BENCH WITHSTANDS NEW MODELS (the proof):**
   * Metal, SmolLM2-360M-Instruct (NEW): TTFT 35.7/40.6/84.5 ms @160/256/550,
     single-stream decode 413/205/331 tok/s, agg@8 720/333/310 tok/s.

## 4-WAY ENGINE RACE — Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on A100: algenta CUDA vs llama.cpp vs vLLM vs SGLang (2026-08-24, algenta-ent-a100, branch race/7b-4way-realrace)

CONTEXT: owner directive — every benchmark is us vs llama.cpp vs vLLM vs other reputable
engines; publish wins only, the ledger gets everything. This round extends the published
Q8_0 prefill race (gitbook/benchmarks/nvidia-llm-throughput.md) to vLLM and SGLang, adds
server TTFT cells, and adds the concurrent-requests aggregate axis (c=1/8/32, 256 out,
greedy). Harness: `benchmarks/llm_smoke/nvidia_race/four_way_race.py` (stdlib only; kills
every server between engines; solo-GPU wait before each run; 3 excluded warmups + 7
measured runs per server cell, median + IQR; algenta cells = 20 runs/cell with the 16-token
oracle gate inside every run).

**Machine:** algenta-ent-a100 (GCP a2-highgpu-1g), 1x A100-SXM4-40GB, driver 595.71.05,
Ubuntu 22.04, SM clocks pinned 1410 MHz (`nvidia-smi -lgc 1410,1410`), solo GPU for every
timed window.

**Engines (all serving the SAME unmodified HF checkpoint unless noted):**

## TC PREFILL ATTENTION LANDED ON THE 7B LANE — the gemma3 vLLM-flip lever ported shape-fact-gated (feat/7b-tc-attention, 2026-08-24/25, algenta-ent-a100): the 4-way prefill losses attacked at the named lever

CONTEXT: the 4-way race (previous section) left prefill losses vs vLLM bf16 (pp256 0.88x,
pp1024 0.51x) and SGLang bf16 (pp1024 0.53x) with the autopsy's named lever: our flash2 f32
SIMT attention was ~55% of the pp1024 wall while the opponents run tensor-core f16 flash.
The gemma3 lane's vLLM-flip round 2 landed exactly that lever (ledger "LEVER 3 LANDED —
TENSOR-CORE PREFILL ATTENTION via cuBLAS strided-batched QK^T + softmax + PV"); this round
ports it to the 7B packed-int8 TC lane.

**The port (additive, -D ALGENTA_7B_PF_TCATTN, session_cuda_p3.mojo):** the TC prefill's
causal attention dispatches, under the shape-fact gate, the strided-batched cuBLAS HMMA
pipeline VERBATIM from the gemma3 round — (i) `_pf_q_pack_hm_f16` (Q [m, h_q*d] f32 ->
head-major [h_q, m, d] f16, the attention scale rides the pack), (ii) per-layer f32->f16
staging of the key range from the f32 KV cache (the additive route — no KV layout change;
the 7B cache stays f32), (iii) QK^T GemmStridedBatchedEx batched over the h_kv KV heads
(GQA: g=7 query heads per KV head ride each batch as g*m rows), (iv) `_attn_softmax_mask_
kernel` causal mask + row softmax -> P f16 (window=0: the family has no sliding layers),
(v) PV GemmStridedBatchedEx, (vi) `_pf_attn_unpack_hm_f32` back to position-major for the
o_proj seam. The two layout kernels are imported VERBATIM from residentk.kernels_prefill_
gemma3 (family-agnostic pure data movement — no twin, no duplication).

**Gate facts (the campaign discipline):**
* SHAPE FACT: the dispatch gate is `TC_NOSEAM and d_head == 128 and m >= _PF_TCATTN_MIN_M`.
  NOSEAM is part of the gate because the async shim entries enqueue without syncs — only
  the legacy-stream ordering contract keeps the pipeline race-free (sync-seam builds keep
  the SIMT kernels). `_PF_TCATTN_MIN_M = 256` — the gemma3 H100 crossover fact REVALIDATED on the A100 by this
  round's A/B: at m=256 the TC path wins +25.0%/+25.2% (10,606/10,626 vs 8,508/8,496) and at
  m=1024 +76.0%/+75.7% (12,261/12,244 vs 6,965/6,969) — the 256 gate stands on both parts.
  (No sub-256 tile was raced this round; below-gate tiles keep flash2 by construction.)
* CORRECTNESS: run_gates_7b.py on the TA binary (p3 arm): **6/6 PASS, 16/16 on every prompt** (fixture +
  chat_0..4; the fixture and chat_0 are 256-token prompts = TC attention ACTIVE; chat_1..4
  are 41-46 tokens = flash2 fallback regression probe). The fixture (256-token
  prompt => m=256 => TC attention ACTIVE) is the direct arithmetic probe; the five chat
  prompts (m < 256 => flash2 fallback) are the regression probe of the flag-off path inside
  the same binary.
* FLAG-OFF ARM: the autopsy ship binary (tc_b1_ns) rebuilt from the SAME tree is the A/B
  control — its cells are byte-identical protocol to the published race.

## ROUND 3 — BOTH WIN-PATH LEVERS CONFIRMED AT THEIR TOOLCHAIN FLOOR (feat/vllm-flip round 3, 2026-08-25, algenta-ent-h100, GPUs 1-7): (a) multi-stream admission RE-PROBED and still blocked — MAX 1.0.0 (ed45d567) DeviceStream still has NO kernel launcher; (b) decode-attention GQA-adjacency grid remap MEASURED and REFUTED (byte-identical, C=50 1116/1110 vs 1126 baseline — GQA K/V re-reads are already L2-cached) — the agg/TTFT wins both remain gated on a stream-handle interop MAX has not shipped

**(a) Multi-stream admission (the agg-axis win path) — re-probed, still blocked.** Round 2
established the CUDA-graph and multi-stream levers are blocked because MAX 1.0.0's
`create_external_stream` returns a `DeviceStream` with no kernel-launch surface. Round 3
re-ran the probe on the current toolchain (Mojo 1.0.0 ed45d567 — UNCHANGED): the probe still
fails with `'DeviceStream' value has no attribute 'submit'` / `no attribute 'enqueue_copy'`.
So ingest (prefill) still cannot overlap decode on a second stream, the open-loop admission
duty cycle stays ~69%, and the agg-axis win over vLLM/SGLang remains gated on a stream-handle
interop MAX has not shipped. The `tc_shim_create_stream` + `_tc_use_legacy_stream` hooks stay
staged, ready to re-bind the moment MAX exposes a launchable stream.

**(b) Decode-attention restructure, attempt 1 — GQA-adjacency grid remap, REFUTED at measure.**
Hypothesis: the two GQA query heads sharing one KV head are spaced n_splits (16) warps apart
in the (seq, q-head, split) grid, so the second sibling's K/V read might miss L2 and re-stream
from HBM; remapping the grid to (seq, kv-head, split, gqa-index) puts the siblings on adjacent
warps (same block) so the shared K/V hits L2, ~halving HBM K/V traffic. Implemented as a pure
scheduling remap behind `-D ALGENTA_G3_DECODE_GQA_ADJ` (each unit still computes the identical
(seq, head, split) partial into the canonical slot — byte-for-byte output by construction).
Measured: B=32 gate byte-identical (PASS); C=50 agg 1115.9 / 1109.8 (median ~1113) vs the
1126.3 baseline = **-1.2%, a LOSS**. Diagnosis: the GQA K/V re-reads are ALREADY L2-cached even
with the siblings 16 warps apart, so the remap buys no HBM traffic; the extra index arithmetic
costs slightly more than it saves. Refuted, code reverted. The 40%-HBM3 decode-attention figure
is therefore the block-8 kernel's own streaming efficiency, not GQA re-read traffic.

**Status of the queue after round 3:** every remaining win-path lever is now known to be
either (i) toolchain-blocked (CUDA graphs + multi-stream admission — both need a MAX
stream handle, re-confirmed absent) or (ii) measured-at-floor / refuted (decode-attention
split-count round 2, GQA-adjacency round 3). f16 activations (kills the ~2.4 ms/step f32->f16
seam converts + halves elementwise, est ~4-5 ms/step -> closed-loop ~1250, open-loop ~865) is
the one remaining tractable step-time lever; it improves but does NOT flip either axis, since
both flips are gated on the stream-handle interop. Tracked as the next concrete increment.

### Round-3 measure cycle (full re-measure, same cell, GPUs freed after)

unchanged — admission duty still ~69%). Reference engines re-run this round, stable to

## FRONT 3 — Qwen2.5-7B CUDA vs TensorRT-LLM 1.2.1, the pp1024 / RAG-4096 gap round
### algenta-ent-a100 (A100-SXM4-40GB, solo GPU), 2026-09-16 00:09-01:57 UTC, clocks pinned 1410 MHz
### branch feat/7b-fused-flash-attn-v2, based on main @ 8b432377f (post-#988). LEDGER ONLY — not published.

Round 2 shipped _c8 and left pp1024 at 0.925x and RAG-4096 at 0.769x. This round attacked the
ranked per-layer gaps and **flipped pp1024 (1.077x) and extended pp256 (1.591x -> 1.858x);
RAG-4096 improved 0.769x -> 0.925x and did NOT flip.**

### Levers (each its own build flag, default OFF; the _c8 binary is byte-identical without them)
| flag | what it replaces | measured per-layer effect (pp1024, nsys) |
|---|---|---|
| `ALGENTA_7B_PF_FA` | the five-pass TC attention chain (head-major Q pack, QK^T GemmEx, masked softmax, PV GemmEx, head-major O unpack) with ONE hand-written WMMA FlashAttention-2 kernel in tc_shim.cu | attention 439.8 -> 141.3 us/layer (**-298.5 us**, -8.36 ms/prefill) |
| `ALGENTA_7B_PF_FASTEXP` | the f16 SwiGLU epilogue's scalar Mojo `exp` (~171 lane-cycles each) with the shim's `__expf` = ex2.approx.ftz, division-free 2-D grid, 16-byte vectors | 172.6 -> 79.0 us/layer (**-93.5 us**, -2.62 ms/prefill). Now BELOW TRT-LLM's silu_and_mul at 82.1 us |
| `ALGENTA_7B_PF_BIASROPE` | the `_qkv_bias_add_rows_kernel` + `_pf_ropewrt_kernel` pair with one fused launch (bit-exact) | 93.6 -> 62.7 us/layer (**-30.9 us**, -0.87 ms/prefill) |

The FA kernel's first cut measured **367 us/layer — SLOWER than the chain it replaces** (~7% MFU).
Root cause: a 128-half shared row stride is exactly 64 32-bit banks, so every row of a 16-row WMMA
tile landed in the same bank group and each `ldmatrix` serialized 8-way. Padding the operand tiles
to 136 halves (272 B = a 4-bank row shift, still 16-byte aligned for the uint4 staging stores)
took it to **121.9 us/layer (3.0x)**; in-session it measures 115.0 us/layer. Both numbers are
recorded in the constant's comment so the padding is never "cleaned up" back.

### Per-layer decomposition, one pp1024 prefill (nsys, m=1024 one-pass window, 28 layers, 2 executions)
| family | _c8 us/layer | _d8 us/layer | TRT-LLM us/layer |
|---|---|---|---|
| cuBLAS/cutlass projection GEMMs | 2088.4 | 1934.8 | 2078.3 |
| attention (all passes) | 439.8 | 141.3 | 87.0 |
| SwiGLU epilogue | 172.6 | 79.0 | 82.1 |
| bias + RoPE + KV-write | 93.6 | 62.7 | 21.7 |
| rmsnorm rows | 38.8 | 39.0 | 30.7 |
| f32->f16 convert (K/V staging) | 29.8 | 26.3 | 0 (native bf16 KV) |
| **GPU busy per prefill** | **75.094 ms** | **63.686 ms** | ~64.6 ms of a 72.2 ms wall |

### A/B sweep (driver median of 20 runs/cell; one process per arm; baseline bracketing; G0 16/16 + G1 64/64 PASS in EVERY process; all cells rel-IQR <= 1.0%, outliers 0)
| arm | flags over _c8 | pp256 | pp1024 | gen64 | gen256 | G0 | G1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| _c8 run1 | — (round 2's adopted arm, rebuilt) | 11,385.6 | 13,218.5 | 83.36 | 82.66 | PASS | 64/64 |
| _d1 | +FA | 12,279.8 | 14,814.0 | 83.25 | 82.56 | PASS | 64/64 |
| _d2 | +FASTEXP | 11,632.1 | 13,509.7 | 83.63 | 82.92 | PASS | 64/64 |
| _d3 | +BIASROPE | 11,419.3 | 13,357.8 | 83.41 | 82.72 | PASS | 64/64 |
| _d4 | +FA +FASTEXP | 12,615.6 | 15,158.1 | 83.43 | 82.72 | PASS | 64/64 |
| **_d8** | **+FA +FASTEXP +BIASROPE** | **12,746.2** | **15,264.6** | **83.43** | **82.74** | PASS | 64/64 |
| _c8 run2 | — (drift armor) | 11,429.4 | 13,244.3 | 83.39 | 82.69 | PASS | 64/64 |

Baseline drift between the two bracketing _c8 runs: pp256 +0.38%, pp1024 +0.20%, gen64 +0.03%,
gen256 +0.02%. Every lever delta below exceeds it. Deltas vs the run-2 baseline:

### RAG-4096: why it did not flip — the exact remaining blocker, accounted for
Modelled from the measured _d8 pp1024 decomposition plus fa_probe's per-shape FA timings at all
four RAG chunk shapes (121.9 + 270.3 + 449.5 + 642.0 us/layer = 1483.7 us/layer x 28 = 41.5 ms):
| term | ours | TRT-LLM | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| projection GEMMs (4 chunks) | 216.7 ms | 232.8 ms | **-16.1 ms (we win)** |
| fused flash attention | 41.5 ms | 24.4 ms | **+17.1 ms** |
| K/V f32->f16 staging | 7.4 ms | 0 (native bf16 KV) | **+7.4 ms** |
| bias+RoPE+KV-write | 7.0 ms | 2.4 ms | **+4.6 ms** |
| rmsnorm | 4.4 ms | 3.4 ms | +0.9 ms |
| SwiGLU | 8.9 ms | 9.2 ms | -0.3 ms |
| **modelled total** | **287.2 ms** | **272.8 ms** | +14.4 ms |
| **measured wall** | **293.1 ms** | **271.2 ms** | +21.9 ms |

Modelled 287.2 vs measured 293.1 = 2.0% unaccounted (host/launch gaps). The three blockers, in
measured ms, and what each needs:
1. **FA efficiency at long n_keys (+17.1 ms).** Ours runs ~26% MFU at the RAG chunk shapes,
   TRT-LLM's fmha_v2 ~44%. Two named causes, both structural to this first implementation:
   (a) no `cp.async` K/V double-buffering, so at 2 CTAs/SM (60 KB dynamic shared, 174 registers,
   0 spills) the global-load latency of each key block is exposed rather than overlapped;
   (b) the f16 P tile round-trips through shared memory because the WMMA API cannot reinterpret
   an f32 accumulator as an f16 `matrix_a` operand — raw `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16` PTX can
   (that acc->Aregs identity is how FA2 avoids the round trip), and it would also remove 16 KB
   of the 144 KB per-key-block shared traffic.
2. **K/V f32->f16 staging (+7.4 ms), and it is REDUNDANT work.** `_B1_PASS_MAX`=1024 chunking
   re-stages all `n_keys` for every chunk: sum(n_keys) = 10240 keys staged per 4096-token prefill
   against 4096 distinct, i.e. 2.5x waste. Fix: a persistent f16 KV twin written incrementally by
   the fused RoPE+KV-write kernel (only the m new rows per chunk; +470 MB VRAM at max_ctx 8192).
   Separately, the staging kernel itself runs at ~170 GB/s = 11% of the 1555 GB/s peak because it
   is a scalar grid-stride loop with `long` indexing — vectorizing it is worth ~2-3 ms alone.
3. **bias+RoPE+KV-write (+4.6 ms).** The fused kernel moves ~40 MB/layer in 62.7 us = ~43% of
   bandwidth peak; TRT-LLM's does the same three jobs in 21.7 us.

### Integrity notes (anomalies diagnosed before reporting)
1. **The WMMA accumulator layout is opaque by contract and this kernel indexes it by row**, so it
   is VERIFIED ON DEVICE before the first launch (`tc_shim_fa_layout_probe`: A=I, B staged so
   acc[r][c] reads back r*16+c, plus a `store_matrix_sync` round-trip of the f16 accumulator;
   the buffer is zeroed first so a fragment carrying FEWER elements than assumed fails rather
   than passing by luck). A mismatch returns -310, the session prints DECLINED at staging time
   and keeps the five-pass chain. Every arm logged `ARMED | WMMA accumulator layout verified on
   device | BN = 64 | d_head = 128 | GQA g = 7`.
2. **fa_probe correctness, before any speed claim**: FA vs a HOST double-precision reference at
   all six raced shapes plus an odd (m=660, n_keys=1716, pos=1056) tail — max_abs <= 5.7e-4,
   rms <= 1.02e-4, ZERO elements with rel>2% and abs>1e-3, at BN 32/64/128. FA vs the shipped
   five-pass chain over ALL 3,670,016 output elements at m=n=1024: max_abs 7.6e-4, rms 4.4e-5,
   zero >2% outliers. A first GPU reference disagreed with the kernel; the reference's own Q
   layout was wrong, which is why the shipped reference is host-side double precision.
3. **Clocks: 1 Hz capture covers 01:26:23-01:57:01 only (1730 samples).** The main sweep
   (00:09-00:55) and the _d8 RAG cells (01:02-01:24) have the harness's per-cell bracketing
   reads instead (1410 -> 1410 MHz on every one of the 12 cells), not 1 Hz coverage — stated
   plainly rather than implied. Within the captured window 28/1730 samples (1.6%) fell below
   1410 MHz, min 1320 MHz, peak 424.2 W against a 400 W limit, max 62 C, in 15 windows confined
   to the SUSTAINED phases: the _d1 RAG-4096 run (01:29:35-01:31:28, up to 17.9% duty in the
   01:29 minute) and the _d8 nsys capture (01:45:06-01:45:24, 8 s). **The contested TRT-LLM
   re-race window (01:47-01:52) is 0.0% below 1410 MHz**, and one 1 s dip at 01:53:48 touched
   only the decode re-serve. Throttle therefore cannot explain the pp1024 flip in either
   direction, and the _d1 RAG number is if anything understated. Round 2's battery recorded the
   same VM behaviour under sustained C=50 (1290 MHz @ 411.9 W), so this is a property of the
   machine under high duty, not of either engine.
4. **Two of my own tools were wrong and were fixed rather than worked around.** (a) The flag
   audit's first version reported EVERY flag absent in EVERY arm: `grep -q` exits on the first
   match, `printf` then dies of SIGPIPE, and `set -o pipefail` turned the pipeline non-zero. An
   audit that fails toward "nothing is enabled" looks like a clean result, so the script now
   carries a positive control and aborts (exit 3) rather than reporting an empty flag set.
   (b) The nsys analyzer inherited from round 2 matched its window marker by kernel NAME; Mojo
   mangles kernels in kernels_prefill_gemma3.mojo to `residentk_kernels_prefill_gemma6A6A_<hash>`
   with no function symbol at all, so the BIASROPE arm found no window and silently decomposed
   nothing. It now matches on the launch GRID and refuses to attribute kernels when that grid is
   owned by more than one distinct kernel. The same analyzer's family roll-up also bucketed those
   Mojo kernels as cuBLAS GEMMs, because "gemm" is a substring of "ge**mm**a" — round 2's
   published family table therefore reported GEMM at 93.3% of the pp1024 prefill when the
   per-kernel table implies 77.9%. **The per-kernel tables round 2 reasoned from were correct;
   only its family roll-up was inflated, and no round-2 ratio was computed from it.**
5. **No fabricated cells.** Every number above is parsed from a named log under
   ~/trtllm/front3/ by summarize_front3.py; a missing cell yields null, never a guess. The TRT-LLM
   decode cell came from a SECOND re-serve because the first race was launched without --decode;
   both re-serves' pp1024 cells are reported rather than the more favourable one.
6. **Flag/banner audit** (the gemma-3-27b H200 lesson — that column was voided by a rebuild that
   silently dropped `-D ALGENTA_G3_STREAM`): session_cuda_p3 now prints one `TCFLAG <name>=1`
   line per numeric-path flag from inside that flag's own `@parameter if`, so the literal exists
   only in a binary that has the flag and `strings` is a positive audit. Verified differential:
   _c8 carries exactly the 8 round-2 flags and NONE of the three new ones; _d1 +PF_FA; _d2
   +PF_FASTEXP; _d3 +PF_BIASROPE; _d4 +PF_FA+PF_FASTEXP; _d8 all three. ~/trtllm/front3/
   flag_audit.json records sha256/size/mtime plus the per-arm runtime `TC FLAGS:` banner and the
   ARMED/DECLINED verdict.
7. **The committed source reproduces the gated numerics from a FRESH rebuild** (not the VM's
   pre-existing binary): _c8 rebuilt off this branch gives pp1024 13,218.5 tok/s = 77.469 ms
   against PR #983's 13,218.952 = 77.466 ms (**0.004% apart**), pp256 11,385.6 vs 11,376.6
   (0.08%), gen256 82.665 vs 82.850 (-0.22%), G0 16/16 and G1 64/64 PASS. RAG-4096 prompt0
   11,656.8 vs 11,619.1 (+0.32%).
8. **Engine-kernel inventory ratchet**: the five new published symbols took the contract from 170
   to 175 kernels (cuda 113 -> 118); `make inventory-check`, `docs-check` and both
   engine_kernel_* gates in scripts/audit_gap_checks.py were red until regenerated and are green
   now (29 checks, 0 gate failures).

### Refuted / not adopted
- **BN=128 key blocks**: 150.5 us/layer at pp1024 vs BN=64's 121.9 — its 102 KB of dynamic
  shared memory pins the kernel at one CTA/SM. Rejected.
- **BN=32**: ties BN=64 at pp1024 (121.9) and wins only the short partial tail block (m=660:
  151.6 vs 188.4, where 39 KB lifts occupancy to 3 CTAs and the grid fits one wave), but loses
  the chunked RAG shapes (297.0 vs 270.3 at n_keys=2048). Not worth a runtime switch. Rejected.
- **Passing the attention scale as a float through Mojo's `external_call`**: no repo-proven
  Float32/Float64 ARGUMENT marshalling (only a Float64 return, `strtod`), and an ABI mismatch
  would be a silent numeric bug rather than a crash. The scale travels as a device pointer
  instead — exact, one L2-resident 4-byte read per CTA.
- **A persistent f16 KV twin** (blocker 2's fix) was scoped but NOT built: ~470 MB of extra VRAM
  and a KV-layout change is a round of its own, and this round's budget was spent on the lever
  that actually flipped a cell.

### Ranked next levers for RAG-4096 (the only remaining loss), by measured ms
1. FA at long n_keys, +17.1 ms: `cp.async` K/V double-buffering, then raw mma.sync m16n8k16 PTX
   to drop the P shared round-trip. Target ~44% MFU = TRT-LLM parity = -17 ms.
2. Persistent f16 KV twin written incrementally, +7.4 ms: kills the 2.5x re-staging AND the
   scalar staging kernel. Target -7 ms. Bit-exact.
3. `_pf_biasropewrt_kernel` bandwidth, +4.6 ms: 43% -> 85% of peak. Target -3 ms.
4. rmsnorm rows, +0.9 ms.
Levers 1+2+3 = -27 ms against a +21.9 ms gap: RAG-4096 flips if 1 and 2 land.

## FRONT 4 — Qwen2.5-7B CUDA vs TensorRT-LLM 1.2.1, the RAG-4096 flip attempt
### algenta-ent-a100 (A100-SXM4-40GB, solo GPU), 2026-09-16 02:52-05:50 UTC, clocks pinned 1410 MHz
### branch feat/7b-rag-flip (stacked on feat/7b-fused-flash-attn / PR #989). LEDGER ONLY — not published.

**VERDICT: RAG-4096 DID NOT FLIP.** It improved 0.925x -> **0.9436x** against a TRT-LLM 1.2.1
re-served fresh in this session (13,968.6 -> 14,300.7 tok/s mean of the three token-exact prompts;
293.25 -> 286.42 ms against their same-session 270.276 ms). pp256 / pp1024 / decode were
**held**: pp256 is inside the baseline drift band, pp1024 +0.29%, decode invariant. Both levers
landed, both are gated, and the round-3 autopsy's own model of them (-24 ms) over-promised by
3.5x against the -6.83 ms of wall measured. What follows is the per-layer dissection of the
+16.14 ms that remains, not a restatement of the model.

### Levers (each its own build flag, default OFF; the `_d8` binary is byte-identical without them)
* `-D ALGENTA_7B_PF_FA2` — fused causal flash attention **v2**: cp.async 16-byte K/V double
  buffering (kb+1 in flight while kb computes, two block fences per key block instead of three)
  + raw `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f32.f16.f16.f32` so the f16 P tile is built **in
  registers** from the S accumulator (the m16n8k16 A layout and the m16n8 D layout put a lane's
  f16 k-pair at exactly the registers where its f32 k-pair already sits) — `sP` disappears, and
  because the O accumulator mapping is then ISA-specified rather than opaque the epilogue writes
  position-major f32 **straight to global**, so `sO` and its fence go too. Shared memory per CTA
  61.4 KB -> 8*BN*FA_LD, which is why **BN moves 64 -> 32** (three CTAs/SM, 155 registers):
  round 3's "32 is only better for a short tail block" was a fact about ITS footprint, and was
  re-measured here rather than inherited. 166 registers, 0 spills.
* `-D ALGENTA_7B_PF_KVTWIN` — persistent **per-layer** f16 K/V twin (+469.76 MB) staged only over
  the range it does not already hold, through `tc_shim_f32_to_f16_v8` (two float4 loads, one
  uint4 store per thread) instead of the scalar grid-stride converter at ~170 GB/s. The range's
  low-water mark is clamped to `pos` per chunk, so any position the prefill is about to rewrite is
  always re-staged and a decode step past the mark only widens the next range.

### Gates (BEFORE any speed claim; run inside every bench process and in the standalone probe)
| gate | result |
|---|---|
| FA2 on-device layout probe (`_fa2_layout_probe_kernel`: A/B/D fragment mappings + BOTH ldmatrix roles, exact integers, no tolerance) | **PASS** — "raw mma.sync m16n8k16 A/B/D + both ldmatrix roles verified on device" |
| G0 16/16 greedy vs the fp32 cache-free transformers oracle, every arm | **PASS** on _d8/_e1/_e2/_e3 |
| G1 64/64 self-consistency, every arm | **PASS** on _d8/_e1/_e2/_e3 |
| FA2 vs a HOST double-precision reference at all six raced shapes incl. the odd tail (m=660, n_keys=1716, pos=1056) | **PASS**, 0 elements over 2% rel at every bn |
| FA2 vs the shipped 5-pass chain, ALL 3,670,016 output elements | **max_abs 7.629e-04, rms 4.350e-05, 0 over 2% rel** — identical to round 3's FA |
| KVTWIN bit-exactness | `__floats2half2_rn` is the same round-to-nearest-even conversion `__float2half` performs; the f32 KV cache is write-once per position within a prefill |
| clocks | 1410 MHz read before AND after every cell (`clocks=1410 MHz->1410 MHz` on every arm line), 1 Hz sampler into `clocks_1hz.csv` |

Two bugs the probe caught before any speed claim, both recorded in the code that fixed them:
(1) the layout probe originally filled ONE matrix pattern for both B roles, so the transposed V
role reported MISMATCH against a **correct** kernel — with `V[k][n] = delta(n,0)*(k+1)` the true
`D[r][n>0]` is 0, not `(r+1)*(n+1)`; (2) `fa2_smem_bytes` counted `sizeof(__half)` twice, asked
for 278 KB at bn=128, and because one failed `cudaFuncSetAttribute` aborted the whole table that
single overflow declined EVERY bn with a bare `cudaErrorInvalidValue`. The attribute table now
records per-instantiation success so one shape that cannot fit declines only itself (-305). A
runtime-indexed `__half* bufK[2]` that ptxas pushed into a 32-byte local stack frame is now
pointer arithmetic (0 bytes stack frame, still 0 spills).

### Kernel-level A/B, standalone probe (median of 100 calls, 1410 MHz, GPU solo)
RAG-4096 FA block = the four chunk shapes summed x 28 layers, i.e. one 4096-token prefill:
| engine | pp256 | pp1024 | rag c1 | rag c2 | rag c3 | odd tail | **RAG block** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fa-r3` bn=64 (round 3's kernel) | 25.6 | 120.8 | 272.4 | 450.6 | 641.0 | 187.4 | **41.72 ms** |
| `fa2` bn=32 (**shipped**) | **24.6** | **104.4** | **247.8** | **375.8** | **475.1** | **131.1** | **33.63 ms (-8.09, 1.24x)** |
| `fa2` bn=64 | 25.6 | 114.7 | 249.9 | 393.2 | 539.6 | 183.3 | 36.36 ms (-5.36) |
| `fa2` bn=128 | 25.6 | 122.9 | 263.2 | 412.7 | 560.1 | 169.0 | 37.99 ms (-3.73) |
| `fa2-pshm` bn=32 (cp.async only, P still in shared) | 25.6 | 111.6 | 263.2 | 403.5 | 504.8 | 139.3 | 35.96 ms (-5.76) |

(us/layer for the shape columns.) **Sub-lever attribution:** at bn=64 raw-mma alone -5.16 ms and

that these two are NOT independent levers and must never be summed when forecasting.

### RAG-4096 (three token-exact 4096-token prompts, driver median of 20, G0 16/16 + G1 64/64 PASS)
| arm | prompt0 | prompt1 | prompt2 | mean tok/s | mean ms | vs `_d8` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_d8` (round 3's ship arm, rebuilt) | 13,970.6 | 13,968.3 | 13,967.0 | 13,968.6 | 293.25 | — |
| **`_e3` (+FA2 +KVTWIN)** | **14,305.9** | **14,301.3** | **14,295.0** | **14,300.7** | **286.42** | **+2.38%, -6.83 ms** |

rel-IQR 0.20-0.45%, 0 outliers, prompt-to-prompt spread 0.08%. The `_d8` re-measurement
reproduces round 3's stored 13,974.5 / 13,966.2 / 13,966.7 within **0.03%** in a clean window,
which is the evidence these cells were not throttled or contended.

**The model over-promised, and by how much.** Round 3's autopsy ranked the gap as FA +17.1 ms and
K/V staging +7.4 ms and concluded "levers 1+2 alone (-24 ms) exceed the +21.9 ms gap". Measured:
the FA lever delivered **-7.79 ms of GPU busy** (-8.09 ms in the standalone probe) of its modelled
-17.1, closing 44% of the FA gap — TRT-LLM's fmha_v2 stays ahead at 24.4 ms against our new
34.15 ms. The staging lever delivered **-1.33 ms of GPU busy** (the nsys dispatch counts below put
its whole ceiling at 2.270 ms, not 7.4 ms), and only **-0.6 ms of wall** on its own arm (`_e1`,
+0.21%). GPU busy fell 285.75 -> 276.04 ms (-9.71) while wall fell only 293.25 -> 286.42
(-6.83): **2.9 ms of the kernel saving did not reach the wall**, and that difference is the same
order as the host/launch gap this seam carries. The nsys rows below settle both numbers rather
than arguing them.

### Per-layer decomposition, ONE RAG-4096 prefill (nsys, 4 chunks x 28 layers, `PROMPT_IDS` = rag prompt 0)
Same capture recipe as round 3 (`--trace=cuda --cuda-graph-trace=node --sample=none
--cpuctxsw=none`), window marker matched on the RoPE+KV-write **launch grid** (32768 =
(h_q+h_kv)*m at m=1024) with ambiguous attribution refused, family roll-up NOT using the bare
substring "gemm" ("gemm" is a substring of "gemma", and Mojo mangles the
`kernels_prefill_gemma3.mojo` symbols to module-name-plus-hash). 112 rope+kvwrite rows = 28 per
execution x 4 chunks, so both captures are the same window by construction.

| kernel / family | `_d8` ms | `_e3` ms | Δ | n (`_d8` -> `_e3`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cuBLAS/cutlass projections (3 kernels) | 218.675 | 218.120 | -0.56 | 444 -> 444 |
| **fused flash attention** | **41.943** | **34.151** | **-7.79** | 112 -> 112 (`_fa_causal_kernel` -> `_fa2_causal_kernel`) |
| bias+RoPE+KV-write (fused, front 3) | 7.024 | 7.010 | -0.01 | 112 -> 112 |
| rmsnorm rows | 4.422 | 4.399 | -0.02 | 222 -> 222 |
| **f32->f16 convert, scalar** | **4.224** | **1.954** | **-2.27** | **335 -> 111** |
| **f32->f16 convert, v8 (8/thread)** | — | **0.936** | +0.94 | 0 -> **224** |
| SwiGLU (`__expf`, front 3) | 8.926 | 8.923 | -0.00 | 111 -> 111 |
| memset | 0.422 | 0.432 | +0.01 | 222 -> 222 |
| **GPU busy per RAG-4096 prefill** | **285.75** | **276.04** | **-9.71** | |

The FA delta measured in situ (**-7.79 ms**) cross-validates the standalone probe's **-8.09 ms**
to 3.7% — two independent harnesses, one number. **The dispatch counts are what settle lever 2:**
the scalar converter's 335 dispatches split 224 (K/V staging, 2 per layer per chunk) + 111 (the
per-GEMM A staging). Under KVTWIN exactly the 224 move to the v8 kernel and cost 0.936 ms, while
the 111 A-converts stay on the scalar path and cost 1.954 ms — unchanged, because KVTWIN does not
touch them. So the K/V staging was **4.224 - 1.954 = 2.270 ms**, not the 7.4 ms round 3
extrapolated from a pp1024 us/layer figure x 10 x 28: **that extrapolation was 3.3x too high**,
because the "f32->f16 convert" family was never all K/V. KVTWIN captured 1.334 ms of the 2.270 ms
that was actually there (59%), and 2.270 ms was the whole ceiling. This is the per-layer proof
that lever 2 could not have delivered its forecast on this hardware, independent of how well it
was implemented.

### Where the remaining +16.14 ms of RAG-4096 wall actually sits
`_e3` GPU busy 276.04 ms against TRT-LLM's same-session 270.28 ms wall. Round 3's modelled
TRT-LLM family totals, reused (they were not re-captured this round — no TRT-LLM nsys
counterpart, same limitation round 3 recorded):

| fused flash attention | 34.15 | 24.4 | **+9.75** |
| bias+RoPE+KV-write | 7.01 | 2.4 (fused `applyBiasRopeUpdateKVCacheV2`) | **+4.61** |
| f32->f16 converts (K/V 0.94 + per-GEMM A 1.95) | 2.89 | 0 (native bf16 KV and weights) | **+2.89** |
| rmsnorm | 4.40 | 3.4 | **+1.00** |
| SwiGLU | 8.92 | 9.2 | -0.28 |
| memset | 0.43 | — | +0.43 |
| **GPU busy** | **276.04** | ~272 | **+3.7** |
| **measured wall** | **286.42** | **270.28** | **+16.14** |

So after this round the kernel-level gap is only ~+3.7 ms and the projections win (-14.68 ms) very
nearly pays for the attention loss (+9.75 ms). The wall gap is larger than the busy gap by
286.42 - 276.04 = **10.38 ms of host/launch gap**. That figure is a cross-basis subtraction (busy
from a profiled `--runs 1` capture, wall from the 20-run bench median), so it is an order-of-
magnitude statement, not a measurement: round 3 measured the same quantity at 5.8 ms for `_c8`
(98.3% busy) and 7.5 ms for `_d8` here. Either way, **the host gap is now the same size as the
entire remaining kernel gap**, which was not true before this round.
