### Ranked next levers for RAG-4096, by measured ms (nothing here is forecast as a win)
1. **FA at long n_keys, +9.75 ms remaining.** Ours 34.15 ms = ~34% MFU against a ~11.5 ms
   arithmetic floor; TRT-LLM's fmha_v2 24.4 ms = ~47%. This round took us from ~26% to ~34%.
   Candidates, all **modelled and NOT measured**: heaviest-CTA-first grid ordering (448 CTAs
   against 324 slots at 3 CTAs/SM is 1.38 waves, and the CTAs are not equal — `qi=0` runs 1 key
   block, `qi=15` runs 128 — so the tail is not free); a per-warp `kb_max` so the upper warps skip
   key blocks that are fully above their own diagonal (must guard the mma work, not the loop, or
   the block barrier deadlocks); and the O-rescale, which is 64 f32 multiplies per warp per key
   block and is amortized over only 32 key columns at BN=32.
2. **bias+RoPE+KV-write, +4.61 ms.** Untouched this round (lever 3, not attempted — budget).
   62.6 us/layer for ~40 MB = 43% of peak against TRT-LLM's fused 21.7 us. The grid is
   (h_q+h_kv)*m blocks of `d_head`=128 threads, each reading one strided 512-byte slice.
3. **f32->f16 converts, +2.89 ms.** The structural price of an f32 KV cache and f32 activations
   against a native-bf16 engine. KVTWIN took the K/V half to 0.936 ms; the other 1.954 ms is
   per-GEMM A staging, which F16NORM already removed for 2 of the 4 projection roles.
4. **rmsnorm, +1.00 ms.**
5. **Host/launch gap, ~7-10 ms** — now the same order as the entire remaining kernel gap.

Levers 1-4 sum to +18.25 ms of gap against a -14.68 ms projection win. **Closing RAG-4096 needs
the FA gap roughly halved again AND bias+RoPE+KV-write fused to TRT-LLM's width**; neither is a
parameter tweak, and this round is the evidence that the round-3 forecast method (extrapolating a
pp1024 us/layer figure by the key-count ratio, and rolling families up) overstates what is
available by 2-3x. Measure the family at the raced shape before ranking it.

## FRONT 5 — Qwen2.5-7B CUDA vs TensorRT-LLM 1.2.1, the second RAG-4096 flip attempt (2026-09-16, algenta-ent-a100)

Same VM, same protocol as FRONT 4. **RAG-4096 improved 0.9434x -> 0.9556x and is STILL A LOSS.**
Ledger-only per the wins-only rule: no gitbook page, nothing published, no ratio promoted.

Mission was to flip RAG-4096 to >=1.0x (needed -16.14 ms of wall) without regressing the three
wins. One of round 4's four ranked levers landed (lever 2, bias+RoPE+KV-write, worth -3.705 ms);
lever 1 (attention) was attacked twice and **both attacks are refuted with numbers**; levers 3-5
were not reached. The gap is 12.639 ms, so the flip did not happen and is not claimed.

### Arms
| arm | definition |
|---|---|
| `_e3` | FRONT 4's SHIP ARM, **rebuilt fresh from this branch**: `_d8` + `7B_PF_KVTWIN` + `7B_PF_FA2`. The baseline; never a remembered number. |
| `_f1` | `_e3` + `ALGENTA_7B_PF_ROPEVEC` — lever 2, the vectorized barrier-free bias+RoPE+KV-write |

`ALGENTA_7B_PF_ROPEVEC` defaults OFF, so `_e3` is byte-for-byte round 4's adopted binary. The
flag audit confirms it at both levels: `_e3`'s literal set stops at `7B_PF_KVTWIN` and its banner
reads `ROPEVEC = False`; `_f1` carries `7B_PF_ROPEVEC` and reads `ROPEVEC = True`.

### Baseline reproduction (the check that makes the rest quotable)
`_e3` rebuilt here against FRONT 4's published `_e3`:

| cell | FRONT 4 `_e3` | FRONT 5 `_e3` (this round) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| RAG-4096 | 14,305.9 tok/s = 286.32 ms; **0.9436x** | 14,197.1 = 288.510 ms; **0.9434x** | -0.76% tok/s, **+0.02% on the ratio** |
| pp1024 | 15,330.8; 1.0690x | 15,219.6 / 15,316.7; 1.0692x / 1.0760x | -0.73% / -0.09% |
| pp256 | 12,778.7; 1.7443x | 12,748.2 / 12,696.3; 1.7674x / 1.7602x | -0.24% / -0.64% |

The RAG ratio reproduces to 0.02% against a TRT-LLM cell that itself moved +0.70% this session.
Every gate ran inside every process: **G0 PASS 16/16** (greedy vs the fp32 cache-free transformers
oracle) and **G1 PASS 64/64** on all five driver runs, `_e3` and `_f1` alike.

### The G0 oracle had to be REGENERATED, and reproduced the historical record
`/tmp` was wiped twice this round (a spot **preemption** at ~14:0xZ terminated the instance
mid-build, and the lifecycle stop that followed). `~/trtllm/front3/f3_setup_v3.sh` — the setup
entry the round carries — **does not exist on this VM** (only `~/f4_setup.sh`, which assumes a
`~/front4_src.tgz` tarball). Setup was reconstructed by hand: the `/tmp/w7b/ckpt` symlink to
`~/trtllm/w7b_ckpt` (57 GB), and the oracle via `~/a2a/run_oracle.sh` ->
`ref_transformers_cpu.py` (HF **fp32 CPU**, `--n-tokens 16`). It is deterministic and it
reproduced the 2026-08-26 `oracle.log` **byte-for-byte on all six prompts** (fixture + chat_0..4),
e.g. chat_2 -> `"Whispering waves kiss,\nMoonlit surface sighs soft,\nNight's e"`. The gate is
therefore the same gate, not a re-baselined one.

### Lever 2 — ADOPTED: vectorized, barrier-free bias+RoPE+KV-write (-3.705 ms on RAG-4096)
`_pf_biasropewrt_vec_kernel` (`-D ALGENTA_7B_PF_ROPEVEC`). Round 4 measured this family at
62.6 us/layer for ~40 MB = ~43% of the 1555 GB/s roof against TRT-LLM's fused
`applyBiasRopeUpdateKVCacheV2` at 21.7 us, and left it "not attempted — budget". Its traffic
floor is 25.7 us, so ~37 us/layer was the kernel's *shape*, not bandwidth. Three changes:

1. **32,768 one-head-per-block launches -> 1,024 one-row-per-block launches** (`grid_dim = m`,
   `block_dim = 256`).
2. **Every global access to float4** via `loadvec._ld4` and a new `_st4` (the store twin lever 0
   never needed). This is the micro-autopsy's finding applied to the store side: without
   `alignment=16`, `width=4` lowers to four scalar `st.global.b32`.
3. **The shared-memory staging and the barrier are gone.** The scalar kernel gives thread `e`
   element `e`, but RoPE pairs `e` with `e+64`, so it staged all 128 elements into `xs` and
   barriered to let thread `e<64` read both halves. That staging is load-bearing only when a q/k
   norm runs (its sum-of-squares reduction needs every element in shared anyway). Qwen2.5-7B has
   **no** q/k norm, so `xs` existed purely to move a value 64 lanes sideways — and the thread
   that needs both halves can load both halves.

**PTX-level proof the lever did what it claims** (`strings <binary> | grep -oE '…global…'`, the
lever-0 audit method):

| binary | `ld.global.v4.b32` | `st.global.v4.b32` |
|---|---|---|
| `_e3` | 38 | **0** |
| `_f1` | **46** | **3** |

The baseline had *zero* vector stores in the entire binary; `_f1` has them, and they are the
RoPE/KV writes.

**Declines, never fakes.** The session keeps `_pf_biasropewrt_kernel` when `qk_norm != 0` (a norm
genuinely needs the staging), `d_head != 128`, or any row stride is not a multiple of 4 elements —
so the 16-byte alignment promise `_ld4`/`_st4` make is discharged by the caller, not assumed.
Qwen3 (no qkv bias) and gemma are untouched: the flag inherits `PF_BIASROPE`'s gate and replaces
that kernel's dispatch slot only.

### Lever 1 — REFUTED TWICE, with numbers. The FA gap is not a parameter.
Round 4 ranked attention first (+9.75 ms: ours 34.15 ms at ~34% MFU, TRT-LLM's single
`fmha_v2_flash_attention_bf16_64_128_S_qkv_128_causal_sm80` at 24.4 ms / ~44%) and noted its own
BN sweep was flat to inverted (32 -> 33.7, 64 -> 36.4, 128 -> 38.0 ms). A sweep that gets *worse*
as the tile gets bigger is the signature of a limit BN cannot touch, so the limit was derived
rather than guessed. The per-chunk ladder from `fa_probe` (A100, 1410 MHz, median of 30):

| chunk | us/layer | GFLOP | TFLOPS | MFU | KV traffic/launch | arithmetic intensity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pp1024 | 106.5 | 7.52 | 70.6 | 22.6% | 117.6 MB | **64.0 F/B** |
| rag chunk1 | 246.8 | 22.56 | 91.4 | 29.3% | 352.4 MB | **64.0 F/B** |
| rag chunk2 | 376.8 | 37.59 | 99.8 | 32.0% | 587.3 MB | **64.0 F/B** |
| rag chunk3 | 475.1 | 52.62 | 110.8 | 35.5% | 822.2 MB | **64.0 F/B** |

**Arithmetic intensity is exactly 64.0 FLOP/byte at every shape and is independent of BN** — an
FA2 CTA covers `FA_BM`=64 query rows of ONE query head, so per key it moves 128 dims x 2 (K and V)
x 2 bytes = 512 B to do 64 rows x 512 FLOP. BN scales traffic and FLOPs together, which is
*precisely* why round 4's BN sweep was flat. Against the A100's L2<->SM balance point of
~312/4 = 78 F/B, 64 < 78 says memory bound, and chunk3 streams **822 MB per layer-launch for an
8.39 MB unique K/V working set — a 98x amplification**, 7/8 of it the same bytes re-read by the
seven query heads sharing one kv head (h_q=28, h_kv=4, g=7).

**Attack A — GQA packing (`_fa3_causal_kernel`), REFUTED.** One CTA covers `BMQ` query rows for
ALL g=7 heads of one kv head, so K/V is fetched once per (row-block, kv-head). Intensity 64 -> 112
F/B at BMQ=16, 224 at BMQ=32 — over the balance point. It is **CORRECT**: the new on-device
`_fa3_layout_probe_kernel` passes (it pins the *hand-built* m16n8k16 A fragment, which FA2's probe
cannot cover because FA2 gets A from `ldmatrix`), and it matches the host **double-precision**
reference at all six raced shapes including the odd tail (m=660, n_keys=1716, pos=1056) with
**0 of 3,670,016 elements over 2% rel** — the same rms (4.350e-05) FA2 bn=32 reports. And it is
**SLOWER at all six configurations** (`fa_probe --iters 30`, RAG-4096 FA block = 4 chunks x 28
layers, one binary, `RESULT: PASS`):

| engine | config | RAG-4096 FA block |
|---|---|---|
| `fa2` bn=32 | **the shipped kernel** | **33.604 ms** |
| `fa3-16n1` | BN=64 BMQ=16 minB=1 | 35.381 ms (**+5.3%**) |
| `fa3-16b2` | BN=32 BMQ=16 minB=2 | 40.399 ms |
| `fa3-16b1` | BN=32 BMQ=16 minB=1 | 40.542 ms |
| `fa3-16n2` | BN=64 BMQ=16 minB=2 | 42.951 ms |
| `fa3-32n1` | BN=64 BMQ=32 minB=1 | 46.764 ms |
| `fa3-32b1` | BN=32 BMQ=32 minB=1 | 52.584 ms |

**Why the model was wrong, and what that proves.** Cutting L2 traffic 7x bought nothing, so L2
bandwidth was *not* the binding constraint. Packing does not reduce **per-warp** shared-memory
traffic at all: every warp still `ldmatrix`es its own copy of the same K/V tile, and the
ldmatrix:mma ratio is 0.5:1 at *any* BN (S phase 8 k-steps x BN/16 loads against BN mma; PV phase
BN/16 x 8 against BN/16 x 16) — so packing left the real limit untouched while cutting occupancy
from 12 warps/SM to 7 (224 threads x 155 regs = 1 CTA/SM). `fa3` also correctly **DECLINES**
(`-313`, too few CTAs to fill 108 SMs) at pp256 and at the odd tail for BMQ=32, which is why it
would have needed per-shape dispatch anyway. It stays in the tree behind
`tc_shim_fa3_causal_async` with `fa_probe`'s `fa3-*` engines so the refutation is reproducible,
and is **not wired into the session** — no arm carries it.

**Attack B — occupancy, REFUTED.** If 12 warps/SM is the limit, more warps should help. BN=32
uses 34.8 KB of shared memory, so 4 CTAs/SM (139 KB of 164 KB) is affordable *if* registers fit:
`__launch_bounds__(128, 4)` got ptxas to 128 registers (24 B of spills) = 4 CTAs/SM = 16 warps.

| arm | regs | CTAs/SM | warps/SM | RAG-4096 FA block |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fa2-mb3` (minBlocks=3) | 158 | 3 | 12 | **34.234 ms** |
| `fa2-mb4` (minBlocks=4) | 128 | 4 | 16 | 36.930 ms (**+7.9%**) |

**More occupancy is slower.** This arm was **REVERTED, not merely disabled**, because of a defect
it exposed: `__launch_bounds__(128)` and `__launch_bounds__(128, 1)` are *not* the same hint to
ptxas. Adding the parameter with a `MINB = 1` default moved the shipped `_fa2_causal_kernel<32,1,1>`
from **155 to 171 registers** — 3 CTAs/SM down to 2 — and cost **+9.8%** (33.89 -> 37.22 ms) in a
kernel whose source had not otherwise changed. A "neutral default" template parameter silently
regressed the adopted arm; the parameter is gone and FA2 is **verified back at 155 registers,
0 spills**. Recorded because it is a trap: any future arm that parameterizes FA2's launch bounds
must re-check the default's register count, not assume it.

**Where that leaves the +9.75 ms.** Three independent levers are now measured negative on A100:
BN (round 4), L2 traffic via GQA packing, and occupancy. What is left is the structure: at
ldmatrix:mma = 0.5:1 the shared-memory stream and the tensor cores are co-limiting (12 warps x 32
`ldmatrix.x4` x 512 B / 128 B-per-clk = 1536 clocks, against 12 x 64 mma x 4096 FLOP / 2048
FLOP-per-clk = 1536 clocks — equal), and between the two mma phases of *every* key block sits a
serial mask -> max -> exp -> sum -> warp-shuffle -> P-pack segment with no tensor work in it.
sm_80 has no `wgmma` and no TMA, so the cross-warpgroup ping-pong that hides that segment on
Hopper is not available; hiding it on A100 needs deep multi-stage software pipelining across key
blocks, which costs shared memory this kernel does not have at 3 CTAs/SM — and trading occupancy
for larger tiles is exactly what BN=64/128 and Attack B both measured as worse. **That is the
per-layer argument that the FA gap is not closable by parameter change on this GPU with this
kernel structure**; closing it means a from-scratch deep-pipelined fmha, which is a kernel project
rather than a lever, and it was not started this round.

### Not reached this round
Lever 3 (host/launch gap, ~7-10 ms — now the largest single un-attacked number, and zero numeric
risk), lever 4 (f32->f16 converts, +2.89 ms) and lever 5 (rmsnorm, +1.00 ms). Budget. Note the
gap ledger has moved: after lever 2 the remaining 12.639 ms is ~+9.75 ms attention (argued above
as structural), ~+6 ms host gap, and ~+3.9 ms converts+rmsnorm+memset, against the -14.68 ms
projection win that is already in the numbers. **The host gap is now the best remaining
expected-value target**, not attention.

## FRONT 6 — Qwen2.5-7B CUDA vs TensorRT-LLM 1.2.1, RAG-4096 **FLIPPED** 0.9556x → 1.0221x (2026-09-16, algenta-ent-a100)

Third attempt at the RAG-4096 loss, and the first one that wins it. Branch
`feat/7b-rag-next2` (stacked on `feat/7b-rag-next` / PR #996, which was still OPEN when this
round started, so `_g0` is round 5's ship arm and not `origin/main`). VM `algenta-ent-a100`,
A100-SXM4-40GB, clocks pinned 1410 MHz and read before and after every timed cell with a 1 Hz
sampler over each stage.

**The round's premise was wrong, and measuring it is what won the cell.** Round 5 ranked the
remaining 12.639 ms as (1) a ~6-10 ms HOST/LAUNCH GAP — "zero numeric risk, best expected
value" — (2) ~2.9 ms of converts plus ~1.0 ms of rmsnorm, (3) do not touch FA. Target (1) does
not exist at that size, and the real 12.6 ms was sitting in a place no previous round had
priced: **the prefill pass shape**.

### 1. Target 1 REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT — the host gap is 3.144 ms, not 6-10 ms

`front6_decomp.py` over a fresh `_g0` capture (nsys `--trace=cuda`, one RAG-4096 prefill, wall
and busy taken from the SAME trace so the gap is a measurement and not a cross-basis
subtraction). Windows are cut on evidence, not guessed: the four per-chunk embedding gathers
(`residentk_kernels_prefill_f32..._6fbdda6b`, 4/prefill) open a window and the prefill's own
lm_head (`..._lmh..._9f8e6b01`, exactly 1/prefill) plus the following argmax close it.

| prefill # | wall ms | busy ms | gap ms | gap % | dev ops | host launch APIs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (cold) | 661.117 | 277.312 | 383.804 | 58.05 | 1580 | 1580 |
| 1 | 284.097 | 280.953 | **3.144** | **1.11** | 1580 | 1581 |
| 2 | 282.771 | 279.610 | 3.161 | 1.12 | 1580 | 1581 |
| 3 | 282.996 | 279.949 | 3.048 | 1.08 | 1580 | 1581 |
| 4 | 286.373 | 283.347 | 3.026 | 1.06 | 1580 | 1581 |
| 5 | 286.448 | 283.403 | 3.045 | 1.06 | 1580 | 1581 |
| 6 | 283.568 | 280.322 | 3.246 | 1.14 | 1580 | 1581 |

The six warm prefills agree to ±0.11 ms: **the gap is 3.026-3.246 ms, 1.06-1.14% of wall**.
Round 5's "~276 ms of GPU busy" was round 4's number for `_e3`, stale by ROPEVEC's own
−3.705 ms; against the correct 280.953 ms the gap is 3.1 ms and not 8.8 ms.

Where the 3.144 ms is: 1515 uniform 1-5 µs gaps totalling 2.597 ms (82.6%) — pure per-launch
cost over 1580 launches — plus 8 gaps of 20-100 µs totalling 0.467 ms (14.9%), which are the
three chunk seams (74.14 / 73.73 / 56.86 µs of H2D→first-kernel, behind a 91.87 / 55.46 /
54.66 µs D2H→H2D pair: the per-chunk token upload and the `ctx.synchronize()` that brackets it)
and three rmsnorm→cutlass gaps. Per chunk the gap is 0.787 / 0.761 / 0.731 / 0.660 ms.

**So the entire host-side prize is ~3.1 ms, of which a CUDA graph could recover at most the
2.597 ms of per-launch gaps** — and it would have to do that against 1580 launches whose mean
GPU-idle cost is 1.65 µs. Round 3 refuted prefill graphs at pp1024 on a 98.8%-busy profile; this
round RE-MEASURED at RAG-4096 as instructed rather than inheriting, and the refutation stands at
98.9% busy. Target 1 is not the best expected-value attack in the round; it is the third.

The cold first prefill is recorded because it is the number that would have misled a shorter
capture: 383.804 ms of gap, 58% of a 661.117 ms wall, from per-shape cuBLAS first-call cost
(the same lazy per-shape module selection that PR #993 root-caused on the gemma lane). The
driver's 3 warmup + 20 measured runs never see it, which is why the median window is the one
reported and why a `--runs 1` capture must be read per-window, not in aggregate.

### 2. Where the 12.639 ms actually was: 80.46% of a 280.953 ms busy is cuBLAS, and the pass shape was wasting it

Per-family GPU busy inside the median RAG-4096 prefill window (`_g0`, same capture):

| family | ms | % | n | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cublas_gemm | 226.048 | 80.46 | 448 | the four projections × 28 layers × 4 chunks |
| fa2_flash | 34.710 | 12.35 | 112 | `_fa2_causal_kernel<32,1,1>`, 309.92 µs mean |
| swiglu | 8.984 | 3.20 | 112 | `_swiglu_f16_fastexp_kernel` |
| rmsnorm | 4.527 | 1.61 | 224 | 20.21 µs mean |
| biasrope | 2.541 | 0.90 | 112 | round 5's `_pf_biasropewrt_vec_kernel` |
| A_convert_scalar | 2.014 | 0.72 | 112 | `_f32_to_f16_kernel`, 17.98 µs mean |
| kv_stage_v8 | 0.822 | 0.29 | 224 | `_f32_to_f16_v8_kernel`, 3.67 µs mean |
| lm_head | 0.713 | 0.25 | 1 | |
| memset | 0.431 | 0.15 | 224 | |
| embed | 0.143 | 0.05 | 4 | |
| **total** | **280.953** | | 1580 | union busy == naive sum: no stream overlap at all |

Two facts fall out. First, **112 `_f32_to_f16_kernel` dispatches** — round 4's "111 per-GEMM A
converts" — are exactly one per layer-chunk, and source inspection says which: under
F16NORM+F16MLP the rmsnorm f16 twin feeds qkv and gate/up, the SwiGLU epilogue feeds down, and
**o_proj is the one role whose A is still f32** (FA2's O epilogue writes `pf_attn` f32). Second,
at 476.33 GFLOP per layer-chunk the 2018.28 µs of cuBLAS is 236.0 TF/s = 75.6% of the A100's
312 TF/s dense f16 peak, and attributed by launch geometry the loss is not spread evenly:

| role | shape (M=1024) | µs | TF/s | % of 312 peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gate_up | N=37888 K=3584, C f16 | 1053.00 | 263.5 | 84.5 |
| qkv | N=4608 K=3584, C f32 | 142.59 | 237.2 | 76.0 |
| down | N=3584 K=18944, C f32 β=1 | 680.10 | 204.0 | 65.4 |
| o_proj | N=3584 K=3584, C f32 β=1 | 142.59 | 184.5 | 59.1 |

Against TensorRT-LLM's own pp1024 kernel mix (`~/trtllm/front1/trtllm_kernel_mix.txt`, 12
requests, the same m=1024 shapes RAG chunks use), the whole non-attention gap decomposes as:
cuBLAS **+6.09 ms**, A converts **+2.01**, rmsnorm **+1.05** (4.527 vs their FusedAddRMSNorm
3.480), KV converts **+0.82**, memset +0.21, biasrope +0.11, SwiGLU −0.21, lm_head −0.05, their
`computeSeqAndPaddingOffsets` −0.64 and torch eltwise −0.32 — net **+8.94 ms of non-attention
device work and +2.98 ms of attention-plus-host-gap**, which sums to the 11.92 ms in-trace wall
gap. **Nothing in that list is worth 12.6 ms on its own.** The win came from a term the
decomposition could not show, because it was invisible in a per-chunk comparison: our per-chunk
GEMM shape is the wrong shape.

### 3. LEVER 1 (adopted, `-D ALGENTA_PF_PASS4096`): one 4096-row pass instead of four 1024-row passes

`_B1_PASS_MAX` has been 1024 since the H100-autopsy lever that introduced it, and a RAG-4096
prompt has therefore always run its projections as four m=1024 passes. Nobody had priced that,
because every round compared kernels against TRT-LLM's per-request totals instead of asking
whether our pass shape was the efficient one. `gemm_probe --msweep` prices the same 1905.3 GFLOP
of per-layer projection work three ways (median of 15, clocks 1410, the exact dtypes and beta of
each role):

| m | passes | per-layer µs | 4096-row µs | 28-layer ms | vs 4×1024 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 4 | 1937.41 | 7749.63 | 216.990 | — (shipped) |
| 2048 | 2 | 3649.54 | 7299.07 | 204.374 | **−12.616 ms** |
| 4096 | 1 | 7326.72 | 7326.72 | 205.148 | **−11.842 ms** |

The mechanism is tail-wave quantization, the same effect the H100 autopsy named for 128-row
chunks: at m=1024 the narrow-N roles tile into 8×28 = 224 output tiles of 128×128 = **2.07 waves
on 108 SMs**, so a third of the machine idles through the second wave. Per role, m=1024 → 4096
raises o_proj 188.9 → 199.9 TF/s and down 212.8 → 244.2, while gate/up (already 278.8, 89% of
roof) barely moves. Total attention work is unchanged — Σ over rows of visible keys is
1024×(512+1536+2560+3584) = 1024×8192 either way — so this is free on the FA side, and it also
deletes three chunk seams, ¾ of the launches (1580 → ~400) and ¾ of the memsets.

The flag raises `_B1_PASS_MAX` to 4096; every `pf_*`/`tc_*` scratch buffer is sized by
`_B1_PF_ROWS`, which derives from it, so the sizing follows by construction rather than by a
second edit. Costs, stated: **+5.6 GB of VRAM** at the 7B shapes (2.8 GB of it `pf_tc_scores` +
`pf_tc_p16`, the five-pass chain's windows, which FA2 leaves dead but which must still be sized
because that chain is FA2's runtime decline path) — measured peak 31.9 GB of 40 GB — and it is
**NOT bit-identical**, because a different M re-selects the cuBLAS algorithm and so the reduction
order. `m = min(n_prompt, cap)`, so **pp256 and pp1024 cannot change**: both are ≤ 1024 and take
the identical single pass at the identical M.

### 4. LEVER 2 (adopted, `-D ALGENTA_7B_PF_LTALGO`): cublasLt on a stage-time timed-search algorithm

`tc_shim_init` calls `cublasCreate` + `cublasSetStream` + `cublasSetMathMode` and **never
`cublasSetWorkspace`**, and every integration entry dispatches `cublasGemmEx` with
`CUBLAS_GEMM_DEFAULT` — which re-runs its heuristic on all 448 calls and, without a workspace,
cannot reach split-K. The lever adds a cublasLt path whose algorithm is chosen once, at stage
time, by TIMING the top-16 heuristics per shape (not taking result[0]: the probe's winners were
not always index 0) and caching it. Only shapes that were tuned take it; an untuned shape returns
**−320 and the caller declines to the shipped GemmEx entry**, so a prompt whose first pass is not
the tuned one runs byte-for-byte the code it ran before. In situ it tuned 4/4 in 892 ms one-time
and picked exactly the probe's winners:

| role | probe µs | in-situ tuned µs | algo |
|---|---|---|---|
| qkv | 510.98 | 511.9 | id=6 tile=20 stages=11 splitK=1 |
| gate_up | 3875.84 | 3924.4 | id=6 tile=20 stages=11 splitK=1 |
| o_proj | 425.98 | 425.4 | id=6 tile=20 stages=11 splitK=1 |
| down | 1963.01 | 1965.1 | id=6 tile=20 stages=11 **splitK=2** |

The two levers **compound**: at m=1024 the same search is worth only −36.35 µs/layer (−4.07 ms
per prefill), at m=4096 it is worth −550.9 µs/layer (−15.43 ms), because the wide pass is what
exposes the tail-wave headroom a better algorithm can then take.

### 6. Where the −18.597 ms came from, measured and not forecast

`front6_decomp.py` on a fresh `_g2` capture, same recipe and same windowing as `_g0`'s, both
recomputed with one analyzer version. `_g0`'s re-decomposition reproduces its original numbers
exactly (284.097 / 280.953 / 3.144), which is the check that the windowing change did not move
the baseline it is being compared against.

| | `_g0` (4 passes) | `_g2` (1 pass) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| device ops per prefill | 1580 | **367** | −1213 (−76.8%) |
| host launch APIs | 1581 | 368 | −1213 |
| chunk seams | 3 × ~200 µs | **0** | −0.60 ms |
| GPU busy (median window) | 280.953 ms | **260.967 ms** | **−19.986 ms** |
| host/launch gap | 3.144 ms (1.11%) | **1.367 ms (0.52%)**; 0.580-0.593 ms steady | −1.777 ms |
| trace wall | 284.097 ms | 262.334 ms | −21.763 ms |

Per family, the busy delta:

| family | `_g0` ms (n) | `_g2` ms (n) | Δ ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| cublas_gemm | 226.048 (448) | **209.947 (112)** | **−16.101** |
| fa2_flash | 34.710 (112) | **30.133 (28)** | **−4.577** |
| memset | 0.431 (224) | 0.060 (28) | −0.371 |
| kv_stage_v8 | 0.822 (224) | 0.636 (56) | −0.186 |
| rmsnorm | 4.527 (224) | 4.497 (56) | −0.030 |
| embed | 0.143 (4) | 0.127 (1) | −0.016 |
| lm_head | 0.713 (1) | 0.720 (1) | +0.007 |
| A_convert_scalar | 2.014 (112) | 2.344 (28) | +0.330 |
| swiglu | 8.984 (112) | 9.439 (28) | +0.455 |
| biasrope | 2.541 (112) | 3.056 (28) | +0.515 |

**The unforecast win is attention: FA2 −4.577 ms (−13.2%).** Per launch it goes 309.92 µs at
m=1024 → 1076.17 µs at m=4096 for exactly 4× the work. Nothing in the kernel changed; the grid
does. At m=1024 FA2 launches 16 row-blocks × 28 heads = 448 CTAs whose causal work is wildly
unequal (round 4 measured row-block 0 running 1 key block and row-block 15 running 128), so
448 CTAs over 108 SMs at 3 CTAs/SM = 324 slots is 1.38 waves and the tail is the heaviest CTA.
At m=4096 the same imbalance is spread over 64 row-blocks = 1792 CTAs = 5.5 waves, and the tail
amortizes. Round 5's instruction "do not touch FA parameters" was right — this win needed no FA
change at all, only a wider pass, and it is a reason to re-read round 4's FA load-balance
analysis as wave-quantization-limited rather than kernel-limited.

The three families that got *slower* per element (swiglu +0.455, biasrope +0.515, A convert
+0.330) are all round-5-shaped kernels whose grids were tuned at m=1024 — `_pf_biasropewrt_vec_kernel`
goes 22.69 → 109.13 µs for 4× the rows (−4.0% efficiency), swiglu 80.22 → 337.10 µs (−5.3%),
the scalar A converter 17.98 → 83.72 µs (−16.7%, and it is now only 28 calls so its total is
2.344 ms). Together they give back 1.30 ms of the 21.29 ms the other families saved.

### 5b. Flag audit — the two levers are shape/algorithm changes, so the literal alone is not enough

`scripts/audit_tc_flags.sh --bin-dir ~/front6/bin --logs ~/trtllm/front6` (`flag_audit.json`).
Neither FRONT 6 lever adds a kernel, so the inventory does not move and `strings` on a kernel name
would prove nothing: PASS4096 changes a comptime SHAPE and LTALGO changes which cuBLAS algorithm a
shape dispatches. For both, **the flag literal can be present while the effect is absent** — a pass
cap no prompt exceeds, or an Lt arm whose four shapes all declined (−320) and ran `cublasGemmEx`
DEFAULT anyway while still printing the flag line. The audit therefore records the runtime effect
alongside the literal, read from the log rather than the binary:

| arm | sha256[0:16] | bytes | flags in binary (beyond the round-5 set) | `pass_max` | `pass_max_4096` | `lt_tuned_4_of_4` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_g0` | c4f3024205778b0b | 2169976 | — | 1024 | **False** | **False** |
| `_g1` | e250396024fa9588 | 2174128 | `PF_PASS4096` | 4096 | **True** | False |
| `_g2` | f470fd370c2bedbf | 2189984 | `PF_PASS4096` `7B_PF_LTALGO` | 4096 | **True** | **True** |

All three carry the identical round-5 flag set (`ONEPASS_B1 FLASH_B1 FLASH2_B1 NOSEAM TCATTN SM1P
F16NORM F16MLP FA FASTEXP BIASROPE FA2 KVTWIN ROPEVEC`), `FA2_variant = 0`, `max_ctx = 8192`, and
the FA/FA2 ARMED verdicts, so the only differences between the arms are the two levers under test.
`lt_tuned_4_of_4` reads the LTALGO TCFLAG line rather than the `TC FLAGS:` banner on purpose: the
banner is printed unconditionally, and calling `_tc_lt_count()` from it would make every flag-off
build reference a cublasLt symbol and fail to link against the stock shim object. The audit's first
run got this wrong and reported `lt_tuned_4_of_4=False` for `_g2` — an arm that had verifiably
tuned 4/4 — because it searched the banner; a field that reads False for a working lever is worse
than no field, so it is fixed rather than dropped.

The shim-object separation behind those binaries is verified, not asserted. The stock object
(`-D ALGENTA_TC_SHIM_LT` absent) against the object FRONT 5 actually shipped
(`~/front5/bin/tc_shim_sm_80.o`): **`.text`, `.rodata`, `.data` and `.bss` all byte-identical**
(`.text` md5 `eefd876c0bfc9642e28d3769a983acce`, 26922 bytes both) and the **defined symbol tables
identical at 157 entries**, with 0 undefined `cublasLt*` and 0 defined `tc_shim_lt*`. The LT
object has 5 defined `tc_shim_lt*`/`*_pre_lt` and 11 undefined `cublasLt*`. A whole-file md5 of
the two stock objects does NOT match, and the reason is worth keeping: an ELF object embeds its own
source path in an `STT_FILE` symbol, and the two builds used different paths of identical length
(`front5`/`front6`), so a whole-file compare reports a difference that is not a code difference.
Section-wise comparison is the correct test.

### 7. Integrity notes — the uncomfortable findings, carried not buried

1. **ZERO-DRIFT IS BREACHED, and the affected cells were NOT re-taken.** The 1 Hz samplers show
   203/4814 off-pin samples in stage 1 (4.22%) and 11/1147 in stage 2 (0.96%), against round 5's
   10/1377. Off-pin samples land inside **14 cell windows** (11 in stage 1, 3 in stage 2). Clocks
   reach **1230 MHz** (−12.8% from the 1410 pin) at 19:36:12, 67 °C, 391.2 W, 37192 MiB. This is
   **power-cap throttling, not thermal and not another actor**: the cap is 400.00 W and the
   sampler records draws up to **532.9 W**, while the maximum temperature all stage is 75 °C
   (A100 throttles well above that), and `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` was empty before every
   cell. Off-pin values are 1230-1395 MHz, i.e. a contiguous band below the pin rather than a
   single spike, exactly round 3's "1.6% samples <1410 (min 1320, 424 W vs 400 W limit) confined
   to sustained phases".
   **Why the cells were not re-taken:** 14 cells × ~7.5 min is ~105 min against a hard report
   budget that had ~85 min left, and re-taking under the same sustained-load conditions would
   reproduce the same throttle — it is a property of a 400 W-capped A100 running a 4096-row
   prefill, not of a contaminated window. **What bounds the effect instead, and this is the
   load-bearing argument:** the cells are interleaved with the baseline bracketing them, and the
   baseline reproduces to **0.044%** across the three RAG prompts (14326.400 / 14325.080 /
   14331.438, taken 19:26 / 19:50 / 20:04, each window containing off-pin samples), to 0.534% on
   pp256 across three independent cells in two rounds, and to 0.105% on pp1024. The claimed
   effect is **+6.958%** — 13× the largest baseline spread and 158× the RAG baseline spread. Every
   cell also carries rel-IQR ≤ 0.65% with **0 outliers** at the driver's 10% deviation threshold,
   which a throttle excursion inside the 20 timed runs would have inflated. `_g2`'s IQRs
   (0.579 / 0.648 / 0.466%) are marginally above `_g0`'s (0.347 / 0.290 / 0.411%) and that is
   disclosed rather than averaged away. A re-take under a lower power cap, or with the runs
   interleaved at finer granularity, is the clean way to close this and is the first thing the
   next round should do if the margin is ever load-bearing on <1%.
2. **The probes OVER-forecast, again, and by a factor worth remembering.** `gemm_probe --msweep`
   put PASS4096 at −11.842 ms of GEMM and LTALGO at a further −15.43 ms, i.e. −27.27 ms together;
   the measured cublas family delta is **−16.101 ms**. Two separate errors, both in the same
   direction. (a) The probe under-models in-situ memory pressure: its isolated `ex_ws0` 4×1024
   total is 216.990 ms against nsys's 226.048 ms for the same 448 calls (+4.2%), and its
   `lt` 1×4096 total 189.723 ms against nsys's 209.947 ms (**+10.7%**) — the wider pass reads
   4× the activations per kernel and runs beside FA2's K/V traffic, which an isolated GEMM loop
   does not see. (b) LTALGO's in-situ algos are the probe's winners to within 1.3% in isolation
   (511.9 vs 510.98 µs, 3924.4 vs 3875.84, 425.4 vs 425.98, 1965.1 vs 1963.01) yet deliver only
   −3.604 ms of wall rather than −15.43, because at m=4096 `cublasGemmEx DEFAULT` in situ already
   lands near the tuned choice — the probe's `ex_ws0` baseline was measured on a **fresh handle
   per shape**, which is not the state the engine runs in. **Lesson, and it is round 4's KVTWIN
   lesson a third time: a standalone probe ranks levers, it does not price them.** Both times the
   ranking was right and the magnitude was 1.7-4.3× too large.
3. **VRAM is now the binding constraint on this lever, and it is close to the edge.** Peak device
   memory in the `_g2` cells is **37192 MiB of 40960 MiB (90.8%)**, against 31940 MiB for
   `_g0`/`_g1`. PASS4096 adds ~5.6 GB of scratch (2.8 GB of it `pf_tc_scores` + `pf_tc_p16`,
   which FA2 leaves dead but which must be sized because that chain is FA2's decline path) and
   cublasLt's internal per-algorithm buffers add more on top of the 64 MB workspace. On a 24 GB
   card this arm demotes the whole TC plan (the existing headroom try prints a record and
   `tc_staged = -1`) rather than failing, but it would then run the JIT-dequant chain and be far
   slower — so **PASS4096 is a 40 GB-class lever as shipped**. Sizing the five-pass chain's
   windows against the pass cap rather than `max_ctx` would recover ~2.8 GB and is the obvious
   next cleanup if this ever has to run on a smaller device.
4. **The RAG-4096 cell had never been oracle-gated, in any round.** Rounds 2-5 raced it on G1
   self-consistency alone, which cannot detect a lever that is deterministically WRONG, and this
   round's lever 1 only activates above 1024 rows so the fixture oracle says nothing about it.
   Fixed by `--cases rag` + the driver comparing `min(len(oracle), G0_TOKENS)`. All arms now pass
   **G0 5/5 on all three raced prompts** and are token-identical to each other.
5. **The first version of that gate produced a false FAIL on a correct engine**, and it is worth
   keeping because it is a trap with no visible symptom. Forcing the reference to 16 tokens with
   `min_new_tokens` does not merely decode past EOS — it sets the EOS logit to −inf, so at the
   step where EOS *is* the argmax the reference picks a different token. All three arms, including
   the untouched round-5 baseline, then read "G0 FAIL — 16 mismatched" against a reference that
   was wrong and they were right. `--no-eos-stop` (`eos_token_id=None`) reproduces the engine
   exactly. **A gate that fails every arm including the baseline is a gate defect until proven
   otherwise.**
6. **The dissection that drove this round nearly did not happen correctly.** The first analyzer
   run clustered the timeline on 2 ms idle gaps and picked "the largest contiguous burst", which
   returned an 8663 ms window spanning the whole decode tail and reported a 23.645 ms gap — a
   number that would have *confirmed* round 5's ranking and sent the round after CUDA graphs. It
   was wrong because Mojo kernel names are mangled (`residentk_kernels_prefill_f32..._6fbdda6b`,
   not `embed`), so the marker search silently matched nothing and fell back to the burst
   heuristic. Markers are now named from the captured kernel table and the window count is
   asserted against the expected 7 prefills. A second defect: windowing on "the last 4 embeds"
   is correct only while the pass cap is 1024 — under PASS4096 it built 3100 ms windows spanning
   four prefills and their decode tails, which is how the first `_g2` decomposition reported a
   12.111 ms gap and a 1410 ms "other" family. The chunk count is now derived from the trace.
7. **`front6_summarize.py` shipped with a PEP-701 multi-line f-string** that the local python 3.13
   accepts and the VM's python 3.10 rejects with "unterminated string literal", so the post stage
   produced no summary table on its first pass. Analyzers that only ever run on the measurement
   host must be parsed there, not locally.
8. **Not re-measured this round:** TRT-LLM's own RAG-4096 nsys trace, so their family split is
   still inferred by scaling round 2's pp1024 kernel mix (`~/trtllm/front1/trtllm_kernel_mix.txt`)
   ×4 for the non-attention families — legitimate because those shapes are per-chunk identical,
   but their FMHA is not, and the residual "+2.98 ms of attention-plus-host-gap" is the one term
   in the decomposition that rests on that extrapolation. TRT-LLM decode was not re-served either;
   our gen256 82.635-82.700 is quoted against round 3's stored 79.04 and is **CROSS-SESSION**.
   `_g1`'s RAG prompts 1 and 2 were not run (budget) — `_g2` covers all three.

### 8. Next round's targets, ranked with measured ms

The remaining gap to a *comfortable* RAG-4096 win, and what is left on the other axes, all from
this round's `_g2` decomposition (260.967 ms busy, 1.367 ms gap):

1. **The three m=1024-shaped elementwise kernels, +1.30 ms and free.** swiglu (9.439 ms, 337.10 µs
   at grid.x=10), biasrope (3.056 ms, 109.13 µs at grid.x=4096) and the scalar A converter
   (2.344 ms, 83.72 µs at grid.x=57344) all lost 4-17% of their efficiency when the pass widened,
   because their grids and vector widths were chosen at m=1024. Re-tuning them for m=4096 is
   arithmetic-free and bit-exact.
2. **Kill the o_proj A convert outright, −2.344 ms.** It is the last f32 A operand in the layer
   (FA2's O epilogue writes `pf_attn` f32) and the only reason 28 `_f32_to_f16_kernel` calls
   remain. Making FA2's epilogue write an f16 O twin and feeding o_proj `_tc_gemm_f16_32c_pre`
   is **bit-exact by the same argument round 4 used for KVTWIN** — `__float2half` of the same f32
   accumulator is the identical RN-even value whether the kernel or a converter computes it — and
   it also removes 28 launches and halves the epilogue's write traffic (58.7 → 29.4 MB per layer).
   This was priced in round 4's decomposition as the 111-convert term and has never been taken.
3. **The cublas family is still 80.45% of busy at 258.4 TF/s (gate/up) and ~236 TF/s aggregate** —
   75.6% of roof. The gap between the probe's 287 TF/s and the in-situ 258 is memory pressure,
   not algorithm choice, so the next increment is a wider workspace plus a per-shape search run
   *in situ* rather than in isolation (this round's error #2), or fusing the SwiGLU into the
   gate/up epilogue via a cublasLt `CUBLASLT_EPILOGUE_*`/custom epilogue so the 9.439 ms swiglu
   pass and its 155 MB round trip disappear.
4. **rmsnorm, +1.017 ms vs TRT-LLM's FusedAddRMSNorm** (4.497 ms over 56 calls = 80.31 µs each
   against their 15.4 µs at m=1024 scaled). They fuse the residual add into the norm; we do the
   add in the GEMM's beta=1 and the norm separately. A fused add+norm writing the f16 twin would
   also remove traffic from the busiest buffer in the layer.
5. **The host gap is now 1.367 ms (0.52%) and 0.580-0.593 ms steady.** CUDA graphs remain
   refuted — twice measured now, at pp1024 and at RAG-4096 — and after PASS4096 there is less
   than 0.6 ms of steady-state gap left to recover. **Do not spend a round here.**
6. **FA2 at 31.1% MFU (30.133 ms) is still the second-largest family** and round 5's structural
   argument stands (arithmetic intensity exactly 64 FLOP/byte against an A100 L2↔SM balance of
   ~78, 98× read amplification, no wgmma/TMA on sm_80). But this round's −13.2% came from wave
   quantization, not from the kernel, so the load-balance question is not closed: at 5.5 waves
   the tail is smaller but not gone, and a heaviest-CTA-first grid ordering is now cheaper to test
   than it was at 1.38 waves.

### branch feat/gemma-fused-tc-attn, based on main @ 4c5f097a6 (post-#993). LEDGER + the two flipped cells; nothing published to gitbook by this front.

Round 4 left pp256 a WIN (37.541 vs 41.297 ms = 1.1001x, published in #995) and two losses:
pp1024 121.473 vs 110.710 = 0.9114x (gap +10.76 ms) and RAG-4096 542.702 vs 425.954 = 0.7849x
(gap +116.75 ms). This round flips **both**, and makes the already-won pp256 stronger. The
bracketing baseline is PR #993's own build rebuilt from this branch (`R5_base`), and it reproduces
the standing column: 121.261–121.429 ms measured against 121.473 stored (+0.04%), 37.455–37.479
against 37.541, 542.096–542.891 against 542.702. That is what makes every delta below attributable
to the levers and not to the tree.

### FINAL STANDINGS — `R5_all2`, the full round-5 stack (post-restart session, TRT-LLM re-served 17:09Z)

| cell | PR #993 (`R5_base`) | round 5 (`R5_all2`) | delta | TRT-LLM 1.2.1 | #993 ratio | **round-5 ratio** |

### The five levers (each its own build flag, default OFF; `R5_base` is byte-identical without them)

| arm | sha256_16 | flags on top of PR #993 | numerics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R5_base` | `a4b7d8cc6219efdb` | — (PR #993) | the shipped path |
| `R5_fa` | `9839f26323a2cb04` | `G3_PF_FA` | online softmax reorders the sum → own gate |
| `R5_mlp` | `a789839b99c8a2d2` | `G3_PF_F16NORM` + `_F16MLP` | F16NORM bit-identical; F16MLP rounds the gate/up C at the GEMM epilogue → own gate |
| `R5_all` | `c02fa6607c9a05f1` | + `_F16ATTN` (all four) | bit-identical given FA |
| `R5_all2` | `fc357d9b92d184eb` | all four + `G3_PF_ROPE2` | **bit-identical** (arithmetic proof in the kernel docstring) |

**1. `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_FA` — one fused WINDOWED WMMA FlashAttention-2 kernel**
(`_fa_g3_window_kernel` in `tc_shim.cu`) replacing the five-pass TC chain: the head-major Q pack,
the strided-batched QK^T GemmEx, the masked softmax, the strided-batched PV GemmEx, the head-major
O unpack, **and** the per-layer f32→f16 K/V staging. QK^T and PV are `wmma::mma_sync` m16n16k16
f16 HMMA with an f32 accumulator — tensor-core by construction. This is NOT the SIMT fused-flash
twin (`_pf_attn_window_flash_kernel`), which is a measured 2x REGRESSION at pp1024 and stays in the
tree only as the negative control.

Three things gemma-3 needs that the 7B lane's `_fa_causal_kernel` (#991) does not have:

* **A sliding window as a KEY-BLOCK RANGE.** 52 of gemma-3-27b's 62 layers are local with
  `sliding_window=1024`. The five-pass chain computes the FULL dense `[g*m, n_keys]` QK^T and then
  throws everything outside the window away in `_attn_softmax_mask_kernel` — at RAG-4096 a local
  layer pays for 4096 keys to keep 1024. Here `kb_min` derives from the CTA's first query row's
  lower bound (`lo` is monotone in `qpos`, so the CTA's first row has its smallest `lo`, and a block
  below `kb_min` is outside the window for every row that CTA owns and is never loaded); the
  per-element predicate runs only on blocks that straddle a boundary. The predicate itself is
  `_attn_softmax_mask_kernel`'s verbatim. Local-layer attention stops scaling with `n_keys` past
  `window + FA_BM`.
* **Native f32 K/V.** The resident cache is f32, so the chain stages it to f16 first: 6 bytes of
  global traffic per K/V element per layer (4 read + 2 write) before the GEMM reads 2 more. The
  fused kernel converts in-register on the way into shared memory — 4 bytes per element, no staging
  launch, identical `__float2half` rounding point. `kv32=0` keeps the staged route as a control arm.
* **Optional f16 O** so o_proj can take its A pre-staged (lever 4).

The WMMA accumulator element layout is documented as OPAQUE and this kernel indexes it by row for
the mask, the O rescale and the final divide, so `tc_shim_fa_layout_probe()` verifies the mapping
ON DEVICE before the first launch; a disagreement returns −310, the session prints DECLINED once at
`seal()` and keeps the five-pass chain, so a declined lever can never masquerade as a measured
fused-attention number. −301/−304/−305/−310 fall back; ANY OTHER status is returned as a real
launch failure, so a CUDA error is never laundered into a slower-but-green benchmark cell.

**2. `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_F16NORM`** — both per-layer rmsnorms write an f16 `pf_xn16` and the qkv and
gate/up GEMMs take it pre-staged. BIT-IDENTICAL: the same f32 arithmetic rounded once at the store,
exactly where the shim's `_f32_to_f16_kernel` would have rounded the same value one launch later.

**3. `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_F16MLP`** — the gate/up GEMM writes its `[m, 2*d_ff]` C as f16, the new
`_pf_geglu_rows_f16_kernel` combines that into an f16 `pf_act16`, and down_proj takes it directly.
At m=1024, d_ff=21504 the layer's largest non-GEMM traffic term goes 176 MB C written + 176 read +
88 act written + 88 read + 44 f16 A written → 88 + 88 + 44 + 44. The GeGLU expression is the f32
twin's verbatim, so the down A is bit-identical; the only numeric change is where the gate/up C
rounds. `nvjet_hss_*` → `nvjet_hsh_*` in the traces is cuBLAS's own confirmation.

**4. `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_F16ATTN`** — the fused kernel writes f16 O and o_proj takes it pre-staged.
Inherits FA's whole gate: the f16 O is that kernel's `of16=1` instantiation, so without FA there is
no producer for the buffer.

**5. `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_ROPE2`** — `_pf_ropewrt_warps_kernel`, one WARP per head instead of one
BLOCK per head. The twin launches `(h_q+h_kv)*m` = 49,152 blocks of 128 threads per 1024-row tile,
one element per thread, with a seven-step SHARED-MEMORY reduction tree carrying a `barrier()` at
every step: 344,064 block-wide barriers per layer per tile to move 67 MB, and 12.2 million block
launches over a RAG-4096 prefill. The replacement is 6,144 blocks (8x fewer), zero `barrier()`,
zero shared memory, five `shuffle_xor` steps. BIT-IDENTICAL, and the proof is arithmetic rather
than a tolerance: lane `t` owns elements {t, t+32, t+64, t+96}, which makes the twin's stride-64
and stride-32 reduction steps **intra-lane in its exact association** and its stride-16..1 steps
five xor-shuffles over the same operand pairs; `inv`, `x = v*inv*g` and the rotation are the twin's
expressions verbatim.

**Why two new shim entries exist (a seam trap).** The pre-staged-A entries #991 added
(`tc_shim_gemm_f16_32c_pre` / `_16c_pre`) honour `g_noseam`, which only `-D ALGENTA_TC_NOSEAM`
sets. The gemma-3 lane gets its zero-sync ordering from a DIFFERENT switch: `-D ALGENTA_G3_STREAM`
binds cuBLAS to the legacy stream and leaves `g_noseam == 0`. Dispatching `_pre` from this build
would have put a `cudaStreamSynchronize(legacy)` back at every one of the 248 projection seams of a
62-layer prefill — the exact per-GEMM sync the stream-ordered lever exists to delete, charged to
the number the lever is supposed to improve. `tc_shim_gemm_f16_{32c,16c}_pre_async` are the
identical GemmEx with no sync path at all.

### REFUTATION: `_f32_to_f16_kernel`'s 8.682 ms at pp1024 was NOT KV-cache staging

Round 4's named lever charged all 8.682 ms to "f32→f16 KV staging … NOT weight conversion", on the
evidence that its instance count scales with tiles (373 at pp256, 1489 at RAG-4096). The counts are
right; the attribution is not. That one kernel is SHARED — it is also the shim's per-call f32→f16
**A-operand** conversion for all four projection GEMMs and the lm_head:

```
373 launches for one pp1024 prefill = 4 seams x 62 layers (248) + K and V x 62 (124) + 1 lm_head
1489 for one rag4096 prefill        = 4 tiles x 372 + 1
```

and by ELEMENTS per layer (m=1024, d_model=5376, n_q=4096, d_ff=21504, h_kv=16, d_head=128,
n_keys=1024):

| caller | elements/layer | share | of the 8.682 ms |
|---|---|---|---|
| down_proj A (`m*d_ff`) | 22,020,096 | 53.0% | 4.60 ms |
| qkv A + gate/up A (`2*m*d_model`) | 11,010,048 | 26.5% | 2.30 ms |
| o_proj A (`m*n_q`) | 4,194,304 | 10.1% | 0.88 ms |
| **K + V staging (`2*n_keys*h_kv*d`)** | **4,194,304** | **10.1%** | **0.88 ms** |
| total | 41,518,752 | 100% | 8.68 ms |

So "make KV natively f16" was worth ~0.88 ms at pp1024, not 8.68 ms, and the named lever's real
total was **+15.4 ms, not +18.20 ms** (softmax 9.429 + Q pack/O unpack 5.099 + KV staging 0.88).
That still flips pp1024 — but it does NOT flip RAG-4096, which is why this round also built the
pre-staged-A chain that deletes the other 89.9%.

**The model is confirmed twice, by count and by measured time.** By COUNT: the traces are
whole-process, so they include PR #993's four seal()-time priming prefills (tile rows
128/256/512/1024 = 249+373+373+373 = 1368 launches), and on that basis every trace reconciles
exactly —

| trace | predicted | observed | |
|---|---|---|---|
| R5_base pp1024 | 1368 + 373 = 1741 | **1741** | MATCH |
| R5_base rag4096 | 1368 + 4×372 + 1 = 2857 | **2857** | MATCH |
| R5_fa pp1024 | 1741 − 4×124 = 1245 | **1245** | MATCH |
| R5_mlp pp1024 | 1741 − 3×62×5 = 811 | **811** | MATCH |
| R5_all pp1024 / rag4096 | 5 lm_head + 62 o_proj = 67 | **67 / 67** | MATCH |

6/6 exact. The 62 that survive in `R5_all` are themselves a prediction and they confirm the
dispatch gates: they are the o_proj A stagings of the m=128 priming prefill, where the fused
attention declines at `m < _G3_PF_FA_MIN_M = 256`, the SIMT kernel writes f32 `pf_attn`, and o_proj
falls back to the staging ladder. `R5_mlp` keeps o_proj's staging for the same structural reason —
`_F16ATTN` is the fused kernel's f16 O and that arm has no fused kernel. By MEASURED TIME:
`R5_base` → `R5_fa` at pp1024 moves the bucket 25.692 ms / 1741 launches → 22.599 ms / 1245, i.e.
**3.093 ms for exactly the 496 removed KV launches**; the timed pp1024 prefill contributes 124 of
those at the largest `n_keys`, so its share is ≈0.8–0.9 ms — the byte-share model's 0.88 ms, within
13%, from an independent measurement.

### Per-kernel decomposition (nsys, whole-process GPU busy, clocks 1410 MHz)

| bucket | R5_base pp1024 | R5_all pp1024 | R5_base rag4096 | R5_all rag4096 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gemm_projection | 239.945 ms | 226.688 | 497.196 | 447.607 |
| mojo_per_layer | 59.756 | 53.467 | 105.374 | 89.509 |
| attention (5-pass `_attn_softmax_mask_kernel`) | 23.304 / 248 | — | 84.274 / 434 | — |
| fused_tc_attention (`_fa_g3_window_kernel`) | — | 28.462 / 248 | — | 86.379 / 434 |
| f32_f16_convert | 25.692 / 1741 | **0.191 / 67** | 57.531 / 2857 | **0.192 / 67** |
| rope_bias_kv | 18.540 / 310 | 18.536 / 310 | 37.573 / 496 | 37.558 / 496 |
| norms | 8.420 / 625 | 0.057 / 5² | 14.656 / 997 | 0.057 / 5² |
| **GPU busy total** | **375.657** | **327.407** | **796.604** | **661.306** |

² Not a disappearance — a re-bucketing. Under `_F16NORM` the producer is
`_pf_rmsnorm_rows_f16_kernel`, which lives in `kernels_prefill_gemma3`, so Mojo mangles it into the
`residentk_kernels_prefill_gemma*` family and it lands in `mojo_per_layer`. Reading the norms row as
"−8.4 ms" would be wrong; the honest reading is that the f32 rmsnorm symbol is gone because the
kernel that replaced it is named differently.

`gemm_projection` falls 49.6 ms at rag4096 with **no change to the projection math**, for two
reasons the traces support: the gate/up C is now f16 (`nvjet_hss` → `nvjet_hsh`), halving the
widest epilogue write in the layer, and the strided-batched QK^T/PV GemmEx moved into the fused
kernel and out of this bucket. `rope_bias_kv` is identical to three decimals between the two arms —
which is precisely what ranked ROPE2 as the fifth lever, and what made it the one that flipped
rag4096.

### Oracle gates — BEFORE any speed claim, on every arm measured

`gate_any.py` against the cache-free fp32 transformers oracle in `~/adj/oracle3`, one process per
cell, watchdog-wrapped, clocks read before and after every cell. `R5_all` was gated TWICE (once
before and once after an instance stop/start, against a regenerated checkpoint) and `R5_all2` once;
all three produced identical verdicts:

```
prompt     max_new verdict                        note
pp256           16 16/16 PASS                     n_gen=16 det=n/a (single run)
pp256           64 64/64 PASS                     n_gen=64 det=2/2 bit-identical
pp1024          16 16/16 PASS                     n_gen=16 det=n/a (single run)
pp1024          64 64/64 PASS                     n_gen=64 det=2/2 bit-identical
val550          16 16/16 PASS                     n_gen=16 det=n/a (single run)
val550          64 64/64 PASS                     n_gen=64 det=2/2 bit-identical
rag4096         64 22/22 + EOS-stop PASS          n_gen=22 det=n/a (single run)

GATE ALL_PASS = True
```

RAG-4096 is the load-bearing cell for the WINDOW: it is the only gated prompt whose tiles make the
window bind (4 tiles → n_keys 1024/2048/3072/4096 against `sliding_window=1024`, so tiles 2–4
exercise `kb_min > 0` on all 52 local layers), and it stops at the oracle's own EOS at 22 tokens.
`val550` (m=550 < window) and pp256/pp1024 (n_keys ≤ window) exercise the causal path, and 10 of
62 layers are global (`window <= 0`) at every shape.

### Element-wise verification of the windowed kernel

`fa_g3_probe.cu` compares `_fa_g3_window_kernel` against a HOST DOUBLE-PRECISION windowed reference
over the same rounded operands the kernel sees (Q pre-scaled and rounded to f16 where the kernel
rounds it, K/V rounded to f16 where the kernel rounds them, P rounded to f16 where both round it),
at twelve shapes — pp256, pp1024, the four RAG-4096 tiles as local AND global layers, plus an odd
`m%64 / n_keys%64 / pos_base%64 != 0` tail — across all four `(kv32, of16)` combinations:

```
[1] WMMA accumulator-layout probe: VERIFIED ON DEVICE (status 0)
48/48 rows PASS, max_abs <= 1.6e-4, max_rel <= 7.1e-3, rms <= 7.0e-6, >2%rel count 0
=== fa_g3_probe: 0 FAIL(s) ===
```

`kv32=1` and `kv32=0` produce **identical** max_abs and rms at every one of the twelve shapes,
which is the direct element-wise proof that the in-register f32→f16 K/V conversion matches the
staged path bit for bit — the claim the native-f16-KV lever rests on.

The first run of this probe reported 4 of 12 shapes as gross failures (`max_rel` exactly 1.000,
rms ~0.39, ~half the sampled cells) on the `kv32=1 of16=0` arm ONLY, while the `kv32=0` arm of the
same shape writing to the SAME buffer agreed to 1.5e-5. Same math, two instantiations, agreeing at
eight shapes and disagreeing at four — a harness race, not a kernel defect: the kernel launches on
the shim's own `cudaStreamNonBlocking` stream, which is not ordered against the legacy stream the
two output-zeroing `cudaMemset`s were issued on, so the memsets could land after the kernel had
written and zero whole output rows, which reads back exactly as "the kernel returned zeros". Fixed
with a device sync between the zeroing and the launch; the session cannot hit this because it
launches the kernel and its consumer on the SAME shim stream. The probe's metric was wrong too — it
divided by `fmax(1e-6, |want|)`, and an attention output legitimately lands within 1e-5 of zero, so
a 1e-5 absolute disagreement (exactly the f16-P rounding level this kernel is designed to sit at)
read as a 100%+ relative error. 44 of the 48 original "FAIL" rows were the reference's zero
crossings, not the kernel.

### How rag4096 flipped: the remainder was one untouched bucket

After four levers rag4096 sat at 0.9694x, 13.465 ms short. The decomposition named the remainder
without ambiguity: `rope_bias_kv` was 37.573 ms in `R5_base` and 37.558 ms in `R5_all` — identical
to three decimals, 496 launches in both — while round 4 had already ranked that bucket +25.355 ms
behind TRT-LLM's single `applyBiasRopeUpdateKVCacheV2`. One bit-identical kernel rewrite against
it returned −19.419 ms, more than the 13.465 ms gap, and flipped the cell to 1.0135x. The lesson
recorded here is the method: the flip came from reading which bucket the first four levers did NOT
move, not from estimating which would be biggest.

Cumulative rag4096: **542.096 ms (#993) → 440.231 (four levers, −101.865) → 421.085 ms (+ROPE2,
−19.419) = −121.011 ms, −22.3%, 0.7873x → 1.0135x.**

### Integrity notes (anomalies diagnosed before reporting, including five of my own tools being wrong)

* **The flag banners were unauditable in the arm that needed them most.** The first cut put all
  four `TCFLAG ALGENTA_G3_*` prints inside `_arm_fused_fa()`, which only compiles under
  `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_FA` — so `R5_mlp`, the arm measuring `_F16NORM` + `_F16MLP` WITHOUT the
  attention lever, carried **zero** flag literals. The `strings` count caught it before any cell
  was measured (`R5_mlp: 0 literals`, expected 2). They now live in `_print_round5_flag_audit()`,
  called unconditionally for the family, with `G3 FLAGS: TCATTN =` as the gemma-3 positive control.
* **This round's battery reproduced the SIGPIPE/pipefail failure mode `scripts/audit_tc_flags.sh`
  exists to prevent.** `strings -a "$bin" | grep -q -F "<control>"` exits on the first match,
  `strings` dies of SIGPIPE, `set -o pipefail` turns the pipeline non-zero, and EVERY arm read as
  carrying no positive control — an audit failing in the "nothing is enabled" direction, which looks
  like a clean result. The guard rail was already written down in the repo and the bug happened
  anyway, in new code, one directory over. Both now use a bash string match.
* **A quiescence check that can only be satisfied by a process that is not us has to exclude us.**
  The first cut carried its own script name in its busy-pattern, `pgrep -f` matched the running
  script on every poll, `clean` never reached 2, and the smoke stage sat in `sleep 15` for ten
  minutes with the GPUs at 0 MiB reporting nothing. Fixed by walking pgrep's PIDs and skipping `$$`
  and `$PPID`.
* **The summariser asserted "same-session" for a comparator it had not checked.** A stale
  `trtllm_*.json` left in the runs directory satisfies the glob just as happily as the current
  chain's own re-serve, and this round's cells straddle an instance stop/start. The label now
  carries the file mtime — which is how the ROPE2 A/B's comparator is visibly the 17:09Z re-serve
  copied into its own measurement tree, not a fresh one. Likewise the within-1% reproduction check
  is suppressed when no re-serve exists, because comparing the stored column against itself printed
  "+0.000% reproduces within 1%" for a session in which TRT-LLM was never served.
* **The decomposition's instance-count prediction was on the wrong basis** and so printed MISMATCH
  against a correct measurement (per-prefill vs whole-process, the difference being PR #993's four
  priming prefills). Fixed; 6/6 traces now reconcile exactly. Its geometry table also only knew the
  1024-row tile, so the priming launches (grid 4096×128 = the SIMT attention at m=128, 43008×256
  and 21504×256 = GeGLU at m=512 and m=256) landed in UNATTRIBUTED — reported, not guessed, which
  is the intended behaviour, and now attributed.
* **The probe harness raced and the probe metric lied** — both diagnosed above rather than worked
  around, and both fixed in the shipped file.
* **`tc_shim.cu` needs a GENERATED header.** It `#include`s `tc_rt_ptx.h` (embedded PTX from
  `tc_rt_kernels.cu`), so a bare `nvcc` on a fresh box dies at the last step of a long chain. It
  only ever worked before because an older run had left the header in the `-I` directory — which an
  instance restart wipes. `build_shim_gemma3_round5.sh` now generates it; the rebuilt object is the
  same 962,728 bytes the measured arms linked.
* **The all-masked-prefix case in the windowed online softmax, and why it is safe.** With
  `window > 0`, a warp whose rows have a larger `lo` than the CTA's first row can see its FIRST key
  block entirely outside the window. Every element then masks to −1e30, `t = NEG`,
  `n = max(m, t) = NEG` and `p = __expf(NEG − NEG) = 1`, so that block contributes 64 spurious unit
  weights to `l` and a spurious `V` sum to `O`. It cannot survive: the first block that does contain
  a valid key gives a real maximum, and the FA2 rescale `alpha = __expf(NEG − real) = 0` multiplies
  both the spurious `O` and the spurious `l` away exactly. No block is all-masked for every warp
  (the diagonal block always contains each row's own key), so a real block always arrives. Written
  down because it is the one place the window interacts with the online softmax non-obviously, and
  the probe's windowed shapes are what prove it empirically.
* **Fixture provenance after the restart.** The checkpoint and all four prompt fixtures were
  regenerated from the deterministic generator; `check_fixtures_gemma3_round5.py` proves they are
  token-identical to the gated ones before the chain is allowed to measure. The first cut of that
  check was an inline heredoc inside a triple-nested ssh quote: the python never ran, the marker
  never appeared, and the chain fail-closed on a check that had not executed. Right failure
  direction, wrong tool.
* Clocks: 1410 MHz read before AND after every cell, re-pinned on drift, 1 Hz sampler during every
  cell. Zero off-pin samples in any of the three brackets.
* Resident serve discipline: TRT-LLM was served ONLY inside its own chain stage and stopped
  immediately after its three cells; every other cell is a one-shot driver process. The box was
  verified at 0 MiB on all 8 GPUs with no watchers and no containers, then the instance was
  STOPPED — the VM is off by default and is only started to measure.

### Ranked next levers (all three raced cells are wins; these are margin, not gaps)

1. **Fused-attention long-`n_keys` efficiency.** `fused_tc_attention` is 86.379 ms whole-process at
   rag4096 over 434 launches and 28.462 ms at pp1024 over 248 — now the largest non-GEMM bucket
   this round ships. Only the 10 global layers still scan the full cache (the 52 local ones are
   window-bounded), so the 7B ledger's ranked lever applies with less headroom but unchanged shape:
   `cp.async` K/V double-buffering, then raw `mma.sync` m16n8k16 PTX to drop the P shared
   round-trip, targeting ~44% MFU.
2. **The per-layer residual/norm passes.** `_pf_norm_accum_rows_kernel` runs twice per layer over
   `[m, d_model]` f32 (read branch + read hidden + write hidden = 66 MB per call, ~33 GB per
   rag4096 prefill). Vectorising it is bandwidth-only and safe; making `pf_branch` f16 is a
   numerics decision on the residual path and is NOT proposed here.
3. **`_G3_PF_FA_MIN_M` and `_G3_PF_FA_BN` are untuned.** The crossover is inherited from the
   five-pass chain's measured 256 so this round's A/B moved one thing at a time, and BN=64 is
   inherited from the 7B lane. The shim implements BN 32/64/128 and both K/V routes; a sweep is
   cheap now that the probe verifies each combination element-wise.
4. **Publication.** pp256 (1.2931x), pp1024 (1.1038x) and rag4096 (1.0135x) are all wins and are
   candidates for `gitbook/benchmarks/nvidia-llm-throughput.md`. Per the publish-wins-only rule and
   this front's brief, nothing was published to gitbook here; that is a top-level decision.

### The levers (all build flags, default OFF; flag-off builds byte-unmodified)

1. `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_FA2` — `_fa_g3_window2_kernel`: #994's 7B FA2 techniques ported onto
   round 5's windowed WMMA kernel (the round's ranked target #1; round 5's decomposition named
   `fused_tc_attention` the largest non-GEMM bucket, 86.379 ms whole-process at rag4096).
   (a) the f16 P tile's A-fragment is packed IN REGISTERS via raw
   `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f32.f16.f16.f32` — the m16n8k16 A layout and the m16n8
   D layout put a lane's k-pair at the same registers, so `sP`, its shared round trip and one
   of the three per-key-block fences disappear; (b) the O epilogue writes position-major
   STRAIGHT TO GLOBAL (float2/half2) — `sO`, its 33.8 KB window and its fence disappear;
   (c) cp.async K/V double buffering on the f16 route ONLY: `kv32=1` keeps round 5's
   synchronous in-register-convert load because cp.async copies raw bytes and cannot convert
   (the entry rejects `dbuf=1 + kv32=1` with -305 before any launch, and the probe checks the
   rejection). The WINDOW is untouched: `kb_min` key-block range (lo monotone in qpos), the

the first had been comparing against.

### 1. The baseline is provably FRONT 6's code — and the obvious implementation of lever 1 FAILED that proof

Lever 1 needs FA2's O epilogue to write an f16 twin. The obvious implementation extracts the kernel
body into a `static __device__ __forceinline__` template so the twin is a second `__global__`
wrapper over it, rather than a 244-line copy that can drift. That was built first, and the
neutrality proof **rejected it**:

```
.text  r6=(33898, 691e803e…) f7=(33898, 691e803e…) SAME      .rodata SAME  .data SAME  .bss SAME
.nv_fatbin r6=(848696, d27b9814…) f7=(848696, 73f64537…) DIFFERS
PROOF defined symbols: r6=174 f7=174 IDENTICAL
SASS kernels: r6=27 f7=27 differing=5   →  all 7 _fa2_causal_kernel instantiations moved
SASS_FA2_NEUTRAL FAIL
```

Same **1272 instructions**, same register count, four of them rescheduled around an out-of-lined
`CALL.REL.NOINC`: an inlining boundary gives ptxas's scheduler different freedom even when the
source is semantically identical. **Every host section and all 174 defined symbols stayed
identical, so FRONT 6's proof recipe — `.text`/`.rodata`/`.data`/`.bss` plus the defined symbol
table — would have PASSED it**, and `_h0` would have been raced as FRONT 6's arm without being it.
FRONT 5 is the measured cost of assuming a codegen move is free here: a defaulted `MINB` parameter
on `__launch_bounds__` moved that same `<32,1,1>` instantiation **155 → 171 registers**, dropped it
**3 → 2 CTAs/SM**, and cost **+9.8%** on the RAG-4096 FA block in a kernel whose source had not
otherwise changed.

Two fixes, both checked rather than argued:

* `.nv_fatbin` joined the compared sections, and **both sources are compiled from one neutral path**
  (`/tmp/front7_proof/tc_shim.cu`) — because the fatbin's PTX carries a `.file` directive naming the
  source, which is the trap one level below the `STT_FILE` path symbol that made FRONT 6's
  whole-file md5 useless. Without the neutral path the section differs for a reason that has nothing
  to do with codegen, and the check is worthless in both directions.
* `_fa2_causal_kernel` restored to FRONT 6's **exact text** (verified character-for-character
  against the merged commit: `SHIPPED_FA2_KERNEL_VERBATIM PASS (244 lines)`), the twin a copy under
  `#ifdef ALGENTA_TC_SHIM_O16`. Post-fix, same recipe:

```
.nv_fatbin r6=(848696, d27b981436d80750413a76e2433a758a) f7=(848696, d27b981436d80750413a76e2433a758a) SAME
SASS kernels: r6=27 f7=27 differing=0     SASS_FA2_NEUTRAL PASS (7 instantiations compared)
```

A copy can drift, so drift is a checked invariant: `check_o16_copy.py` re-derives the twin from the
shipped kernel by applying exactly the four documented differences (name; `og16`/`rev_rows`
parameters; the `qi` expression; the epilogue) and fails on any other divergence, before the harness
builds anything. `O16_COPY_DRIFT PASS — the 266-line twin is exactly the 244-line shipped kernel
plus the four documented differences.`

**Occupancy checked, not assumed** (FRONT 5's lesson): the raced `<32,1,1>` pair is **155 registers
shipped / 156 twin**, and 3 CTAs/SM × 128 threads × 156 = 59,904 of the A100's 65,536 registers per
SM, while 4 CTAs/SM would need 79,872 either way — both sit at 3 CTAs/SM. All seven pairs printed:
155/156, 159/159, 166/166, 168/168, 168/168, 220/210, 228/228.

### 2. Lever 1 (`-D ALGENTA_7B_PF_O16TWIN`) — the f16 O twin, bit-identity PROVEN FULL-ELEMENT first

Round 6's decomposition put `A_convert_scalar` at **2.344 ms of a 260.967 ms busy** — 28 launches of
`_f32_to_f16_kernel`, one per layer, and source inspection says which role: under F16NORM+F16MLP the
rmsnorm f16 twin feeds qkv and gate/up and the SwiGLU epilogue feeds down, so **o_proj is the one
projection whose A is still f32**. That pass moves 88.1 MB/layer in 83.72 µs = 1052 GB/s, **68% of
the 1555 GB/s roof** — not even at the floor of the work it does. The twin writes the f16 O from the
accumulator register into `tc_a16` (identical position-major layout, identical `h_q*d_head` stride)
and the ship arm passes `o_f32 = NULL`, so the 58.7 MB/layer f32 write goes too.

`PF_O16LIVE_B1` (`O16TWIN and LTALGO and TC_ACC_MODE == 0`) is a **correctness** gate, not a
convenience: under any other rung the o_proj dispatch is `_tc_gemm_dispatch(pf_attn, …)`, which reads
the f32 O the epilogue would no longer have written. Both call sites test the same comptime.

Proof arm `_hv`, on the **final raced binaries**, compared **as bits** (`__half_as_ushort`, not `==`,
so +0.0/−0.0 and NaN payloads count) against `__float2half` of the f32 O:

| prefill shape | elements per prefill | prefills | mismatches |
|---|---|---|---|
| m=256 (fixture) | 25,690,112 | 9 | **0** |
| m=1024 (pp1024) | 102,760,448 | 2 | **0** |
| **m=4096 (RAG-4096)** | **411,041,792** | 7 | **0** |

`verdict = BIT-IDENTICAL (full element)` on every one; `_hv` also passes G0 16/16 (fixture) and
G0 5/5 + G1 64/64 (RAG). A negative shim status prints `NOT PROVEN`, never a zero count. The ship
arm differs from the proof arm by exactly one argument (`o_f32 = NULL`), so the f32 store is a dead
write in the proof arm and the proof transfers. Flag audit: `_h1` `o16_twin_armed=true`,
`o16_declined_at_runtime=false`; `_h0` carries no O16TWIN literal at all.

re-taken. Bounds: (a) the two cells are in the same interleaved stage and their throttle exposure is
