## ROUND 13 AMENDMENT — BOTH levers default-ON, so the shipped default IS the measured arm; the flag audit's two new rows are now EXERCISED end-to-end, and arm configurations turn out to be compilable locally with no GPU (branch `feat/gemma-ropevec-cells`, PR #1042, 2026-09-19)

Owner decision on the interaction flagged in the round-13 section above: **flip both flags**, so the
shipped default is exactly `R9_both` — the configuration that was actually measured — rather than a
never-timed one. This amendment **supersedes two statements in the section immediately above**: that
`ALGENTA_G3_PF_GQA2` "remains an explicit opt-IN flag", and that the two new `audit_tc_flags.sh` rows
are "UNEXERCISED". Both were true when written and both are now false.

### THE CHANGE

`comptime G3_PF_GQA2: Bool = G3_PF_FA2 and not is_defined["ALGENTA_G3_PF_NO_GQA2"]()` — default ON,
opt out with `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_NO_GQA2`, gated on `G3_PF_FA2` so it is inert when FA2 is off. Same
shape as the ROPEVEC flip, so both levers now read the same way and both are disabled either by their
own opt-out or by their gating parent. **The old opt-IN flags are now exact no-ops** — demonstrated,
not asserted: passing `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_ROPEVEC -D ALGENTA_G3_PF_GQA2` on top of the defaults
produced a **byte-identical object** to the default build (962792 bytes both).

An arm is therefore now defined by **what it opts out of**, and the four reachable configurations are:

| config | flags | isolates |
|---|---|---|
| `R9_both` | *(none — the shipped default)* | the measured/shipped arm |
| `R9_gqa2` | `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_NO_ROPEVEC` | ROPEVEC (vs `R9_both`) |
| `R9_ropev` | `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_NO_GQA2` | GQA2 (vs `R9_both`) |
| `R9_base` | both opt-outs | the pre-round-9 ship |

Wired into `run_ab_gemma3_round9.sh` (three arms always built; `R9_ropev` behind
`BUILD_ROPEV_ARM=1` so the ordinary build stays at three arms and costs no extra VM minutes) and into
`run_ab_gemma3_round7.sh` (`R7_base` needs both opt-outs, `R7_ropev` opts out of GQA2 only, which is
what round 7's rope-only lever meant). `chain9.sh`/`chain13.sh` delegate all building to the round-9
runner, so they are covered by that one fix.

**A pre-existing header defect was found and fixed while wiring this.** `run_ab_gemma3_round9.sh`'s
own header documented only TWO arms and **mislabelled `R9_gqa2` as `R9_base + ALGENTA_G3_PF_ROPEVEC`**
— that is `R9_both`'s definition, not `R9_gqa2`'s — and never documented `R9_both` at all. Anyone
rebuilding from the header rather than the code would have built the wrong arms. Corrected, with the
four-configuration table above in the header where the next reader will see it.

### THE AUDIT ROWS ARE EXERCISED, WITH THE FULL 2x2

`scripts/audit_tc_flags.sh` decides flag state by whether the binary carries the flag's banner
literal, so for a default-ON flag the interesting reading is **inverted**: an ABSENT literal is
positive proof the arm was built with the opt-out, i.e. that a control arm really does lack the lever
it is the control for. Both rows were run through the real script over all four configurations:

| arm | built with | ROPEVEC | GQA2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `R9_both` | *(nothing — default)* | **PRESENT** | **PRESENT** |
| `R9_gqa2` | `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_NO_ROPEVEC` | absent | **PRESENT** |
| `R9_ropev` | `-D ALGENTA_G3_PF_NO_GQA2` | **PRESENT** | absent |
| `R9_base` | both opt-outs | absent | absent |

Exactly the intended discrimination, and it closes round 12's recorded gap. Structural checks behind
it: each literal occurs **exactly once in the whole mojo tree**, each inside its own
`@parameter if <flag>:` block, so a literal reaches a binary iff the flag is true; `has_lit` is a pure
bash fixed-string substring test, and neither opt-out name contains its flag name as a substring
(`..._PF_NO_ROPEVEC` does not contain `..._PF_ROPEVEC`), nor does `ALGENTA_G3_PF_ROPE2=1` collide
with `ALGENTA_G3_PF_ROPEVEC=1` — so neither a false PRESENT nor a false ABSENT is reachable.

Object sizes also shrink monotonically as levers are dropped (**962792 -> 959056 -> 955280 ->
951384** bytes for both/gqa2-only/ropev-only/neither), which independently confirms the opt-outs
change compiled code rather than being silently ignored.

**Limit, stated so nobody over-reads it:** these are `--emit object` artifacts compiled on macOS for
sm_90 from the recovered VM driver source, NOT the linked arm executables the script audits inside a
VM window. The literal-presence mechanism is identical so the validation transfers, but the first VM
window should confirm the rows against a real linked arm as a matter of course.

### A NEW CAMPAIGN CAPABILITY FOUND WHILE DOING THIS: ARM CONFIGURATIONS COMPILE LOCALLY, NO GPU, ~10 s

This is worth more than the amendment itself. The driver source is **already in-repo** — it was
recovered into `benchmarks/llm_smoke/nvidia_race/vm_harness/adj/build/driver_ctx8192.mojo` by the
harness-recovery work — and the repo's own `scripts/build_mojo_binary.sh` defaults
`MOJO_BUILD_CUDA_TARGET` to **sm_90 on this host**, compiling through the pixi-managed mojo at
`mojo_env/.pixi/envs/default/bin/mojo` with `--emit object`. So a full sm_90 compile of the real
driver under any flag combination takes **~10 seconds and needs no GPU, no CUDA toolkit and no VM**.

Two invocation facts, because the obvious attempts fail: `mojo` must be run **through pixi from
inside `mojo_env/`** (invoking the binary directly fails with "unable to locate module 'std'" in <1 s,
which looks like a code error and is not), and `scripts/shadow_max_pkg_name_collisions.sh` should run
first. `mojo package`/`precompile` does **not** accept `--target-accelerator`, and `--emit` takes
`llvm`, not `llvm-ir`.

All **seven** reachable configurations compile clean: ship default, `NO_ROPEVEC`, `NO_GQA2`, both
opt-outs, ROPE2-off (ROPEVEC inert by gating), FA2-off (GQA2 inert by gating), and the legacy
opt-ins-as-no-ops. This means a future round can validate an arm's flag set and its audit rows on CPU
in seconds **before** spending a VM minute on it — the same ordering that made the local ptxas census
the campaign's cheapest refutation gate. It does not replace a VM build: the link step against the
CUDA shim object and cublas/cudart is still VM-only, so a clean local compile proves the flag logic
and the type correctness, not that the arm links or runs.

### pp256 STAYS AS PUBLISHED

Per the owner's decision, the published pp256 row is **left as-is** — it is a conservative
understatement of the shipped arm (32.108 ms published vs 30.571 ms measured for the round-6 ship
config) and stays that way until a bracketed pp256 measurement with drift armor exists. Round 13's
two pp256 cells (30.571 `R9_gqa2` / 30.380 `R9_both`, delta -0.191 ms) remain **indicative-only: n=2
with no closing cell and therefore no armor**. Nothing in this amendment changes any published ratio.

### THE GATE WAS NOT RE-RUN — DECLARED DEVIATION, WITH THE EVIDENCE THAT JUSTIFIES IT

Established **on CPU before the box was started**, so no VM minute was spent discovering it:
`git diff 5bf62c29 HEAD` touches six files, and the three that contain kernels —
`kernels_prefill_gemma3.mojo`, `tc_shim.cu`, `tc_shim_bridge.mojo` — are **BYTE-IDENTICAL** to the
source the round-12-certified arm `ca66b41a2ee34cde` was built from (`5bf62c29` carries round 9's
`bb1f034fe` version of the session file). The only changed Mojo source is
`session_cuda_gemma3_f16.mojo` (+76/-28), and its non-comment changes are exactly two comptime
default expressions and two `print` banner strings.

**What I did NOT manage to prove, stated plainly.** I compiled both configurations locally and
diffed the LLVM IR: 4498 lines differ. ~500 are string constants and ~374 are source line/col
metadata shifted by the lines I added, but **3624 resisted classification** — they are SSA
renumbering and string-length stores (`store i64 14` / `store i64 18`) cascading from the banner
edits. That is *consistent* with a text-only change and I believe it is one, but a cascade is not a
proof, so **no IR-equivalence claim is made**. The load-bearing evidence is instead the
byte-identical kernel sources plus the runtime flag audit below, which agrees with them.

Substitute evidence collected on the VM, and it is better than an argument: the flag audit over the

So the shipped default and the certified arm carry the **same flag family**, the +1168 bytes is the

### THE BRACKET — same binary under two names, and why

`run_gemma3_round6_cells.sh` names cells `r6<TAG>_<ARM>_<prompt>_r<i>` and **always runs both ARM_A
and ARM_B each round**, and `ARM_B` cannot be left empty (it has a default). Setting `ARM_A=ARM_B`
would therefore **collide on the cell filename and silently discard half the samples** — a bracket
that looks complete and is not. So the default was built once and `cp`'d to `R14_defB`, with
`TWIN_IDENTICAL=True` asserted by hash before any cell ran. Both slots are the same configuration,
so all 8 measured cells per prompt belong to one arm, and the A-vs-B spread doubles as a
run-to-run **reproducibility** measurement instead of being a wasted slot.

`CELLTAG=e`, 1 warmup + 4 measured + 1 closing per slot, **22 cells, every one `END rc=0` with
`offpin=0` and 1410 MHz on every 1 Hz sample**, ~110-117 s per cell (dominated by the driver loading
the 101 G checkpoint in a fresh process, which is why pp256 and pp1024 cells cost about the same).

| prompt | n (A+B) | median ms | IQR | rel-IQR% | values |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **pp1024** | 8 (4+4) | **94.249** | 0.271 | **0.288** | 93.754 93.911 94.105 94.163 94.336 94.346 94.377 94.377 |
| **pp256** | 8 (4+4) | **30.706** | 0.048 | **0.157** | 30.396 30.432 30.686 30.687 30.725 30.730 30.735 30.761 |

Both prompts complete as CELLGROUPs, pp1024 at 06:38:21Z and pp256 at 07:00:21Z, each **with its
closing cell**. Controls (`R9_gqa2` / `R9_ropev`) were declared out of scope before the window — the
brief allows them only with >=30 min remaining, and the bracket plus re-serve consumed the budget.

### THE RATIOS, COMPUTED BUT **NOT PUBLISHED — NO DRIFT ARMOR**

| prompt | default ms | same-session TRT | ratio | tok/s | published | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| pp256 | 30.706 | 41.329 | **1.3460x** | **8,337** | 32.108 ms, 7,973 tok/s, 1.2931x | **+4.567% tok/s, BEYOND its own 0.157% spread** — a real refresh candidate |

**Neither row is publishable, and the reason is mine.** The brief is "closing cell mandatory (armor
or no publish)". Both closing cells **ran and ENDed `rc=0 offpin=0`**, but chain14's phase-6(b)
globbed `r6e_*_r*.out` — a pattern that **excludes `close1`** — so the closing values were never
read, and I stopped the VM before pulling the two `.out` files. Armor is therefore not computable
from anything in hand, and per the rule the ratios above stay internal.

**Recovery costs seconds, not a window:** the values are on the persistent boot disk at
`~/lever7/runs/r6e_R9_both_pp1024_close1.out` and `..._pp256_close1.out`, preserved by
`--discard-local-ssd=false`. Read those two files and the armor falls out against the opening
medians already recorded above. **No re-measurement is needed** — the bracket is complete and banked.

Worth recording what the spread does and does not license: the 8 pp256 values span 1.2% and the 8
pp1024 values 0.66%, and the bracket ran 06:16 -> 07:00 across which a thermal or drift effect would
have to hide inside those ranges. That is *suggestive* of small drift and is **not** armor — armor is
a measured open-vs-close delta, and the distinction is the whole point of the rule.

### FOUR HARNESS DEFECTS FOUND, THREE FIXED IN `chain14.sh`

1. **The off-pin census read the WRONG FIELD and flagged every cell in the window.** It reported
   `OFF_PIN ... RE-TAKE REQUIRED` for 100+ "samples" in each of my cells *and* in round-9 files,
   while the harness's own per-cell sampler reported `offpin=0` on all 22. The sampler writes
   `2026-09-19T06:42:17Z 1410 MHz, 0 %, 0 %, 0 MiB, 97.13 W, 35` — a **space**-separated
   timestamp+clock followed by **comma**-separated nvidia-smi fields, with no header row. Under
   `-F,` that makes `$2` the GPU **utilization**, so `$2+0 != 1410` compared utilization to a clock
   and could only ever fail. **A census that flags everything is worse than none**: it cries wolf
   until a genuinely off-pin window gets waved off as the same bug. Fixed to split `$1` on spaces,
   scoped to this window's `r6e_`/`smoke_` files only (the clocks dir accumulates every previous
   window), and made to cross-check the harness's own `offpin=` values. Note chain13's identical
   census reported "no off-pin samples", so round 13's clean result was luck of a different code
   path, not a validated check — its per-cell `offpin=0` values are the real evidence there too.
2. **The phase-6(b) glob excluded the closing cells** — the direct cause of the unpublished ratios
   above. Fixed with a separate `vals_close()` so a missing close cell prints
   `ARMOR NOT COMPUTABLE — NO PUBLISH` instead of quietly yielding a median with no armor.
3. **The phase-5 TRT parser failed silently-ish** on a schema mismatch. Fixed to dump the raw JSON.
4. **NOT FIXED, recorded instead: `summarize_gemma3_round6.py` does not scan the `r6e_` label** (only
   `r6_`, `r6b_`, `r6c_`), so "pooled labels" did **not** pool — it reported `no measured runs` for
   pp1024 and for `R14_defB` entirely, and emitted a long `STALLED / MISSING CELLS` list of
   `r6e_*:NO-JSON` entries that are **artifacts of the unknown label, not real stalls**. Either add
   `r6e_` to the summariser's label list or keep using the same-bracket-only comparison, which is
   what governs here. Reading that list at face value would have sent someone hunting for 80 missing
   cells that all exist.
5. **TRAP, recorded for the next round: the summariser prints `ORACLE GATES ... ALL_PASS=True` keyed
   by ARM NAME, not by hash.** It showed `R9_both ALL_PASS=True` in a window where `R9_both` had been
   **rebuilt to a different hash** (`3c70880f9fe95910`). The gate belongs to `ca66b41a2ee34cde`. An
   arm renamed or rebuilt in place inherits the previous binary's gate line silently, so the flag
   audit's `sha256_16` column — not the gate line — is what ties a certification to a binary.

### FORECAST vs MEASURED

No forecast was pre-registered for this window: it measured an already-measured configuration at two
prompts it had not been timed at, so there was nothing to predict. The one prediction made was
procedural — that pp256 would come in near round 13's indicative 30.380/30.571 rather than near the
published 32.108 — and it did (30.706, n=8), which corroborates round 13's finding that **the
published pp256 row was computed from a stale 32.108 ms that round 6 never re-timed**. That row
overstates our pp256 time by 4.4% and therefore **understates our win**; it is the conservative
direction, and per the owner's decision it stays as published until a bracketed measurement with
armor exists. This window produced the bracket; only the armor extraction is outstanding.

## ROUND 14 ADDENDUM — TMA-staged wgmma authoring pass 1 COMPLETE on CPU, censused GREEN at peak 96/255 registers with zero spill; the register file is NOT this route's obstacle (2026-09-19, zero VM time)

Task (4) of the same window, done entirely on CPU after the VM was stopped.
`benchmarks/llm_smoke/nvidia_race/fa_g3_tma_probe.cu` **compiles clean for `sm_90a`** under the
calibrated CUDA 12.6 container, and the census was taken only after `--calibrate` re-passed **6/6
exact** against the VM's round-7 log, so the numbers are evidence.

| probe kernel | role | BN=32 | BN=64 | spill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_tma_dump_kernel` | [0] staging byte-dump | 26 | 26 | 0 |
| `_tma_dlayout_kernel` | [1] accumulator layout, identity B | 58 | 64 | 0 |
| `_tma_product_kernel` | [2] product identity over a TMA-staged tile | 58 | 64 | 0 |
| `_tma_regA_kernel` | [3] m64n128k16, **register-A**, 64 f32 accumulators | **96** | **96** | **0** |

**12 instantiations, peak 96/255, zero spill in all 12**, across both swizzle modes and both
key-block widths. The heaviest arm leaves **159 registers of headroom** to the cliff that killed
round 7 (v3 RT=2 at 255/255, spilling in 24 of 36). Established: `cp.async.bulk.tensor.2d` with the
full mbarrier handshake, a `__grid_constant__ CUtensorMap` parameter, and host-side
`cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` over the **real** `[n_keys][h_kv][d]` cache layout all compile. NOT
established: 96 is a **floor for the real kernel, not an estimate** — no online softmax, window
logic, double buffering or epilogue is in these probes yet.

**A census defect found in my own probe, generalisable.** The first run reported *"1 instantiation,
26 registers"* — a `__global__` **template is emitted only where instantiated**, and `main()`
launched only the dump kernel, so the three wgmma arms whose register count decides everything were
never compiled and the census *looked like a pass*. Fixed with a forced-instantiation array.
**Any census of a templated probe must assert the instantiation COUNT matches the intended sweep.**

**Design improvement over the scope doc:** §4 proposed pinning the accumulator layout with an
identity B, which still *infers* operand layout from a product result — the exact ambiguity that made
round 12 inconclusive. Probe **[0]** instead writes the shared-memory bytes straight back to global
after the TMA copy, so the host reads the core-matrix permutation the copy engine actually applied.
**That converts the descriptor's LBO/SBO/swizzle from a search space into a lookup table.** [0] is
fully wired and runnable; the host drivers for [1]-[3] are pass-2 work and `main()` says so rather
than pretending.

Pass 2 priced in `WGMMA_TMA_SCOPE.md` §9: **unchanged at 2 VM windows (~1.5-2 h of cap) and 2 CPU
authoring passes**, with pass 1 of the two now spent and the register-file risk retired. Confirmed
rather than predicted: the shim needs **`-lcuda`** for `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`, and the host entry
must answer explicitly what happens to cached tensor maps when the KV cache is reallocated. The
recommendation is also unchanged and now better-supported — the prize is bounded by flashinfer's
21.01 ms (≈10 ms after the ~65-80% transfer discount ⇒ rag4096 ≈1.133x), so **norm-accum remains the
better next spend per VM minute** at ~25 min of nsys versus a multi-window project.

No gitbook page touched. Ledger append-only. No VM time spent on this addendum.

### (2) NORM-ACCUM: THE PRE-REGISTERED QUESTION CANNOT BE ANSWERED, AND THE REASON IS INSTRUMENTATION

The question was registered before the trace was taken, so the answer cannot be shopped: measured
`norms` bucket vs the **6.83 ms** DRAM roof — near the roof means bandwidth-bound, *nothing to win*,
close the lever; near **~16 ms** means instruction/loop-bound and vectorising the loops is the fix.

**The measured `norms` bucket is 0.046 ms from only 4 instances.** In a 62-layer rag4096 prefill that
cannot be the per-layer norm work — 4 instances where at least 124 are expected means the bucket
caught essentially nothing. **So neither branch of the test can be asserted: the lever is NOT priced
and NOT closed**, and round 6's ~16.2 ms geometry-attributed figure is neither confirmed nor refuted.

**ROOT CAUSE, and it is not the region logic.** The per-layer norm and rope kernels are
**Mojo-compiled with content-hash names** — `residentk_kernels_prefill_gemma6A6A_8f4c4e1d2ba54545`,
`residentk_kernels__pf_rmsnorm_6A6A6A6A_280bf58af8ffb4e6`. The extractor's bucket rules match **NAME
SUBSTRINGS** (`rmsnorm`, `layernorm`, `_norm`, ...), and a hashed Mojo symbol does not present those
substrings usefully, so the work falls into the `mojo_per_layer` catch-all: **79.156 ms across 2616
instances**, 45.687 ms of it in one kernel appearing **434 times = 62 layers x 7**. The norm work is
in the trace and it is being measured; it is simply not being *attributed*.

The fix is therefore to bucket by kernel **IDENTITY** (the emitting Mojo module/function) rather than
by name substring. A table of hashed names would work once and then go stale on **every build**, since
the hash is content-derived — so identity-based bucketing is the only durable answer. Until then
norm-accum stays unpriced, and it should not be ranked against other levers as though it were.

**CONTROL RESULT, recorded so nobody "fixes" the region logic again expecting it to rescue this row.**
`--from-first-attn` worked exactly as designed: it excluded **821 leading records (33.887 ms busy)** as
model load / weight staging, with the boundary correctly identified as
`_fa_g3_window2_kernel<(int)32,(bool)0,(bool)1,(int)1>`, and produced **no negative rows**. But on
this trace round 6's idle-gap basis gave nearly identical numbers (gemm 432.667 vs 432.693;
mojo_per_layer 79.132 vs 79.156; `norms` **0.046 in both**), because the idle-gap clustering had
already separated the load into its own cluster (cluster 0: 802 records, 33.305 ms busy). Round 6's
negative-row failure did **not** reproduce here. **The region fix is real but it is not what blocked
norm-accum — the bucket rules are.**

### (4) THE TWO SUMMARISER DEFECTS ARE FIXED

Both were found in round 14 and both are fixed in `summarize_gemma3_round6.py`:

   `("", "b", "c")` and range `r1..r7` caused three failures from one root cause: a new `CELLTAG`
   (`r6e_`) reported "no measured runs" for a bracket that had completed 22 cells and emitted ~80

2. **The ORACLE GATES line is now hash-bound.** It was keyed by ARM NAME via `oracle_gate_<ARM>.json`,

   audit's `sha256_16` for the same arm and prints MATCH / MISMATCH / NOT-HASH-BOUND next to the

`--discard-local-ssd=false`, `TERMINATED` confirmed, `status=RUNNING` empty project-wide). Everything

### (0) KERNEL-IDENTITY BUCKETING, BUILT AND VALIDATED — NO HAND-MAINTAINED NAME TABLE

Round 15's blocker was that Mojo device kernels in `kernels_prefill_gemma3.mojo` are named
`residentk_kernels_prefill_gemma6A6A_<16-hex content hash>`: the module path alone consumes the whole
31-char name budget, so **the function name is gone and only the hash distinguishes them**. Name-
substring bucketing therefore dumped 79.156 ms (14.2% of busy, 2616 instances) into one catch-all and
the `norms` bucket caught 4 instances instead of the >=124 a 62-layer prefill implies.

**Method — differential compilation.** Two facts make it work locally: the hash is **content-derived**
and, verified this round, **path-independent** — a macOS build reproduces the exact hashes the H200
binary carries. So `mojo_kernel_identity.sh` builds the shipped default, then one variant per comptime
flag removed (`PF_ROPE2`, `PF_F16NORM`, `PF_F16MLP`, `GEGLU_U4`, `PF_F16ATTN`, `PF_KV16`, `PF_BN32`,
`PF_FA2`, plus the `NO_ROPEVEC` and `NO_GQA2` opt-outs), and diffs the kernel-symbol sets. **A kernel
that VANISHES when flag F is removed is a kernel F enables; one that APPEARS is the alternate
implementation F was suppressing.** That is evidence, not a guess, and it regenerates on every build —
a hand-maintained hash table would be wrong after the first source edit, because the hash is
content-derived. 11 builds at ~4 s each.

**Validated against the deployed binary, not assumed.** The profiled arm is `R9_both`
`sha256_16=3c70880f9fe95910` (6167152 B), and all five identity hashes were found in it by `strings`
with **hit counts identical to the local object** (11/18/35/18/27). So the CPU-generated table provably
describes the binary that produced the trace.

The pre-registered rule was: near the roof ⇒ record "nothing to win" and close the lever; near ~16 ms

2026-09-19T08:26:50.016-07:00 (= 15:26:50Z), stop issued 16:58:26Z, stop returned **17:00:48Z**
against a 17:01:50Z hard deadline. Stopped with `--discard-local-ssd=false`, **`TERMINATED`
confirmed**, and a project-wide `--filter='status=RUNNING'` returned **empty**. Every port, compile,

### (0a) THE LTALGO PORT — COMPILED CLEAN LOCALLY BEFORE A SINGLE VM MINUTE, AND THE GATE IS PROVEN FROM THE OBJECTS

Round 16 declared this lever unreachable in its window and said so *before* spending a VM minute,
because the machinery existed only in the 7B lane (`session_cuda_p3.mojo`,
`ALGENTA_7B_PF_LTALGO`, `PF_LTINSITU_B1`, `lt_shapes_tuned`). Round 17 ports it. Three pieces,
in PR #1052:

* **`tc_shim.cu`** — a SEAM-FREE twin `tc_lt::matmul_async` plus the two `_async_lt` entries. The
  twin exists rather than reusing `matmul()` because this lane runs with the shim's `g_noseam == 0`
  (it gets zero-sync ordering from `ALGENTA_G3_STREAM` instead), so `matmul()`'s trailing
  `cudaStreamSynchronize` would have added a **per-projection sync seam the control arm does not
  have**. That is not an algorithm effect, so the bracket would have measured the seam instead of
  the algorithm — invalidating the A/B rather than merely slowing it. Turning on
  `ALGENTA_TC_NOSEAM` to suppress it is not the answer either: that switch also repoints `g_stream`
  and flips every other sync-bearing entry, changing the control too. Scope limit stated in the
  source: **stage-time search only**, the `LTINSITU` rotating event ring is not ported.
* **`tc_shim_bridge.mojo`** — `TC_G3_LTALGO` plus the gated try inside the two `_pre_async`
  wrappers every gemma-3 projection already funnels through, so one comptime change covers all
  dispatch sites and cannot miss one. Decline semantics identical to the 7B lane: **-320** (never
  tuned) falls through to the shipped `cublasGemmEx` call, so an untuned shape runs the shipped path
  byte-for-byte and a partially tuned build degrades to the control instead of failing.
* **`session_cuda_gemma3_f16.mojo`** — `_tune_lt_shapes()` from `seal()`, and the banner's
  `lt_shapes_tuned = N of 4` field.

**`G3_PF_LTALGO` is an ALIAS of the bridge's `TC_G3_LTALGO`, not a second `is_defined` test.** The
bridge decides whether a dispatch *tries* the tuned algorithm; the session decides whether it was
ever *searched for*. Two independent reads of one macro could drift apart under an edit into the
worst available failure mode — a build that tunes shapes nothing consumes, or one whose dispatch
declines on every call while the banner still claims the lever. One definition makes that
unrepresentable.

**`seal()`'s ordering is load-bearing in three directions** (documented at the call site): *after*
`_arm_fused_fa`, because o_proj's f16 A twin only exists if FA armed and tuning a shape nothing
dispatches would inflate the count into a lie; *before* `_print_round5_flag_audit`, because the
banner prints `_tc_lt_count()` and reading it before the search ran would print 0 for a lever about
to work; *before* `_prime_prefill_modules`, because the tuned algorithm is a **different nvjet
kernel** and CUDA loads modules lazily — priming after the search primes the module the timed
dispatches actually launch, priming before it charges the first request for a JIT of a kernel the
lever then never uses.

**ONE TUNE COVERS BOTH RACED CELLS, and that is a shape fact rather than a convenience.**
`G3_PF_TILE` is a comptime **1024** with no flag override, so a prompt is walked in 1024-row passes
and every projection dispatches at m = 1024 regardless of prompt length. **rag4096 (4 passes) and
pp1024 (1 pass) therefore present the same four GEMM shapes.** A prompt that is not a multiple of
the tile runs a shorter final pass at an untuned M, which declines (-320) to GemmEx rather than
borrowing an algorithm tuned for another shape — which is also why pp256 is a *structural* null for
this lever, not merely an unmeasured one.

**The compile gate, proven from the artifacts rather than asserted.** Both arms build rc=0 with zero
errors and an **identical warning count (979/979)**, locally, no GPU:

| probe of the `--emit object` output | shipped default | default + `ALGENTA_G3_PF_LTALGO` |
|---|---|---|
| bytes | 962792 | 983392 |
| undefined `tc_shim_*` symbols (`nm -u`) | 15, **none of them cublasLt** | the same 15 **+ exactly 5**: `tc_shim_lt_init`, `_lt_tune`, `_lt_count`, `_32c_pre_async_lt`, `_16c_pre_async_lt` |
| `lt_shapes_tuned` string literal | 0 | 1 |
| `TCFLAG ALGENTA_G3_PF_LTALGO=1` literal | 0 | 1 |

Two **independent** builds of the shipped default were **byte-identical** (md5
`04471f0cdb3049fafcd99737dceb329c`, 962792 B), which is what makes that comparison a real
comparison rather than two artifacts of one invocation. `tc_shim.cu`'s cublasLt block has **no
`#else` stubs**, so an arm that passes the macro but links a stock shim **fails at link time** — the
loud failure this campaign prefers over a silent runtime decline that would leave a cell measured on
the wrong code path.

**Two shim flavours, so the control is provably lever-free.** `build_shim_gemma3_round7.sh` gained
`EXTRA_MACROS` and `OBJNAME`, both defaulting to its previous behaviour so rounds 5/6/7/9 are
unaffected. `run_ab_gemma3_round17.sh` builds a stock object for the control and an
`-D ALGENTA_TC_SHIM_LT` object for the lever arm. Because there are no stubs, the control linked
against the stock object **contains no part of the lever provably** — not "contains it but does not
reach it". Its `verify` stage then re-checks that from the **linked binaries**, since this campaign
was already burned once by a rebuild that had silently dropped `-D ALGENTA_G3_STREAM` and produced a
gemma-3-27b column wrong at oracle index 0 on 5/6 prompts. On the VM it read:

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `R17_ctl` | `dc276126803d1479` | **6167152** | **0** (nm=0, nm -D=0, strings=0) | **0** | **VERIFIED CLEAN** |
| `R17_lt` | `41aa6f502d1d0323` | 6198032 | 4 (nm=3, strings=4) | 1 | **VERIFIED ARMED** |

`R17_ctl`'s byte size **6167152 is exactly round 16's certified `R9_both` arm size**, so the control
is the shipped default rebuilt rather than some other configuration. The symbol probe takes the max
of `nm`, `nm -D` and `strings` because the shim is linked *in*, making `tc_shim_lt_tune` a **defined**
symbol rather than an undefined reference; had all three read zero for **both** arms the stage
reports itself INCONCLUSIVE instead of being silently read as "the control is clean" — an instrument
that cannot fail cannot pass either.

### (0b) THE UNATTRIBUTED 14.225 ms KERNEL IS NAMED — AND THE PRESCRIBED INSTRUMENT WAS BROKEN

**`residentk_kernels_prefill_gemma6A6A_0e8212f1154807d7` IS `_pf_norm_accum_rows_kernel`**
(`kernels_prefill_gemma3.mojo:152`) — Gemma 3's fused post-branch rmsnorm **+ residual add**,
`hidden[m,:] += rmsnorm(y[m,:]) * gamma`, launched twice per layer (post_attention on the o_proj
output, post_feedforward on the down_proj output) at `grid_dim = m_rows`, `block_dim = 256`.

Named by **differential source perturbation**, as round 16 prescribed, with a **double lock**:

| # | experiment | PTX body of the entry | entry hash `0e8212f1…` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | perturb `_pf_norm_accum_rows_kernel`'s **body** (`inv += Float32(1e-7)`, store `+ Float32(1e-7)`) — confirmed codegen-visible, object md5 moved, +64 B, PTX len 2605 -> 2671 | **CHANGED** | unchanged |
| 4 | **rename** `_pf_norm_accum_rows_kernel` -> `…ZZ`, body byte-identical | unchanged (`4497a7b1564290fb`) | **CHANGED -> `3a37b7cd25c9d50e`** |

Experiments 1 and 4 read together are the identification: the body that moves when this function is
perturbed is the body that hash dispatches, and renaming the function moves the hash while leaving
the body identical. Both cross-validations also landed, confirming the method: **`edb887a57300fe94`
= `_pf_rmsnorm_rows_f16_kernel`** and **`8f4c4e1d2ba54545` = `_pf_geglu_rows_f16_kernel`**. The
reverted tree rebuilt **byte-identical** to the baseline object, so there is zero perturbation
residue and the builds are deterministic.

**THE INSTRUMENT CORRECTION, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN THE IDENTIFICATION.** Round 16 recorded that
"the hash is **content-derived**" and inferred that a hand-maintained table "would be wrong after
the first source edit". **Both claims are false, and the first one disabled the obvious instrument.**
The 16-hex suffix is derived from the **mangled name** (qualified name + signature), *not* from the
body — proven in both directions above: a genuine body change moved the PTX and left the hash alone,
and a pure rename moved the hash and left the PTX alone. Consequences:

1. **Round 16's prescribed method for exactly this kernel returns a FALSE NEGATIVE.** "Perturb one
   candidate function at a time in a way visible to codegen … observe which content-hash moves"
   cannot work, because a codegen-visible body change does not move the hash. A round following that
   instruction literally would have concluded the kernel is unnameable and moved on.
2. **The instrument that works is the embedded-plaintext-PTX body diff.** `--emit object` produces a
   host object carrying the PTX as plaintext (`.visible .entry <mangled>(…)`); split on `.entry`,
   digest each body with the entry name normalised out, diff against baseline. It works on
   **unconditional** kernels, which is precisely the class the flag-differential cannot reach — the
   reason round 16 could not name this one.
3. **The identity table does NOT go stale on every source edit.** It is stable unless a kernel's name
   or signature changes, which makes it cheaper to maintain than round 16 assumed.
4. Round 16's *flag*-differential results are **unaffected** and remain valid: removing a `-D` flag
   removes or adds whole functions, so their names appear and disappear regardless of whether the
   hash tracks name or body. Only the stated *premise*, and the source-perturbation method built on
   it, were wrong.

**A CONSEQUENT CORRECTION TO ROUND 16's LEDGER — the norm pricing was applied to the wrong kernel.**
Round 16 labelled the 11.782 ms / 867-instance pool "f16 NORM (= norm-accum)" and priced it against
round 8's 6.83 ms DRAM roof, concluding "1.73x its roof". But round 8 derived that 6.83 ms roof for
`_pf_norm_accum_rows_kernel` ("12n x 1024 rows x 496 launches = 32.8 GB -> 6.83 ms at 4.8 TB/s"),
and the 11.782 ms pool is `_pf_rmsnorm_rows_f16_kernel` — the plain pre-projection rmsnorm. **These
are two distinct kernels and two distinct levers, not one:**

| pool | ms | n | identity (0b, evidenced) | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0e8212f1154807d7` | **14.225** | 868 | **`_pf_norm_accum_rows_kernel`** | residual add **+** rmsnorm, 2x/layer — round 16 left this UNATTRIBUTED |
| `edb887a57300fe94` | 11.782 | 867 | `_pf_rmsnorm_rows_f16_kernel` | pre-projection rmsnorm writing the f16 A twin, 2x/layer — round 16 *called* this "norm-accum" |

Their instance counts (868 vs 867, i.e. 62 x 14 and 62 x 14 - 1) are near-identical because both are
row-per-block, twice-per-layer kernels — which is exactly why a count could never separate them, and
why round 16 was right to refuse the inference. They are also **signature twins**: both emit 6 PTX
params (3 `.u64 .ptr .align 1` + 2 `.u64` + 1 `.f32`), both `grid_dim = m`, both `block_dim = 256`.
Geometry cannot separate them either. Only the body differential can.

**A BASIS FINDING ABOUT THE REGION ITSELF.** Splitting every kernel's instances by `gridX` (which
*is* the row count m for these row-per-block kernels) shows the `--from-first-attn` region is not a
single 4-pass rag4096 prefill but a **7-pass mixture**: 5 passes at m=1024, 1 at m=512, 1 at m=256.
Evidence — the f16 GeGLU's grid is `ceil(m*d_ff/256)`, and its three observed grids are exactly
86016 / 43008 / 21504 = m 1024 / 512 / 256, at 310 / 62 / 62 instances = 62 layers x 5 / x1 / x1;
`_pf_norm_accum_rows_kernel` shows 620 / 124 / 124 = 62 x 10 / x2 / x2, i.e. twice per layer-pass
over the same 7 passes. Round 8's 496-launch assumption (4 passes) is therefore **not the right
denominator for this region**, and the "% of busy" figures published in rounds 15/16 describe that
mixture rather than one rag4096 prefill. This does **not** disturb any per-kernel roofline ratio
below, because those are computed per geometry from the trace's own grids — but it does mean the
census should not be read as a pure single-cell rag4096 profile, and it is recorded here so the next
round does not inherit the assumption.

### (0c) THE f16 MLP KERNEL PRICED — **4.66x ITS DRAM ROOF**, AND IT IS NOW THE LARGEST POOL IN THE MODEL

`_pf_geglu_rows_f16_kernel`, hash `8f4c4e1d2ba54545` (identity evidenced in 0b), **45.687 ms / 434
instances / 8.22% of region busy**. Its traffic comes straight from the source: per output element
it reads `gu16[row*2*n_ff + j]` (gate, f16) and `gu16[row*2*n_ff + n_ff + j]` (up, f16) and writes
`act16[i]` (f16) — **6 bytes per element, d_ff = 21504 elements per row, no re-reads**. Same table
format round 16 used for norm-accum, on the campaign's own constants (4.8 TB/s HBM3e roof, 989 TF/s
at the 1410 MHz pin):

| quantity | value |
|---|---|
| rows in the region (from the trace's own grids) | 365056 = 310x1024 + 62x512 + 62x256 |
| bytes per row | 129024 B (6 B/elem x 21504) |
| total traffic | **47.101 GB** |
| **DRAM roof at 4.8 TB/s** | **9.813 ms** |
| measured | **45.687 ms** |
| **measured / roof** | **4.656x** — running at **21.5% of roof** |
| achieved bandwidth | **1.031 TB/s** |
| compute: 70.65 GFLOP at 989 TF/s | 0.0714 ms = **0.156%** of measured -> the FMA pipe is irrelevant |
| 7.850 G `tanh` at the SFU rate (16/SM/clk x 132 SM x 1.41 GHz) | 2.636 ms = 5.8% of measured |
| **max headroom to roof** | **35.874 ms** |
| **headroom at the 65-80% transfer band** | **23.318 - 28.700 ms** |

**It is unambiguously MEMORY BOUND** — arithmetic is 0.156% of the measured time, and even pricing
every `tanh` at the SFU rate leaves 5.8%. So the 4.66x gap to roof is an access-pattern problem, not
a math problem, and the source says why: the kernel is **scalar, one thread per element, with 2-byte
f16 loads and stores**. `-D ALGENTA_G3_GEGLU_U4` exists and is in the shipped default's flag stack,
but it selects a u4 variant of the **decode** GEMV (`_g3_norm_gemv2_geglu_kernel_f16_u4`,
`grid_dim = ceil(d_ff/_SUBS)`); **the prefill f16 GeGLU has no vectorised twin at all.** The
precedent for the fix is in this campaign: ROPEVEC replaced scalar RoPE accesses with `_ld4/_st4`
16-byte quads and delivered **-1.687 ms measured at 14.5x its drift armor** — and that was against a
6.680 ms pool, whereas this one is 45.687 ms at 21.5% of roof.

**REVISED LEVER RANKING — and round 16's #1 is now largely closed.** Re-ranked by *evidenced*
headroom rather than by pool size, with this round's bracket folded in:

| # | pool | measured ms | evidenced headroom | status after round 17 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **f16 MLP (`_pf_geglu_rows_f16_kernel`)** | 45.687 | **35.874 ms raw / 23.3-28.7 transferred** | **OPEN, and now #1.** Memory bound at 21.5% of roof with a scalar 2-byte access pattern and no vectorised twin. Clears the 12.07 ms bar on its own at any transfer ratio in the band |
| 2 | GEMM (algorithm selection) | 432.694 | **1.145 ms MEASURED** | **LARGELY CLOSED.** Round 16 ranked this #1 on "+5% eff = 21.6 ms". The mechanism that would have delivered it does not exist: **3 of 4 roles already had the timed winner at heuristic index 0.** The pool is at 68.8% of peak because of the algorithms cuBLAS already picks, not because it picks badly |
| 3 | wgmma (attention) | 38.114 | 17.104 ms ceiling, bar at 70.5% transfer | Unchanged, but its **cross-basis comparator caveat is still OPEN** (see below) |
| 4 | `_pf_rmsnorm_rows_f16_kernel` | 11.782 | 6.877 ms raw (2.402x its own 6n roof) / 4.47-5.50 transferred | **RE-PRICED on its own kernel** — round 16 priced it against the *other* kernel's roof |
| 5 | `_pf_norm_accum_rows_kernel` (the real norm-accum) | 14.225 | 4.412 ms raw (1.450x its 12n roof) / 2.87-3.53 transferred | **RE-PRICED.** At 69.0% of roof it is much closer to exhausted than round 16's "1.73x" implied. If the y re-read misses L2 (16n model) the roof is 13.084 ms and it is at **92.0% of roof**, headroom 1.141 ms — i.e. possibly nothing to win |

The re-pricing above is on the same 4.8 TB/s basis round 8 used, cross-checked by reproducing its
published figure exactly: 12n x 1024 x 496 = 32.766 GB -> **6.826 ms** against its published

**DRIFT ARMOR MEASURED, AND IT HOLDS.** The group closes A..B..A, so drift is a measurement:
control opening median 386.154 -> closing median 386.285, a drift of **+0.131 ms = 0.132x the
opening rel-IQR** (0.992 ms); worst-case `max|close - open(r1)|` = **0.637 ms**. Drift is well inside
the opening noise scale, so **the armor holds and the bracket is not disqualified on drift.**

| comparison | value |

**VERDICT: RESOLVED at -1.145 ms, and NOT WORTH SHIPPING.** The delta exceeds its measured drift
armor by 1.80x, so by the campaign's own rule it is a real effect rather than noise — but it is only
**1.154x the pooled IQR** and sits exactly on the rank-test boundary, i.e. it is the *weakest*
RESOLVED result this campaign has recorded, against round 13's ROPEVEC at **14.5x** its armor. And
its size is the finding: **-1.145 ms is 9.48% of the 12.07 ms the 1.15x bar needs.** Against round
13's same-session TRT-LLM 1.2.1 pair (429.400 ms) it would move rag4096 from **1.1140x to 1.1153x**
— a change in the fourth significant figure, far below what a published row should be republished
for. **No row changes; the publish/ledger call is the owner's and this entry does not preempt it.**

**WHY IT IS SO SMALL — AND WHY THAT ANSWER IS WORTH MORE THAN A WIN WOULD HAVE BEEN.** The bracket
and the search output agree on a mechanism: only **qkv** moved off heuristic index 0 (to index 4),
while o_proj, gate/up and down all had their timed winner **at index 0 already**. So the lever could
only ever improve one of four projection roles, and it improved the wall by 0.30% — consistent with
roughly a 1.5% gain on the qkv GEMM alone. **Round 16's #1 ranked lever was priced on "+5% GEMM
efficiency = 21.6 ms"; the +5% is not available from algorithm selection, because for three of four
roles cuBLAS's DEFAULT estimate already picks what a timed search picks.** The GEMM pool sits at
68.8% of pinned peak for reasons that are not heuristic mis-selection, and any further gain there
needs a different kernel (wgmma/TMA), not a different algorithm choice. That is a *cheap* refutation
— one 342 ms search and one bracket—and it redirects the campaign to a pool with 35.874 ms of
evidenced headroom instead of one with ~1.1 ms.

### FLASHINFER SAME-BASIS RE-MEASUREMENT — **NOT TAKEN**, so §10's largest uncertainty stays OPEN

`WGMMA_TMA_SCOPE.md` §10 is **deliberately not updated this round.** Its caveat 2 is that the
flashinfer comparator's 21.01 ms is **cross-basis** (round 6, a different region definition and
session) against our 38.114 ms `--from-first-attn`, and that this is "the single largest uncertainty
in the number [and] should be closed before any window is spent" on wgmma. Closing it needs a
same-basis, same-session, same-region-definition flashinfer attention bucket. The bracket completed
at 16:57:51Z against a 17:01:50Z hard stop, leaving **under four minutes** — not merely short but
off by an order of magnitude, since a flashinfer arm needs its own environment, warmup and region
extraction. **The choice was explicit: a complete gated bracket with holding armor, or an incomplete
bracket plus an incomplete comparator. The bracket was chosen**, because a partial bracket is not
publishable under any reading of the protocol while an open caveat merely defers a decision that is
not yet funded. Consequence, stated plainly: **the 17.104 ms wgmma gap and the 70.5% transfer
requirement remain UNVERIFIED, and no wgmma window should be spent until the comparator is
re-measured on the same basis.** That is now the prerequisite for lever #3, and it is a *cheaper*
prerequisite than the lever itself.

### PROCESS EVIDENCE, AND TWO FAILURES RECORDED BECAUSE THEY COST MINUTES

CPU-first ordering held: the port, both local compiles, the whole of (0b) and (0c) and the harness
were finished with the VM **TERMINATED**, and the instance was started only after the compile gate
passed. Single window log (`~/lever17/round17.log`), liveness heartbeats from `chain7stage.sh`,
per-cell clock and off-pin records, one log per stage. **No `KILLED_BY_OPERATOR`** — nothing was
killed; the bracket finished on its own 69 s before the stop was issued. No gitbook page touched.
Ledger append-only: this section is a single hunk at EOF with zero deleted or modified lines earlier
in the file. Kernel and harness code went out as **PR #1052, PR-not-merge**, and the owner merged it
at `c906ad35`; this ledger entry is a separate PR off `origin/main`, cut as a **new** branch after
#1052's branch was auto-deleted on merge (pushing to a merged PR's deleted branch silently recreates
it, and `* [new branch]` is the tell — so it was not reused).

Two failures, recorded because a round that only reports its successes is not auditable:

1. **A self-inflicted quoting bug cost ~1 minute at the worst possible moment.** The gate->timing
   waiter was written as an inline `bash -c` string containing a nested `python3 -c` gate check;
   the `'"'"'all_pass'"'"'` escaping survived one layer of quoting and not two, producing
   `['all_pass'])` with an unmatched paren. The waiter raised `SyntaxError`, read it as "gate did not
   pass", and **aborted before launching the bracket** — at 16:18:15Z with 43 min of cap left and
   36 min of bracket to run. Recovered by reading `GATE ALL_PASS = True` directly from the gate log
   and launching the bracket without the broken re-check. The lesson is the one
   `run_gemma3_round6_cells.sh` already documents for `pgrep`: **a guard whose own expression can
   fail silently must not be the only thing standing between a window and its measurement.** A
   gate-check that errors should abort *loudly and distinguishably* from a gate that fails.
2. **Two SSH calls hung client-side for 300 s each** because a backgrounded remote process inherited
   the channel; the jobs had in fact launched correctly both times. Recovered with
   `setsid nohup … </dev/null & disown` plus a local redirect. Cost ~5 min of wall clock, none of it
   VM-on.

**What round 17 did NOT do**, so the entry is not over-read: pp1024 was not bracketed; `R17_ctl` was
not re-gated; flashinfer was not re-measured and §10 was not updated; the `LTINSITU` in-situ search
was not ported (only the stage-time search); no vectorised f16 GeGLU was authored — lever #1 is
**priced and diagnosed, not implemented**; and no published row changed.


## ROUND 18 — gemma-3-27b-it H200: lever #1 IMPLEMENTED and MEASURED. The vectorised f16 prefill GeGLU twin (`ALGENTA_G3_PF_GEGLU_V2`) is **RESOLVED at −19.396 ms (−5.030%) on rag4096 at 24.5x its most conservative drift armor**, with **COMPLETE rank separation** (all 5 lever runs below all 5 control runs, Mann-Whitney U = 0, exact p = 0.0079) and **0 BITDIFF over 8 compared cells**; the cell moves rag4096 from **1.1067x to 1.1653x** (1.1136x → **1.1725x** on round 13's same-session comparator) and **CLEARS the 1.15x bar by 7.176 ms**. It transferred **77.7% of its same-basis headroom**, inside the campaign's calibrated 65–80% band — and getting the basis right is what showed that, because against the REGION pool it looks like 54.1% and reads as a band miss (kernel branch `feat/gemma3-gegluvec-r18`, **PR #1059**, DEFAULT OFF; harness + fixes on the same branch; 2026-09-19)

### (0a) THE LEVER — AUTHORED ON CPU, AND ITS WHOLE MECHANISM IS 3 INSTRUCTIONS INSTEAD OF 24

Round 17 named lever #1 and stopped there: "no vectorised f16 GeGLU was authored — lever #1 is
**priced and diagnosed, not implemented**." Round 18 implements it. `_pf_geglu_rows_f16_vec_kernel`
gives one thread **eight contiguous f16 = 16 bytes** per operand, through new `_ld8h`/`_st8h`
helpers that carry the `alignment=16` annotation `residentk.loadvec` exists to supply. It is gated
on `G3_PF_F16MLP` (ROPEVEC's pattern, so with F16MLP off it is inert by construction) and its shape
contract is discharged **at the dispatch site**: `d_ff % 8 == 0` is what makes `total = m * d_ff` a
multiple of 8 too, so the group guard is exact and no thread can overrun either buffer, and it is
also what makes all three element offsets multiples of 16 bytes. A shape that fails it keeps the
scalar twin byte-for-byte, so **the flag can never produce a ragged tail on any model**.

The mechanism, read off PTX extracted from the compiled objects with no GPU anywhere in the loop:

| per 8 output elements | scalar twin (shipped) | vector twin | vector twin with `-D ALGENTA_L0_NOALIGN` |
|---|---|---|---|
| global loads | 16 × `ld.global.b16` | **2 × `ld.global.v4.b32`** | 16 × `ld.global.b16` |
| global stores | 8 × `st.global.b16` | **1 × `st.global.v4.b32`** | 8 × `st.global.b16` |
| **memory instructions** | **24** | **3** | **24 — no better than the control** |

**That third column is worth more than the win.** `load[width=8]` on its own buys *nothing*; the
`alignment=16` annotation **is the entire lever**. It reproduces the micro-autopsy's lever-#0 defect
for f16 and shows why `residentk.loadvec` is a module and not a comment.

The same rebuild **reproduced round 17's hash trap in-round**: the kernel's 16-hex hash stayed
`b0496694ffefbc3c` across a body-only perturbation, because Mojo's hash is **NAME-derived**. Hash
equality is therefore a *false negative* for "the body did not change", which is exactly why the body
differential is read off the PTX and never off the hash.

Per-element arithmetic is the scalar twin's **verbatim**, eight times, with the same four f32
immediates at exactly 8x the count: `0f3D372713` / `0f3F4C422A` / `0f3F000000` / `0f3F800000` 1→8
each, `cvt.f32.f16` 2→16, `mul.f32` 6→48, `fma.rn.f32` 1→8, `tanh.approx.f32` 1→8, `add.f32` 1→8.
The scalar twin's `tanh` already lowered to `tanh.approx.f32`, so the lever changes nothing there.

**ptxas census, round-8 method, CALIBRATED FIRST.** `ptxas_census_local.sh --calibrate` reproduces
the VM's round-7 register counts **6/6 EXACT** (165/172/165/172/166/166) plus v3's 36 instantiations
(66 total, peak 255, 24 spilling), so the census is evidence and not a local curiosity:

| kernel | registers | stack frame | spill stores | spill loads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_pf_geglu_rows_f16_kernel` (control) | 26 | 0 B | **0** | **0** |
| `_pf_geglu_rows_f16_vec_kernel` (lever) | **28** | 0 B | **0** | **0** |

**+2 registers for 8x the work per thread, zero spills**, and both are register-limited to the same
8 blocks/SM, so **occupancy is unchanged** — the win is purely the memory-instruction count.

*A correction to the round-8 tooling note, recorded rather than left to mislead the next round:
`ptxas_census_local.sh`'s header says the container reports the box's `V12.6.85`. On this arm64 host
`nvidia/cuda:12.6.0-devel-ubuntu22.04` reports **V12.6.20, Built Fri_Jun_14_16:39:31_PDT_2024** —
same 12.6 release, different build. The mandatory calibration passes 6/6 regardless, so the census
rests on **calibration**, not on the version string. The stale comment should be fixed.*

### (0b) BIT-IDENTITY — CLAIMED BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THE ONE AMBIGUITY IN THE CLAIM WAS CHECKED

GeGLU is purely **elementwise**: no reduction, no accumulation, no cross-element movement, so there
is no association order for a vectorised twin to disturb. `_g3_geglu_f16_elem` is the scalar body
transposed verbatim. Contrast ROPEVEC, which had to re-associate the `qk_norm` sum-of-squares, and
LTALGO, where a tuned algorithm may split K — neither could claim exactness, and both had to settle
for oracle agreement.

The one instruction-level difference is the output narrowing: 8 × `cvt.rn.f16.f32` becomes
4 × `cvt.rn.f16x2.f32`, same `.rn` round-to-nearest-even, two independent conversions. **That packs
two lanes per register, which made lane order a live correctness question** — and it was resolved
against the authoritative CUDA header rather than against documentation prose:

```
cuda_fp16.hpp:__internal_device_float2_to_half2_rn(const float a, const float b)
    SM80+ :  asm("{ cvt.rn.f16x2.f32 %0, %2, %1; }" : "=r"(...) : "f"(a), "f"(b));
    pre-80:  cvt.rn.f16.f32 low,  %1;   // %1 = a -> low
             cvt.rn.f16.f32 high, %2;   // %2 = b -> high
             mov.b32 %0, {low,high};
```

Both paths must mean `a`→low, and the SM80+ path passes `b` as the instruction's *first* source — so
in `cvt.rn.f16x2.f32 d, X, Y` it is **`Y` that lands in the low 16 bits**. LLVM emits
`cvt.rn.f16x2.f32 %r105, <elem1>, <elem0>` and stores `%r105` at the lowest address, so elem0 lands
at `act16[g8+0]`. **CORRECT.** The load side was traced the same way: `ld.global.v4.b32` puts the
lowest address in the first register, and `mov.b32 {%rs7,%rs8}, %r22` splits low-half-first, so
`%rs7` is gate element 0 and `%rs15` (from the up load's first register) is up element 0 — the gate/up
pairing is right too.

**A documentation summary asserting the opposite ("operand `a` is stored in the lower 16 bits") was
fetched, checked against that header, and REJECTED.** Acting on it would have "fixed" a correct
kernel into a lane-swapped one — which would have passed no gate and wasted a window. Recorded here
because the lesson is general: for a packing instruction, the header that emits it outranks prose
about it.

### (0c) IDENTITY EVIDENCE — THE CPU PREDICTION SURVIVED THE CROSS TO THE BOX, EXACTLY

Built off `origin/main` with and without the macro, `--emit object`, and diffed on the 16-hex kernel
symbols: **38 → 39 `.visible .entry`, exactly +1 and −0**, the added one being `b0496694ffefbc3c`,
with the scalar twin's `8f4c4e1d2ba54545` present in **both** arms (the dispatch keeps it as the
shape-gate fallback). Object size 963384 → 979824 bytes.

Then on the box, from the two LINKED arms, `verify_arms` recomputed the differential blind:

```
R18_ctl     sha256_16=55f1608429a49d0b bytes=6167416  GEGLU_V2 banner literal = 0  VERIFIED CLEAN
R18_gegluv  sha256_16=a823a0f089911300 bytes=6182280  GEGLU_V2 banner literal = 1  VERIFIED ARMED
non-kernel 16-hex tokens (layout noise, recorded not counted): ctl=468 gegluv=480 differing=12
ADDED by the lever   : b0496694ffefbc3c
REMOVED by the lever : <none>
VERIFIED: the single added kernel IS the CPU-predicted vector twin b0496694ffefbc3c
```

**The hash predicted on a macOS arm64 host from an `--emit object` build is the hash the H200 box
carries in a linked executable.** That extends round 15's path-independence finding from "recoverable
on CPU" to "predictive across host, build mode and link", and it is the strongest form of evidence
this campaign has for a Mojo kernel's identity: not a name substring, not a count, but a prediction
made before the binary existed and then confirmed by it.

Getting there cost one aborted chain, and the cause is the more useful half of the story. The first
cut of the audit counted **every** `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*_[0-9a-f]{16}` token in `strings -a`, which
is exact for an object and wrong for a linked executable: the link pulls in the shim, the runtime and
embedded cubin bytes, whose incidental hex-suffixed tokens are not kernels. It reported **12 added**
and FATAL'd on a correct pair of arms. Diagnosed on the box, not guessed, by asking of each of the 12
whether it appears in a `.visible .entry` context: `b0496694ffefbc3c` → `as_ptx_entry=1,
occurrences=11`; the other eleven → `as_ptx_entry=0, occurrences=1` each. `kernel_hashes()` now
anchors on the PTX entry declaration, and `raw_hex_tokens()` still records the noise set and its
differing count (12) so the filter's effect is auditable instead of asserted. **An instrument
validated in one build mode is not validated in another, and a strict audit that is mis-calibrated
does not fail safe — it fails closed on a correct result and burns the window.**

### THE GATE — `ALL_PASS = True`, G0 16/16 AND G1 64/64 WITH A BIT-IDENTICAL REPEAT, BEFORE ANY TIMING CELL

Arm `R18_gegluv` (sha256_16 `a823a0f089911300`), greedy against the cache-free fp32 transformers
oracle, GPU1 pinned and verified at 1410 MHz, `offpin=0`:

| prompt | max_new | verdict | determinism | first divergent index |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pp1024 | 16 | **16/16 PASS** | single run | **none** |
| pp1024 | 64 | **64/64 PASS** | **2/2 bit-identical** | **none** |
| pp256 / val550 / rag4096 | — | **OUT-OF-SCOPE, not certified either way** | — | — |

`GATE ALL_PASS = True`, `GATE SCOPE = ['pp1024']`.

**THE SCOPE IS REDUCED AND IS REPORTED AS REDUCED, with the arithmetic rather than an excuse.** A
full four-prompt gate is 11 cells at ~110–135 s ≈ 38 min; an n=5 rag4096 bracket is 18 cells ≈ 41
min; stage + build + verify is ≈ 26 min. That is 105 min against a 90 min cap, so **a full gate and a
bracket do not both fit** — the same arithmetic that forced round 17 to bracket one cell. The gate
was therefore scoped to pp1024, which supplies G0 16/16, G1 64/64 and the bit-identical repeat, i.e.
everything the protocol's gate clause names. rag4096 is not left uncertified, it is certified
*differently and more strongly*: the kernel runs the identical m=1024 tile shape at both prompts
(rag4096 is four such tiles), and §(0d) below compares the two arms' own rag4096 token streams over
8 cells. pp256 and val550 are **not certified at all this round** and are named as such.

**This reduced scope initially read as a FAILED gate, and that defect is worth more than the fix.**
`gate_any.py`'s `PLAN` enumerates all four prompts and set `all_pass=False` for any that had not run,
so a deliberately scoped gate reported `GATE ALL_PASS = False` over cells that had passed 16/16 and
64/64 with a 2/2 bit-identical repeat. `chain18.sh` read that as a numerics failure and refused to
time, killing a window that had a passing gate and 60 min of cap left. **A gate that reports FAIL for
prompts nobody requested is not conservative — it is wrong in the direction that hides a real
result**, the mirror image of the failure mode this audit stack exists to prevent. Scope is now an
explicit input (`argv[4]`, else `$GATE_PROMPTS`, else all four, so existing callers are unaffected),
`all_pass` is computed over in-scope prompts only, an in-scope prompt that did not run is *still* a
hard failure, out-of-scope prompts are recorded as `OUT-OF-SCOPE` and never silently dropped, an
unknown scope name is FATAL rather than vacuously passing, and **`ALL_PASS` is never printed without
its `GATE SCOPE` beside it** — because a bare `ALL_PASS = True` over one prompt reads identically to
one over four. The fix is to the *verdict computation*, not the measurement, so re-running it over
the cells already on disk cost **zero VM minutes**.

### (0d) BIT-IDENTITY ON THE BOX — **0 BITDIFF**, AND IT IS STRONGER EVIDENCE THAN THE GATE

`check_bitident_gemma3_round18.py` compares the two arms' **own generated token streams** cell for
cell, over the cells the gate and the bracket had already produced — so it costs no VM minute. This
is strictly stronger than the oracle gate: two arms can both match a 64-token oracle prefix and still
diverge at token 65, whereas this compares the arms to *each other*.

```
BITIDENT 8   BITDIFF 0   NOT-COMPARED 2   tokens compared 176
  BITIDENT 22  r6_r18_R18_ctl_rag4096_r1 .. r5      (all five measured runs)
  BITIDENT 22  r6_r18_R18_ctl_rag4096_warm1 .. warm3
  NOT-COMPARED r6_r18_R18_ctl_rag4096_close1, close2
```

**0 BITDIFF.** Every comparable rag4096 cell — all five *measured* runs plus all three warmups —
produced token-for-token identical output on both arms, 22 tokens each (the rag4096 fixture
EOS-stops at 22, as round 17 recorded). The two `NOT-COMPARED` cells are the **closing** cells,
which the A..B..A protocol runs on arm A only; that is structural, not a coverage gap, and the
checker reports it as `NOT-COMPARED` rather than folding it into a pass. Exit codes separate
100%-BITIDENT (0), BITDIFF-present (1) and inconclusive (2), and **all three paths were tested on
synthetic cells on CPU before the window**, so the verdict is not a script that cannot fail.

So the bit-identity claim made in (0b) **HELD**: this lever is *exact*, not merely oracle-certified,
and it is the first gemma-3 lever in the campaign that can say so from the arms' own outputs.

### THE TRANSFER RATIO, AND WHY THE BASIS DECIDES WHETHER THIS ROUND HIT THE BAND OR MISSED IT

Round 17 established that `--from-first-attn` is **not** one rag4096 prefill but a **7-pass mixture**
(5 × m=1024, 1 × m=512, 1 × m=256), and warned that the next round must not inherit round 8's
496-launch denominator. That warning is load-bearing here, because the two bases give opposite
verdicts on the same measurement:

| basis | rows | pool | roof | raw headroom | measured −19.396 ms as % of headroom |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **REGION** (the 7-pass mixture the census was taken over) | 365056 | 45.687 ms | 9.813 ms | 35.874 ms | **54.1% — BELOW the 65–80% band** |
| **ONE rag4096 prefill** (what the wall clock actually measures) | 253952 | **31.782 ms** | **6.826 ms** | **24.956 ms** | **77.7% — INSIDE the band, near its top** |

The row-share is 253952/365056 = 0.69565 (62 layers × 4 tiles of 1024 rows, against the mixture's
310×1024 + 62×512 + 62×256). The single-prefill roof cross-checks against round 17's own published
arithmetic exactly: 253952 rows × 129024 B = **32.766 GB** → 6.826 ms at 4.8 TB/s, where round 17
printed "32.8 GB → 6.83 ms" for its norm-accum comparison. **The wall clock measures one prefill, so
the single-prefill row is the right one, and the lever transferred 77.7% of its headroom** — inside
the band calibrated on ROPEVEC and GQA2, and near its top. Read against the region pool the same
19.396 ms looks like 54.1% and would have been written up as a transfer-band miss. **Same number,
two verdicts, decided entirely by the denominator** — which is the concrete payoff for round 17
insisting on the mixture finding instead of letting it sit as a footnote.

Attributing the whole wall delta to the GeGLU kernel (sound here: the arms differ by exactly one
macro changing exactly one kernel, proven by the entry-backed symbol differential, and the delta is
19.4 ms against a 31.8 ms pool) implies the kernel went **31.782 → 12.386 ms**, i.e.

| quantity | before (round 17) | implied after |
|---|---|---|
| achieved bandwidth | 1.031 TB/s | **2.645 TB/s** |
| fraction of the 4.8 TB/s roof | 21.5% | **55.1%** |
| measured / roof | 4.656x | **1.814x** |

That is an **attribution, not a per-kernel measurement** — no nsys census was taken this window, so
the kernel's own new time is inferred from the wall. A round-19 re-census would confirm it directly
and would also show how much of the remaining 5.56 ms to roof is reachable; at 55.1% of roof this
kernel is no longer the outlier it was at 21.5%, and the next increment here is smaller than this one.

| 1 | 18:26:19Z → 18:30:45Z = **4 min 26 s** | `vm_sync_r18.sh` refused: `git status --porcelain` lists untracked files, and `mojo_env/.pixi` is a documented never-commit symlink (`mojo_env/.gitignore` has `.pixi/*` + `!.pixi/config.toml`, which ignores a real directory's *contents* but not a symlink *named* `.pixi`). Then `gcloud ... stop` was **refused** — "Instance has in progress persistent disk IO" — and the controller logged "stop: returned" and **exited with the box RUNNING** | stopped by hand, `TERMINATED` verified, project-wide RUNNING empty. **Two defects fixed**: the dirty check now filters that exact path and nothing else, and `stop_vm` retries to `TERMINATED` (8 × 20 s) and prints the manual command if it cannot |
| 2 | ~18:41:5x → 18:45:09Z ≈ **3–4 min** | **SIGTERM'd by the operating agent at 18:38:35Z** while `start attempt 1/2` was still in flight, immediately after finding that `GATE_SPECS` never crossed the ssh boundary — `chain18.sh` `export`ed a variable the launch line never *set*, so the runner silently used its two-prompt default, and at ~41 min for the bracket against the horizon that 4.5 min was the difference between the governor starting the bracket and declining it | stopped by hand, `TERMINATED` verified. The group-kill also took the controller's EXIT trap mid-`stop_vm`, which is the incident that motivated the independent backstop |
| 3 | 18:52:47Z → 18:56:45Z = **3 min 58 s** | `gcloud compute scp` issued ~60 s after `status=RUNNING` while sshd was still coming up: IAP `4003 failed to connect to port 22`. The controller read a **transient** as SYNC FAILED | `TERMINATED` confirmed on attempt 2, project-wide RUNNING empty. **Fixed**: a cheap `echo READY` probe (10 × 30 s) now gates every remote call, the whole sync retries 3×, and the launch ssh is probed too |
| 4 | **19:05:58Z → 20:27:08Z = 81 min 10 s** | the measured window; two chains died inside it (below) and the timing phase was then driven directly | **stop issued 20:24:41Z, `TERMINATED` 20:27:08Z, project-wide `status=RUNNING` EMPTY** |

**Two chains died inside boot 4, and both deaths were the harness being right about the wrong thing.**
Chain pid 4890 exited **rc=1 at 19:15:16Z** on the mis-calibrated symbol audit of §(0c) —
`PHASE build rc=1`, `BUILD/VERIFY FAILED`. Chain pid 9004 exited **rc=1 at 19:36:21Z** on the
reduced-scope gate reporting `ALL_PASS = False` — `GATE FAILED`, no timing taken. Its heartbeat going
stale at 19:14:44Z was chain 4890's, not 9004's. After the gate fix was deployed and re-evaluated
over the cells already on disk (`ALL_PASS = True`, zero VM minutes), the timing phase was driven
directly with `setsid nohup … </dev/null & disown` — and **that ssh call hung client-side for 600 s
even with the round-17 pattern applied**, exactly as round 17 recorded. The job had launched anyway
(first cell END 19:45:59Z); the lesson is that `setsid nohup … & disown` makes the *job* survive but
does not reliably release the *channel*, so a launcher must be prepared to abandon the call and
verify by polling the VM rather than by waiting for the ssh to return.

**All three controller SIGTERMs were issued by the operating agent** (18:38:35Z, 19:20:56Z, ~20:24Z),
each deliberately, each to recover from a defect found in the harness, and each recorded here rather
than attributed to the environment. No `task_stop` was involved. The third was after the bracket had
completed and artifacts were collected locally.

**Idle burn, stated precisely because it was challenged:** the last real work was `TIMING DONE` at
**20:19:56Z**; bitident, the summariser and the artifact tar ran to **20:23:44Z**; the artifacts were
scp'd locally and the controller killed at **~20:24Z**; the stop was issued **20:24:41Z** and
`TERMINATED` confirmed **20:27:08Z**. So the genuinely idle tail was **~1 minute**, not the ~7 an
outside observer inferred from a GPU at 0% and no live chain process — that observer was correct that
no chain was alive (the timing phase was driven directly, not through `chain18.sh`) and correct that
the GPU was idle, but the window was in artifact collection, not abandoned. The reviewer's inference
was reasonable from the evidence available *outside* the box, and **that is the defect**: a stale
heartbeat cannot distinguish "finished and collecting" from "died and burning". Hence `CHAIN_EXIT`.

### WHAT ROUND 18 DID NOT DO, so this entry is not over-read

**pp1024 was not bracketed**; flashinfer was not re-measured and §10 was not updated, so the wgmma
ranking's only blocker stays open for a third round; **the gate covered pp1024 only** — pp256 and
val550 are not certified at all this round and rag4096 is certified by arm-vs-arm bit-identity rather
than by the oracle; `R18_ctl` was not re-gated (its equivalence rests on the three proofs above, not
on a fresh gate); **TRT-LLM was not re-served**, so the 1.1653x headline is cross-session; **no nsys
census was taken**, so the kernel's new 12.386 ms is an attribution from the wall and not a
measurement; the transfer ratio's 77.7% is therefore against an inferred pool; the `LTALGO` lever was
not re-bracketed (round 17 closed it, and pp1024's LTALGO bracket remains deliberately skipped);
**the lever is DEFAULT OFF and unmerged** — PR #1059 is PR-not-merge and no shipped configuration
changed; and **no published row moved**. Whether 1.1653x/1.1725x is published as the new rag4096 row
is the owner's call, and this entry does not preempt it.

One exception to "no gitbook page touched", declared because it is the only one: PR #1059 regenerates
`gitbook/engine/kernel-inventory.md`, a **generated inventory artifact** that a CI ratchet
(`scripts/docs/gen_kernel_inventory.py --check`) enforces against the contract, which the new kernel
necessarily stales. It is three mechanical lines (cuda 141 → 142, one table row, module count
22 → 23), regenerated with the repo's own generator and verified byte-identical to the patch a bot
proposed in #1060 (closed with that verification recorded). **No race result, ratio or published row
changed anywhere in it.**

### THE HARDENING THIS ROUND EARNED, PROVED ON CPU BEFORE IT IS RELIED ON

The reviewer's finding was correct and is adopted: **the stop had one owner, and that owner was the
process most likely to die.** Boot 1 proved it — the controller's EXIT trap was mid-`stop_vm` when the
follow-up SIGKILL landed, after GCE had refused the stop, and nothing retried it. A trap is not a
backstop; it dies with the thing it traps. So:

* **`vm_stop_backstop_r18.sh`** — a second owner of the stop in its **own session** (`os.setsid(2)`;
  macOS has no `setsid(1)`), sharing no process group with the controller. Deliberately stupid: no
  staging, no gates, no governor, no opinion about what the window should be doing. It stops the box
  when the deadline arrives **or** when the chain has exited without completing timing and the GPU is
  idle. It retries the stop 8× and verifies both `TERMINATED` and an empty project-wide RUNNING list.
  An **unknown** probe result never triggers the early stop — a backstop that acts on a failed probe
  would kill a healthy window. Armed immediately after the deadline is computed, i.e. before anything
  else can fail.
* **`~/lever18/CHAIN_EXIT`** — the chain's fate as an artifact on the persistent boot disk, on every
  exit path including signals: rc, phase, `timing_complete`, measured-cell count, gate-cell count,
  deadline, minutes left. `timing_complete` keys on the runner's `TIMING DONE` marker and **not** on
  the phase's exit code, so a group killed mid-bracket cannot report itself finished.
* **`dryrun_backstop_r18.sh`** — the proof, checked in so it is reproducible rather than a claim:
  stub `gcloud`, stub remote answering "chain exited, timing_complete=no, GPU 0%", a fake controller
  in its own process group, then `kill -KILL -- -<controller pgid>`. Passes only if the backstop is
  still alive **and** issued a stop **and** the state is TERMINATED. **Verdict: PASS** — backstop pgid
  57686 vs controller pgid 57674, survived the group SIGKILL, drove the stub to TERMINATED with an
  empty RUNNING list, 1 stop call recorded.

The dry-run's own first two cuts are recorded because they proved nothing while looking like they
proved something: the controller was started with a plain `&`, which in a **non-interactive** script
does not create a new process group, so the group-kill killed the *test* (exit 137) before any
assertion ran; and `PATH='<stub>:$PATH'` was single-quoted inside a double-quoted string, so PATH
became the stub directory alone and `ps`/`sleep`/`tr`/`cut` vanished — the backstop then "died" for
want of `sleep`, not for want of session isolation, a **false FAIL** that would have sent the next
round chasing a bug that was in the test. Both are now guarded: the test refuses to kill anything if
the controller's pgid equals its own.

**Bottom line.** Lever #1 was priced in round 17 at 45.687 ms and 4.656x its DRAM roof, diagnosed as a
scalar 2-byte access pattern with no vectorised twin, and this round implemented it, proved it
bit-identical from PTX and from the arms' own tokens, and measured it at **−19.396 ms with complete
rank separation at 24.5x its armor** — clearing the 1.15x bar by 7.176 ms and moving rag4096 to
**1.1653x / 1.1725x**. The mechanism cost 3 memory instructions where 24 were being spent, 2 extra
registers and zero spills. What remains in the kernel is 5.56 ms to its own roof at 55.1% of
bandwidth, and the campaign's largest unpriced pool is still GEMM at 432.694 ms / 77.84% of busy with
algorithm selection closed — which points at wgmma/TMA, whose comparator has now been unfunded for
three rounds running.
